_note: Single source of truth for the names we have given addresses in Lords2.exe.
GOG Windows build, 21 Jul 2009, 1,031,680 bytes, ImageBase 0x400000, no ASLR.
Adding a name is a one-line edit here. Then:
node tools/symbols/symbols_md.js            regenerate the tables in docs/symbols.md
node tools/symbols/symbols_md.js --check    fail if docs/symbols.md is out of date
analyzeHeadless ... -postScript ApplySymbols.java   push the names into Ghidra
confidence: 'verified' = read out of the binary or an exact invariant in the data.
'inferred'  = consistent with everything measured, not proven.
'signature' is optional; when present it is applied to the function in Ghidra and
its parameter names are what docs/symbols.md shows beside the name.
'comment' becomes the Ghidra plate comment (functions) or EOL comment (globals).

sections.title: Diplomacy, messages and the AI lords
Platform: window, DirectDraw, video and the log

functions.name: Eng_CopyString
functions.signature: void Eng_CopyString(int dest, int group, int index, int len)
functions.comment: Copies len bytes of L2.eng string (group, index) into a caller buffer, walking the group exactly as Eng_DrawString does. The fifth and last function that takes a literal (group, index) pair - the others are Eng_DrawString, Eng_Seek, Ui_DrawCentred and FUN_0040328E - and therefore the fifth place a call site names its own subject. Note the pair is at arguments 2 and 3 here, not 1 and 2.

functions.name: Eng_GroupBase
functions.comment: Returns the byte offset of an L2.eng group, read as the low 24 bits of the u32 at file offset 8 + group*4. See docs/formats/eng.md.

functions.name: Eng_Seek
functions.comment: Walks L2.eng to the (group, index) string and leaves the pointer in g_engCursor, exactly as docs/formats/eng.md 1.3 describes. New-game setup calls Eng_Seek(7, realm[+0x07]) and copies 16 bytes into g_playerNames - the game naming its own lords out of group 7, which is what fixes 1 = The Knight, 2 = The Baron, 3 = The Countess, 4 = The Bishop.

functions.name: Ui_NumberToBuffer
functions.signature: void Ui_NumberToBuffer(int value, int start, int forceSign)
functions.comment: Formats value into g_numberBuffer starting at index start, writing '-' or '+' at start and shifting when it does. Callers pass start = 1 so index 0 stays free for a sign character.

functions.name: Ui_DrawText
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawText(byte * str, int x, int y, void * font, int colour)
functions.comment: Draws a plain string, each glyph three times - at y-1 and y+1 in two shadow colours, then at y in the real one. Advances g_penAdvance, plus four pixels of trailing space.

functions.name: Glyph_Draw
functions.comment: Text blitter. Shifts the destination down by frame-record byte 0x0D before clipping, reserving rows above the rectangle. The only consumer of that byte.

functions.name: Ui_DrawCentred
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawCentred(int group, int index, int x, int y, int width, void * font, int colour)
functions.comment: One L2.eng string, centred inside width.

functions.name: Eng_DrawString
functions.signature: void Eng_DrawString(int group, int index, int x, int y, undefined * font, undefined4 colour)
functions.comment: Draws string `index` of L2.eng group `group`: Eng_GroupBase(group), then skip `index` NUL-terminated strings, then skip any bytes below 0x20. The (group, index) pairs in the callers are the best evidence available for what a subsystem is.

functions.name: Ui_DrawDelta
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawDelta(int value, int mode, byte * prefix, char * suffix, int x, int y, void * font, int colourPos, int colourNeg)
functions.comment: A signed number with a prefix and a suffix - and nothing at all when the value is zero and mode is 0, which is why the happiness and population panels have blank rows in a quiet season.

functions.name: Ui_DrawNumber
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawNumber(int value, char lead, char * suffix, int x, int y, void * font, int colour)
functions.comment: A number with a leading character and a suffix. lead overwrites buffer index 0, which Ui_NumberToBuffer leaves free for a sign; '@' is the blank glyph that keeps a zero aligned with its neighbours.

functions.name: Ui_DrawNumberRight
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawNumberRight(int value, char lead, char * suffix, int x, int y, int width, void * font, int colour)
functions.comment: Ui_DrawNumber, right-aligned inside width.

functions.name: Ui_DrawInsetRect
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawInsetRect(int x, int y, int w, int h)
functions.comment: A recessed rectangle: colour 0x10 along the top and right edges, 0x1F along the bottom and left.

functions.name: Ui_DrawBevelRect
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawBevelRect(int x, int y, int w, int h)
functions.comment: Four clipped lines: top and right in palette index 0x1F, bottom and left in 0x10.

functions.name: Clip_Horizontal
functions.comment: Computes horizontal clipping and sets g_clipState, g_clipVisibleWidth, g_clipSrcSkip, g_clipDstAdvance.

functions.name: Clip_Vertical
functions.comment: Sets g_blitRowCount to height - rowsClippedAtTop, unconditionally. That is why the byte-0x0D load in Pl8_DrawFrame is dead.

functions.name: Rand_Advance
functions.comment: The pseudo-random generator the battle AI uses. Two 31-bit Fibonacci LFSRs (taps at bits 0 and 4) are each stepped 31 times, then masked into six output globals - &0x7FFF, &0x7F and &7 per generator. Distinct from FUN_00404B2C / DAT_005C9A84, the counter the battlefield builders use.

functions.name: Pct
functions.comment: x * p / 100. The whole economy is written in this.

functions.name: PctOf
functions.comment: a * 100 / b, 0 when b is 0.

functions.name: DivCeil
functions.comment: (a + b - 1) / b, 0 when b is 0.

functions.name: Table_Lookup
functions.signature: int Table_Lookup(int x, int * pairs, int count, int dflt)
functions.comment: Generic (threshold, value) ladder: returns the value of the first pair whose threshold exceeds x, else the default. Used for the battlefield size class and the men-per-figure scale.

functions.name: Dist_Manhattan
functions.signature: int Dist_Manhattan(int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: Returns |dx| + |dy| and leaves the two absolute deltas in g_absDx and g_absDy.

functions.name: Dist_Chebyshev
functions.signature: int Dist_Chebyshev(int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: Returns max(|dx|, |dy|) and leaves the two absolute deltas in g_absDx and g_absDy.

functions.name: Dist_MinAxis
functions.signature: int Dist_MinAxis(int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: Returns min(|dx|, |dy|) and leaves the two absolute deltas in g_absDx and g_absDy. The third member of the Dist_Manhattan / Dist_Chebyshev family; used by Siege_FindCellSurface4.

functions.name: Map_DrawFrame
functions.comment: One campaign map frame. Zeroes g_countyTileTally, gives the current selection a 30-tile head start, runs Map_RenderIso (which tallies +1 per tile drawn and +5 for a castle tile), then the flag and army passes, and finally - only at zoom 0 - moves g_selectedCounty to whichever county filled most of the viewport. Scrolling therefore changes which county the right panel describes.

functions.name: Map_RenderIso
functions.comment: Walks the 65x129 lattice. Cells below 0x0FFF0000 hold a runtime offset into the tile array; cells still holding 0x0FFF0000 + b are off-map surround, where b is the background tile graphic index from the file.

functions.name: Map_RenderAlignedRow
functions.comment: One aligned lattice row: cols tiles at x = g_mapViewX + c*pitch, clip mode 0, tallying each into g_countyTileTally.

functions.name: Map_RenderOffsetRow
functions.comment: One half-offset lattice row: the first tile with clip mode 3 (right half, origin x - halfPitch), then cols-1 tiles a half pitch to the right, then one with mode 4 (left half). Consumes cols+1 lattice columns.

functions.name: Map_DrawTile
functions.signature: uint Map_DrawTile(undefined4 x, undefined4 y, int tileOffset)
functions.comment: Draws one map tile. bank = tile[+2] & 0x1c selects one of five sprite tables; tile[+3] is the frame index within it; tile[+1] is the flags and tile[+7] the county.

functions.name: Map_DrawTileApex
functions.signature: undefined8 Map_DrawTileApex(undefined4 a, undefined4 b, int mode)
functions.comment: Draws the chevron ("overhang") records that sit above a diamond tile. Reaches them by adding a fixed body size to the frame data pointer: 900 at zoom 0, 0xC4 at zoom 1, 0x24 at zoom 2, which are h*h/2 for h = 30, 14 and 6 and so pin the three tile sizes from the instruction stream alone.

functions.name: Sprite_TopIt
functions.signature: int Sprite_TopIt(int a, int b, int c)
functions.comment: THE GAME'S OWN NAME FOR THIS ROUTINE: its three failure messages read "ERR:top_it no data " and "ERR:top_it bad data ", written by Log_Write from a literal address (0x004D1C6C-ish) at 0x004071A0. The whole 0x00409934-0x0040A9B0 blitter family names itself the same way and five of those names confirm symbols we had already guessed - see docs/decisions.md CNEW-selfname. Draws the part of a tall map sprite that overhangs the tile above it; it marks the tiles it touches through the dirty helpers at 0x00452436/0x00452489/0x004524DC.

functions.name: Map_DrawPathMarker
functions.comment: The gold path-preview ball, NOT the county flag. Draws Flags1a.pl8 frame 0x38 + cost on every runtime tile carrying **bank** bit 0x40 - the transient mark Path_MarkPreviewTiles (0x004A91BA) sets along the local player's ordered path and FUN_0046C6BA clears grid-wide - at offset (+0x14, +6) from the tile, clipped by Clip_Horizontal(g_mapViewX, 0x1DE) and Clip_Vertical(0x18, 0x1DA), so the map viewport is x < 478 and y in 24..473. The cost comes from g_moveDistLocal minus one, clamped to 0 when the step is out of the unit's remaining allowance, and a castle, settlement or plot draws frame 0x4E instead. CORRECTED: this entry said "county flag over a castle tile" and was marked verified; four documents carried the same error. The county and castle flags are FUN_004071A0, off plane-0 bank bit 0x80, frame (shield - 1) * 8 + phase. The two bits are both called 0x40 and 0x80 in different planes, which is how the readings were crossed. docs/decisions.md C49, and docs/armies.md 2.3 has used this name all along.

functions.name: Map_DrawArmies
functions.comment: Walks the unit list hanging off a tile and draws each from g_spriteSheetA or g_spriteSheetB, offset by an 8-orientation by 16-frame table per zoom at 0x004D8108/0x004D8188 (zoom 0), 0x004D8208/0x004D8288 (zoom 1) and 0x004D8308/0x004D8388 (zoom 2). The sprite direction is the unit facing minus g_mapRotation, mod 8.

functions.name: Ui_DrawBox
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawBox(int x, int y, int cols, int rows)
functions.comment: Ui_DrawBoxBorder(0, ...) plus Ui_DrawBoxInterior inset by one cell. Sizes are in 16-pixel cells: the strip under the far-zoom map is Ui_DrawBox(0, 412, 30, 4) = 480x64.

functions.name: Sprite_GenFrame
functions.signature: void Sprite_GenFrame(int a, int b, int c, int d)
functions.comment: The game calls this routine `gen_frame`: its two failure messages are "ERR:gen_frame bad data ". Sibling of Ui_DrawBoxBorder (`mos_frame`) - the `gen_` family takes a caller-supplied sheet where the `mos_` family uses the mosaic sheet.

functions.name: Sprite_GenBlank
functions.signature: void Sprite_GenBlank(int a, int b, int c, int d)
functions.comment: The game calls this routine `gen_blank` ("ERR:gen_blank bad data "). Sibling of Ui_DrawBoxInterior (`mos_blank`).

functions.name: Ui_DrawBoxBorder
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawBoxBorder(int style, int x, int y, int cols, int rows)
functions.comment: Draws a 16-pixel-cell border from Panels.pl8: frames 0/1/2/3 are the TL/TR/BR/BL corners, 4..15 the top edge, 16..27 the bottom, 28..39 the left and 40..51 the right, each cycled (n-1) mod 12. A style above 0 adds 0xCC to reach the second complete border set at 204..255; style 2 also replaces the two top corners with edge pieces and omits the top edge.

functions.name: Ui_DrawBoxInterior
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawBoxInterior(int x, int y, int cols, int rows)
functions.comment: Fills a 16-pixel-cell area with Panels.pl8 frames 52 + (c mod 12) + (r mod 12)*12 - a 144-frame texture that the file lays out as a 12x12 grid on the artists sheet.

functions.name: Ui_DrawTileStrip
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawTileStrip(int x, int y, int cols, int rows)
functions.comment: Tiles Panels.pl8 frames 196 + (c mod 8) - the eight 24x24 frames - at 24-pixel steps. The menu bar background.

functions.name: Blit_Raster
functions.signature: void Blit_Raster(int src, int x, int y, short w, short h)
functions.comment: Blits a bare w*h raster with no PL8 record through the standard clipper. Used for the 128x128 minimap picture.

functions.name: Sprite_GenSprite
functions.signature: void Sprite_GenSprite(int a, int b, int c)
functions.comment: The game calls this routine `gen_sprite` ("ERR:gen_sprite bad data ").

functions.name: Pl8_DrawFrame
functions.signature: undefined4 Pl8_DrawFrame(void * buf, int frame, int x, int y)
functions.comment: Reads the frame record at buf + frame*0x10 + 8, range-checks the data offset, calls the clipper, dispatches to a blitter. Independently confirms the 8-byte header / 16-byte record layout inferred from offset arithmetic. Also reads record bytes +12, +13 and +14.

functions.name: Pl8_DrawFrameClipped
functions.signature: void Pl8_DrawFrameClipped(int buf, int frame, int x, int y)
functions.comment: The game calls this routine `write_c_sprite` ("ERR:write_c_sprite no data " / "bad data ") - the clipped twin of Pl8_DrawFrame, whose own messages say `write_sprite`. The three-message shape (no data / bad data / bad data) is identical in both, which is what identifies them as a pair.

functions.name: Pl8_DrawFrameHere
functions.signature: void Pl8_DrawFrameHere(int sheet, int frame, int x, int y)
functions.comment: Pl8_DrawFrame without the inline range diagnostics: reads the 16-byte frame record, sets g_drawX/g_drawY and g_clipDstAdvance = 0x280 - width. That 0x280 is where the 640-byte screen stride is visible.

functions.name: Sprite_WGenSprite
functions.signature: void Sprite_WGenSprite(int a, int b, int c)
functions.comment: The game calls this routine `w_gen_sprite` ("ERR:w_gen_sprite bad data "). One of three `w_gen_*` variants at 0x0040A682, 0x0040A80E and 0x0040A9B0; what the `w_`, `_h_` and `_f_` stand for is NOT established here.

functions.name: Sprite_WGenHSprite
functions.signature: void Sprite_WGenHSprite(int a, int b, int c)
functions.comment: The game calls this routine `w_gen_h_sprite` ("ERR:w_gen_h_sprite bad data ").

functions.name: Sprite_WGenFSprite
functions.signature: void Sprite_WGenFSprite(int a, int b, int c)
functions.comment: The game calls this routine `w_gen_f_sprite` ("ERR:w_gen_f_sprite bad data ").

functions.name: Ui_DrawMenuTitles
functions.comment: Lays the menu-bar titles out left to right from a 16-byte-per-item table, writing each measured x back into the table so the drop-downs know where to open. The campaign table is g_menuBarItems, three items, L2.eng groups 1, 2 and 3.

functions.name: Menu_SaveBackdrop
functions.comment: Saves the 400 x 180 band at (0, 24) that an open drop-down will cover, into the scratch buffer, via FUN_004b3f0a with row stride 0xF0. 100 dwords a row is 400 bytes; 400 + 240 = 640, the screen stride.

functions.name: Menu_RestoreBackdrop
functions.comment: Screen 0x32 is "a drop-down is open", and its painter only puts back what Menu_SaveBackdrop took: the same 400 x 180 band at (0, 24), through the restore twin FUN_004b3ec0. The drop-down itself is drawn by the widget pass.

functions.name: Screen_ConfirmBox
functions.comment: The 0x1E painter: a 14 x 8 cell box at (g_confirmX - 16, g_confirmY - 16) with group 10 index g_confirmPrompt inside it. The two widgets - frames 29 and 31, a mailed hand thumb-up and thumb-down rather than a tick and a cross - are drawn by the widget pass at the same offset.

functions.name: Screen_SliderBox
functions.comment: The 0x21 painter: a 15 x 7 cell box at (x - 16, y - 16), group 12 index g_sliderPrompt as the caption and index 0, "Click Right to Exit", underneath, with the value in a 3 x 1 recess. g_sliderFormat 1 divides by ten, 3 appends a per cent sign.

functions.name: Widget_Draw
functions.signature: void Widget_Draw(int xOffset, int yOffset, short * table, int count)
functions.comment: Draws a table of 24-byte widget records. Frame is record +0x04, plus 1 while the press timer at +0x0D runs. The size at +0x06 selects the sheet: below 24 from g_miscCtySheet, otherwise from g_systemSheet.

functions.name: Ui_OkButton
functions.signature: void Ui_OkButton(int x, int y, int mode)
functions.comment: The 24x24 picture in a panel's bottom-right corner: g_systemSheet frame 0x33 for mode 0, 0x10 for mode 1 (the same picture with a raised bevel). NOT A TICK - decoded, both frames are a cursor arrow pointing into a small black hole: a close button whose artwork is the instruction it gives. Measured rather than described: of System.pl8's 84 frames these two are the 4th and 5th darkest, 15.3% and 11.5% near-black against a median frame's 1.2%, while the genuinely thin widgets sit at 0.2% and 0.0%. It is a target as well as an instruction, and the right button closes the panel too, so the game offers two ways out: it stashes x and y into DAT_0055CE78 / DAT_0057C8A0, which FUN_0040E7E4 hit-tests on a left release - and it stashes only the LAST call's position, so a screen drawing two of them makes only the second clickable. The name is ours and predates the frame being looked at; docs/screens-county.md 2.7.

functions.name: Widget_Test
functions.signature: int Widget_Test(int xOffset, int yOffset, short * table, int count)
functions.comment: Hit-tests the same table Widget_Draw draws, and runs the press timer and the auto-repeat counter. The hit box is a square of side record +0x06. Publishes record +0x10 and +0x14 into g_uiHotspotId and g_uiHotspotArg, then calls record +0x08.

functions.name: Menu_OpenDropdown
functions.comment: Opens a menu-bar drop-down. Menu_HitTitle picks the title under the pointer; on a hit this saves g_screenId into g_menuPrevScreen, sets g_screenId to 0x32, points g_menuOpenItem at the last record and calls Menu_SaveBackdrop. Both call sites pass (g_menuBarItems, 3).

functions.name: Menu_HitTitle
functions.comment: Hit-tests the menu-bar titles: record short 0 is x, short 1 the measured right edge Ui_DrawMenuTitles wrote back, short 2 is y, and the height is a fixed 12. Returns a 1-based index, 0 for a miss.

functions.name: Hotspot_Test
functions.signature: int Hotspot_Test(int xOffset, int yOffset, short * table, int count)
functions.comment: The invisible variant: the same 24-byte record read as {x0, y0, x1, y1, callback, ...} with nothing drawn. The map sidebar's buttons are these.

functions.name: Ui_OpenConfirm
functions.signature: void Ui_OpenConfirm(int prompt, int x, int y, void * onAnswer)
functions.comment: Opens screen 0x1E, the yes/no box: saves g_screenId, stores the prompt index into g_confirmPrompt, the origin into g_confirmX / g_confirmY and the callback into g_confirmCallback, then paints. The prompt is an index into L2.eng group 10 - 0 "Exit the game?", 1 "Start a new game?", 9 "Autocalc battle?", 11 "Surrender castle?". The campaign map fills in the rest of that group, and it is a directory of the game's confirmable actions: 4 "Slaughter villagers?", 5 "Combine armies?", 6 "Disband army?", 7 "Garrison castle?", 8 "Besiege castle?", 10 "Destroy field?", 12 "Retreat from field?", 13 "Lift the siege?", 14 "Quit? (no destination).". Thirteen literal call sites cover indices 0, 1 and 4..14, so a callback passed to index 7 IS the garrison callback, by the text the player reads - which is what named six move-order globals at once. See docs/armies.md section 8.5.

functions.name: Ui_OpenSlider
functions.signature: void Ui_OpenSlider(int prompt, int * value, int step, int max, int min, int x, int y, int format)
functions.comment: Opens screen 0x21, the value spinner: the prompt indexes L2.eng group 12 ("Adjusting game speed", "Adjusting scroll speed", "Adjusting music level", ...), and value / step / max / min are stored for the two arrow widgets.

functions.name: Ui_OkButtonClicked
functions.comment: Hit-tests the corner picture Ui_OkButton last drew: returns 0 unless the LEFT button was released this frame (DAT_004E65D8) inside a 24x24 box at (DAT_0055CE78, DAT_0057C8A0), and on a hit calls FUN_004B18E3 to consume the click. Ui_OkButton is the only writer of those two globals and stashes only its LAST call's position, so on a screen that draws two corner pictures only the second is clickable - which is safe only because the draw pass runs before this one in the frame. Screen_FrameInput calls it 26 times. The message scroll has its own, larger hotspot: FUN_0047685D tests a 48x48 box round a copy of the same coordinates.

functions.name: App_IdleFrame
functions.comment: One turn of the idle work App_WinMain does when no window message is waiting. Asks IDirectDrawSurface::IsLost (vtable +0x60) of both surfaces and compares against DDERR_SURFACELOST (0x887601C2, which the decompiler prints as -0x7789fe3e); if either is lost it calls Display_RestoreSurfaces and, on failure, App_OnPaused and returns 0. Otherwise it steps the season/turn drivers and calls App_Draw (0x0040E890). Returns 0 when a quit has been requested (g_quitRequest == 1).

functions.name: App_WinMain
functions.comment: [V] WinMain. The PE entry point is 0x004C3370 (SizeOfImage header, EntryPoint RVA 0xC3370) and 0x004C3370 is the ONLY caller of this function; it takes an HINSTANCE and returns msg.wParam, which is WinMain's exact shape. Reads L2.eng into g_engText (120,000 bytes), calls App_InitWindow, Sound_Init, then loops on PeekMessageA/GetMessageA, calling Net_PumpReceive whenever the queue is empty and App_IdleFrame when the window is active. Its five log lines are the game's own account of its startup: "ERR:Exited, couldn't InitApp.", "OK :Game partialy setup.", "ERR:Exited, couldn't InitGame.", "OK :Game fully setup.", "ERR:Exited, couldn't LoadGame.".

functions.name: App_PumpOnce
functions.comment: One iteration of App_WinMain's message pump, lifted out so a modal wait can keep the window alive: PeekMessageA, else Net_PumpReceive; GetMessageA/TranslateMessage/DispatchMessageA; returns 0 on WM_QUIT. Called from the multiplayer preload wait at 0x004ADCF6.

functions.name: Ini_ReadConfig
functions.comment: Hardware and CD detection, and it runs AFTER Options_Load, overwriting eight g_options fields the file has just supplied. Parses l2.ini for WindowsDir=, then <dir>\sierra.ini (falling back to sierra.ini) for CDRomDrives=, CDROM=, SoundChannels=, PhysicalMem=, VideoSpeed= and CPU=. Key strings at 0x004D2838ff are [V]; the field mapping is [D]. NOT a preferences path: nothing here is player-facing, and the shipped GOG L2.INI has no CDRomDrives= key at all, so the drive letter always falls through to the 'D' default.

functions.name: Screen_Draw
functions.comment: The interface's master switch: 39 cases on g_screenId, each calling one screen's painter. With Screen_DrawWidgets and Screen_HandleInput these are the only three places the screen id is dispatched. docs/screens-county.md section 1.

functions.name: Screen_DrawCampaign
functions.comment: Draws the whole campaign screen: Misc_cty frames 54, 57 and 59 at x 478 (y 24, 430, 460), the map through Map_DrawFrame, the menu bar, the county panel, the minimap at (480, 25), and finally Palette_Set(g_paletteBase01).

functions.name: CountyStrip_Draw
functions.comment: The selected county's strip in the map sidebar: name, population, happiness, tax rate, ration achieved and the health thermometer for an owned county; frame 0x3A and the owner's name for one you do not hold. docs/screens-county.md section 2.

functions.name: CountyStrip_DrawCastleIcon
functions.comment: One county's castle cell on the county strip, not a castle screen. Picks a g_miscCtySheet frame from whether the castle is complete, and when county +0x1D0 or +0x1D4 (stone/wood still needed) is non-zero draws a materials icon plus L2.eng group 71 string 0x12 'Needed'. DAT_0056D68C is the strip row counter it advances on the way out.

functions.name: Minimap_Draw
functions.comment: Called as Minimap_Draw(0x1E0, 0x19). Blits the 128x128 g_minimapPixels raster at (x-2, y+3) = (478, 28), tints it through Minimap_DrawOverlay, draws a 29x123 Misc_cty strip at (x+0x83, y+7) and a mode badge at (x+5, y+5). The picture is drawn at (478,28) while Minimap_Click hit-tests (480,25): that 2/3 pixel disagreement is the original.

functions.name: Minimap_DrawOverlay
functions.signature: void Minimap_DrawOverlay(uint selected, int x, int y, int mode)
functions.comment: Recolours the minimap raster per county. Source pixels 10..13 are land inside a county and are replaced from an 8-byte-per-realm ramp at g_minimapRealmRamp indexed realmColour*8 + (v-10); shade 10 of the selected county becomes index 0x20. Modes 1..3 instead colour the county from the 6-entry g_minimapRatingRamp, and ALL THREE rating branches skip the pixel unless owner == g_localPlayer - the statistic modes show your own counties and nobody else's. Everything else is left as the picture drew it. CORRECTED: the rating index is county +0x03, +0x02 and +0x01, not +0xB3/+0xB2/+0xB1 - the old numbers were 0x0053F9B3 read as an offset rather than as an address into g_counties (0x0053F9B0). Minimap_ComputeBands (0x00451BBA) fills those three bytes and this function calls it first on every draw. docs/decisions.md C59.

functions.name: Panel_Population
functions.comment: Draws L2.eng group 73 next to county +0x28 (last season), +0x30 (births), +0x34 (deaths), +0x38 (army), +0x3C/+0x58 (emigrants to), +0x40 (immigrants) and +0x24 (this season).

functions.name: Panel_Tax
functions.comment: Draws L2.eng group 86: "Tax rate" = county +0xB9, "People pay" = +0xC0, "This county" = realm +0x28 + county +0x0F, "Other counties" = county +0x16.

functions.name: Panel_Happiness
functions.comment: Draws L2.eng group 85 ("Happiness in / Last season / From taxes / From ration / From health / From army / From ale / This Season / Average happiness / From events") next to county fields +0x0D, +0x12, +0x13, +0x14, +0x15, +0x194, +0x17, +0x0C and +0x18. This is what names those fields.

functions.name: Panel_Ration
functions.comment: The ration panel (screen 0x19). Draws L2.eng group 87 against county +0x15E (wanted), +0x15D (achieved, red when they differ), +0x09 (health band), +0x11 and +0x10 as happiness deltas, and the Fed / Eaten rows from +0x16C, +0x170, +0x174, +0x178 and +0x17C.

functions.name: Panel_RationSlider
functions.comment: The grain-to-livestock slider: caps from g_systemSheet frames 0x4A and 0x4B at x 200 and 324, a 100-pixel track from x 224 to 323, and the knob (frame 0x4C, 10 wide) at 220 + county +0x15F.

functions.name: Village_Draw
functions.comment: The village screen (screen 0x02): villani1/villani2/vill.pl8, villtops.pl8, and the weather and fertility lines when Advanced Farming is on. The scene starts at y = g_villageTopY.

functions.name: Village_Animate
functions.comment: Steps the village's animation counters and draws the animated overlays.

functions.name: Village_DrawPeasants
functions.comment: Draws the eight peasant clusters at g_jobClusterOrigins + (0x40, g_villageTopY).

functions.name: Village_DrawCluster
functions.signature: void Village_DrawCluster(int cluster, int x, int y)
functions.comment: One cluster: up to 25 icons from g_peasantIcons at the offsets in g_peasantIconOffsets, each frame bumped by one while the cluster is the drag source.

functions.name: Panel_JobDetail
functions.comment: The job popup (screen 0x0F) for g_jobPanelJob, 1..9 into L2.eng group 74. Draws the worker count with the group 8 noun for job*2 + 30, red when labour +0x00 is below +0x04 and a second colour when it is above +0x08 - which is what shows the labour record to be three integers a job, not one.

functions.name: Panel_JobIndustry
functions.comment: The mining, quarrying, wood and blacksmith bodies of the job popup. Maps jobs 5, 6, 7 and 8 to industry records 1, 3, 0 and 2, the same order the village artwork implies.

functions.name: Panel_JobBlacksmith
functions.comment: The blacksmith body of the job popup, with smithy.pl8 and hearth.pl8 and the weapon's cost from g_weaponCost.

functions.name: Panel_JobGrain
functions.comment: The grain body of the job popup: store, fertility band, the event and weather effects on the store, and either what will be sown in spring or what is growing and when it is harvested. Nothing on it is clickable - the player never chooses how much to sow.

functions.name: Panel_JobCattle
functions.comment: The cattle body of the job popup: L2.eng group 77 calf births, cow deaths and the herd-crowding bands.

functions.name: Panel_JobReclamation
functions.comment: The field-reclamation body of the job popup: how many fields are being reclaimed and how many seasons to the next one.

functions.name: Screen_SoundLevels_Dead
functions.comment: Draws a 19-cell box at (64, 112) and, for mode 0 or 1, the three sound-level numbers from g_options+0x3C/+0x40/+0x44 with '%', '%' and ' ' suffixes (chars at 0x004D3EE4/E8/EC). ITS ONLY CALLER PASSES 3, which draws the box and no numbers. Dead content: Ui_OpenSlider has exactly two call sites in the whole image (game speed and scroll speed), so L2.eng group 12 indices 3, 4 and 5 - 'Adjusting music level', 'Adjusting sound level', 'Number of samples' - are unreachable strings. The volume values are still defaulted and still written to lords2.inf on every exit. See also the orphaned widget table at 0x004DDE08. docs/bugs.md.

functions.name: Screen_SaveLoad
functions.comment: Screens 0x35 and 0x36, one painter with a mode flag: L2.eng group 40 index 0 "Loading a conquest." or 1 "Saving a conquest.".

functions.name: SaveLoad_DrawStatus
functions.comment: The progress and error line of the load/save screens 0x35 and 0x36 - not the file browser. Switches on g_screenId to choose L2.eng group 40 string 2 'Loading game. Please wait.' or 3 'Saving game. Please wait.', and prints 4 'File error. Operation canceled.' on failure.

functions.name: Screen_AdvancedOptions
functions.comment: Screen 0x39. A 24 x 13 cell box at (48, 96); L2.eng group 50 index 0 as the heading and 1..4 as four rows at y 160, 192, 224 and 256, each with a group 18 Yes/No beside it at x 320. Publishes 4 into g_advancedOptWidgetCount, which the widget pass reads. The four widgets in g_advancedOptWidgets sit at y 156, 188, 220, 252 - each label y minus 4.

functions.name: Screen_SoundOptions
functions.comment: Screen 0x42. Group 51: Music, Sound effects and Speech, each with a group 19 On/Off at x 320, and 3 into g_soundOptWidgetCount.

functions.name: Screen_DisplayOptions
functions.comment: Screen 0x43. Group 52: Animations (On/Off) and Full screen (Yes/No). Group 52 index 3, "(F5 key re-sizes window to 640x480)", is drawn only when g_optFullScreen is 0 - a hint about the window that appears exactly when there is a window.

functions.name: Screen_About
functions.comment: Screen 0x25. A 22 x 9 cell box at (96, 224) holding group 59 - "Lords 2.", the release version and the copyright line - and nothing else but the OK tick.

functions.name: Screen_HelpOptions
functions.comment: Screen 0x31. Group 45: Tip screens and Tool tips as Yes/No rows, and "Start game help" as a plain button whose handler calls WinHelpA on l2help.hlp.

functions.name: Ui_HistoryGraph
functions.signature: uint Ui_HistoryGraph(int x, int y, int mode)
functions.comment: The 402x155 history graph on the population and happiness panels. mode 0 reads g_countyHistory +0x00 (population, u32), mode 1 reads +0x04 (happiness, u8), walking g_historyLength turns from g_historyHead and wrapping at 400. Returns the peak, which the caller prints. Background from graphs.pl8.

functions.name: Screen_GreatestNoble
functions.comment: Screen 0x20, the standings. Loads grtnoble.256 / grtnoble.pl8 and flags.pl8 - the filename is the identification - and draws L2.eng group 35, the seven 'Most counties,' / 'Most castles,' / ... / 'Greatest noble,' categories, with string 7 'undecided.' where no realm leads. Walks the realms at stride 0x160 and labels each from g_playerNames.

functions.name: Screen_Merchant
functions.comment: Screen 0x08. Loads merchant.256 as its palette, then merchant.pl8 and mercgrid.pl8.

functions.name: Merchant_HoverPlaque
functions.comment: Screen 0x08's widget pass. Draws one price plaque for the good under the pointer, at that good's own position out of g_goodsStall, and erases the last one first - so at most one is ever on screen and two goods may claim the same 128x64 box (grain's and stone's do). The plaque is a 8x4-cell box, the group 6 name centred in it, and BOTH PRICES side by side at (x+0x24, y+0x22): the stall price, then stall + max(1, Pct(stall, merchant morale)), the same arithmetic as Trade_BeginGood written out a second time. It is throttled by a countdown at 0x0053EF54 that is set to 500 on entry and after every change, so the plaque does not chase a moving pointer.

functions.name: Screen_TradeGoods
functions.comment: Screen 0x0C. Re-uses merchant.pl8 as the backdrop and overlays icontrad.pl8.

functions.name: Trade_DrawPanel
functions.comment: The widget pass of screen 0x66, the merchant trade panel. Draws essentially all of L2.eng group 68 - 1 'We receive', 5 'Buying', 6 'Selling', 8 'Total cost of', 9 'Buying price', 0xA 'Selling price', 0xC 'You have.', 0xE 'Purchase?', 0xF 'Sale?', and the four wrapped advice paragraphs 0x10..0x13 - beside the goods names in group 6.

functions.name: Court_Draw
functions.comment: The court screen (0x09): L2.eng group 70 against the realm record - gold +0x118, iron +0x120, stone +0x128, wood +0x130, six weapon stocks from +0x140, army wages +0xFC and expected tax +0x15C.

functions.name: Diplo_DrawScreen
functions.comment: Screen 0x0B, 'the other lords'. Loads faces.pl8, draws one lord card per rival, and draws L2.eng group 72 as the action menu in one of four layouts held in g_diploMenuState: no ally (items 2-5), allied to this lord (2,3,4,6,7,8), allied elsewhere (2,3,4), or a message already pending from them (item 24 alone).

functions.name: Diplo_DrawLordCard
functions.comment: One rival's card: portrait from faces.pl8 frame lord*3-3 (frame 12 for a human), shield, name from g_playerNames, allied / at-war / mail icons, and a 10 x 63 standing thermometer whose three colours break at standing >= +11 and <= -11 - exactly the two thresholds Diplo_ReplyAllianceOffer decides on.

functions.name: Screen_DiploDialog
functions.comment: Screen 0x1A, which docs/screens-county.md could not identify: the seven diplomacy dialogs, selected by g_diploKind and all drawing L2.eng group 72. 0 is the gift of gold, 1..4 the four letters, 5 and 6 the two requests that need a county.

functions.name: Diplo_DrawGiftGold
functions.comment: g_diploKind 0. Group 72 index 10 "Send gift of gold to" and the target's name, index 23 "Last gift was" and the per-pair record at 0x0057BF8C, index 18 "Gift of" and g_diploGold, index 17 "Dispatch ?".

functions.name: Diplo_DrawLetter
functions.comment: g_diploKind 1..4, called with kind - 1. Draws group 72 index 11 + kind - "Give a compliment to", "Insult", "Ask for an alliance with", "End alliance with" - plus the target's name and the draft body.

functions.name: Diplo_DrawCountyRequest
functions.comment: g_diploKind 5 and 6. Group 72 index 15 + kind, "Plead for help from" / "Plan strategic attack with", a county map, and then either index 19 / 20 ("Choose the county you want help in / attacked") while g_pickedCounty is 0 or index 21 / 22 plus the county name from group 100.

functions.name: Screen_Armoury
functions.comment: The armoury, screen 0x0A - AND the first frame of the raise-army screen, 0x17, which draws its Ui_DrawBox on top of the room this paints and never clears. Loads armoury.256, armoury.pl8, arm_grid.pl8, one of the five arm_it_<colour>.pl8 (base1a.pl8 if that read fails) and armtorch.pl8; draws the wall items, the racks and L2.eng 69/6, 69/7 and 69/8 - 'Create', 'Change', 'Cancel' - centred at x 0x21E; ends with Palette_Set(armoury.256). [V] That one painter serves both screen ids is why the levy window is in the armoury's palette and not the campaign map's. docs/decisions.md C61.

functions.name: Screen_ArmouryRepaint
functions.comment: Screen_Armoury without the three big File_ReadChunk calls or the hit map - the cheap repaint that screen 0x0D returns to the armoury with. Same background, same racks, same three L2.eng group 69 labels. [V] Called from Screen_FrameInput's 0x0D arm on a right release or on the corner picture.

functions.name: Armoury_DrawRacks
functions.comment: Screen 0x0A: the eight troop portraits along the bottom of the armoury and the count under each, from g_armouryRacks (0x004D2CE8), 8 records of {frame, spriteX, spriteY, numberX, numberY}. Slot 0 is the unequipped peasants, 1..6 the weapon types, 7 the total. A rack is drawn for slot t when g_levyBasket[t].available > 0 OR when the county mercenary offer is of that troop type, in which case the band men are ADDED to the printed count. [V] The loop guard is `if (6 < i) return`, so slot 7's arm - including its `frame 13 + shieldIndex - 1` tint - is DEAD CODE and the total is never drawn. docs/armies.md 6.2; crates/l2-game/src/screens/armoury.rs.

functions.name: Armoury_DrawWallItems
functions.comment: Screen 0x0A: the six weapons hanging on the armoury walls, from g_armouryWallItems (0x004D2D88), 6 records of {frame, x, y} indexed by weapon slot. Each is drawn only when g_realms[player].weapons[t-1] > 0, so the picture is an inventory of what the realm owns - which is the 'listing of their tools' a player said was missing. [V] The six positions agree cell for cell with arm_grid.pl8's six hit regions, two tables that know nothing about each other; asserted in crates/l2-game/tests/armoury.rs.

functions.name: Armoury_LoadScreen
functions.comment: Screen 0x0D, one weapon's rack. Reads arm_cros|mace|swor|pike|bow|mail.pl8 by g_armourySelectedType (falling through to arm_cros.pl8), then Ui_DrawBox(0x60, 4, 0x1A, 7), Ui_OkButton(0x1E4, 0x58, 0), Ui_DrawInsetRect(0x65, 9, 0x66, 0x66) and frame 0 of the weapon's 24-frame 100x100 animation at (0x66, 10), then FUN_00418E2D for the count and the spare. [V]

functions.name: Screen_RaiseArmy
functions.comment: The raise-army screen: L2.eng group 69 over the levy slider, the six weapon stocks from realm +0x140, the happiness cost, and the mercenary offer for county +0x1AD - count and nationality from g_mercBands, the hire price, and men/2 as the seasonal wage.

functions.name: Armoury_RestoreWalkerStrip
functions.comment: Screen 0x0A and 0x0D, per frame: restores whichever of the four background strips Screen_Armoury saved (y 0xD8, height 0x9E; x 0, 0xA0, 0x140 at width 0x3C and x 0x1E0 at width 0x28) according to the walking soldier's own x, DAT_0056D630. [V] Was Armoury_DrawPanel in docs/hypotheses.json, which had the role right and the verb wrong: it erases, it does not draw. Promoted with Armoury_DrawWalker and Armoury_DrawTorches, which are the other two thirds of the 0x0A overlay pass.

functions.name: Armoury_DrawWalker
functions.comment: Screen 0x0A and 0x0D, per frame: advances the soldier who walks across the armoury after a rack is equipped - x += 4 from -0x50 along y = 0xD8, out of the trp_<weapon>_<colour>.pl8 buffer FUN_004AABD8 loaded, stopping the walk at x = 0x280. The frame cycles 0..7 until he reaches DAT_00568228, the per-type x from the table at 0x004DE6F0, and then runs a second cycle from frame 8. [V] Presentation only; nothing here reads or writes the levy basket.

functions.name: Armoury_DrawTorches
functions.comment: Screen 0x0A and 0x0D, per frame: two guttering torches from armtorch.pl8 at (0x9A, 0x76) and (0x19A, 0x76), the second thirteen frames behind the first. [V] Presentation only.

functions.name: Screen_ArmyDivision
functions.comment: Screen 0x11. L2.eng group 17, "Army Division.", and icon_tmp.pl8.

functions.name: Screen_SplitArmyRows
functions.comment: The eight rows of the army-division screen (L2.eng group 17): troop types 0..6 from the levy basket in two columns, then row 7 as the mercenary band, then the two Total men lines.

functions.name: Screen_CastleBuild
functions.comment: Screen 0x1B, the castle chooser. Loads cas_back.256 / cas_back.pl8, the chosen castle's picture out of caspics.pl8 by DAT_004D2DD0[type], and cas_bits.pl8 into DAT_005533C4, then sets the DAT_005440B8 dirty flag and calls Screen_CastleBuildPanel.

functions.name: Screen_CastleBuildPanel
functions.comment: The stats panel of screen 0x1B, redrawn only when DAT_005440B8 is set. Names the selected type from L2.eng group 71 index DAT_0056D898 + 1 (1 'Wooden palisade.' .. 5 'Royal castle.'), then prints g_castleMaterial's stone and wood **net of the castle already there** (it subtracts g_castleMaterial[existing type]), g_castleWorkforce with 8 'will take' / 9 'to build.', g_castleTaxBonus with 0x10, g_castleGarrisonCap with 0xB/0xC, and 0xF 'Start construction?'. The four named constant tables all appearing together is what confirms this, rather than the group label, against the three other group-71 callers that are not this screen.

functions.name: Screen_DrawMenuBar
functions.comment: The 640x24 bar at y 0: background tiled from Panels.pl8 frames 196+(c mod 8) at 24px steps (25 cells from x 0 plus 2 from x 592 = 640 exactly), a bevel outline, the File/Options/Help titles from L2.eng groups 1/2/3, one 13x16 Misc_cty banner per live realm at x 270+16i y 4, the year and season at x 360 and the local realm treasury at x 500.

functions.name: Screen_DrawEndTurn
functions.comment: Draws Misc_cty frame 59 (162x20) at (478, 460) and centres L2.eng group 4, "End turn", in it at (478, 462) in the 9-point font. That strip is the End Turn button.

functions.name: Ui_DrawYear
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawYear(int year, int x, int y, int style)
functions.comment: A year with BC or AD from L2.eng group 26. style 3 prints the number alone, which is what the graph axes use.

functions.name: Ui_DrawCount
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawCount(int value, int unitIndex, int x, int y, void * font, int colour)
functions.comment: A number followed by a noun from L2.eng group 8: index unitIndex when the value is 1 or -1, unitIndex + 1 otherwise. Group 8 is singular at even indices and plural at odd.

functions.name: Ui_DrawUnitNoun
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawUnitNoun(int value, int unitIndex, int x, int y, void * font, int colour)
functions.comment: Just the group 8 noun, singular when the value is 1.

functions.name: Ui_DrawHappinessDelta
functions.signature: void Ui_DrawHappinessDelta(int value, int x, int y, void * font, int colourPos, int colourNeg)
functions.comment: Draws a bracketed signed number with the happiness face after it: a bracket, Ui_DrawDelta, g_miscCtySheet frame 0x17, a closing bracket.

functions.name: Screen_SendSupplies
functions.comment: Screen 0x18. L2.eng group 33, "Send supplies", with county names from group 100.

functions.name: UnitPanel_Draw
functions.comment: Draws the info panel for the selected unit. Its Eng_DrawString (group, index) pairs name every unit type: L2.eng group 31 strings 0 'Merchant.', 5 'Revolting peasants.', 2 'Supplies for', 15/16 army; descriptions 12/13/14/15/16. For a merchant it also draws group 5 indexed by the route number - the merchant's name.

functions.name: TileInfo_Draw
functions.comment: The 'what is this tile' panel. Switches on the plane-0 flag byte in DAT_005440B0 (a copy of runtime tile +1) and picks a heading, a description paragraph and an icon frame out of L2.eng group 30: bit 0x01 -> 1 'Road.' + 0x17, 0x04 -> 3 'Sea.' + 0x18, 0x08 -> 4 'Mountain.'/5 'Woodland.', 0x10 -> 48 'Village'/50 'Ruined village.', 0x20 -> the farm-field table at 0x004D2EC8, 0x40 -> 7 'County town.' + 0x1B, 0x80 -> the resource sites (9 mine, 10 quarry, 11 lumber mill, 82 blacksmith) or the castle (8, or 14/15 for under construction/repair). Delegates to TileInfo_DrawGrain, TileInfo_DrawHerd and TileInfo_DrawCastle. Every heading pairs with the matching description, which is what fixes the bit meanings - see decisions.md C25 for the 0x40/0x80 correction this forced.

functions.name: TileInfo_DrawGrain
functions.comment: The grain half of TileInfo_Draw. Prints fertility from L2.eng group 22 indexed by (county +0x208 + 100) / 29 - seven strings for a -100..+100 range, which is exactly how many group 22 has - then sacks sown, the yield at g_grainYieldPerSack, and group 77's grain-store lines 0x18 'No outside factors affected stored grain.', 0x19 'eaten by rats.', 0x1A 'found as surplus.'. The advanced-farming lines are gated on g_optAdvancedFarming.

functions.name: TileInfo_DrawHerd
functions.comment: The herd half of TileInfo_Draw, and NOT a sowing forecast as first guessed. Draws only group 77's livestock lines: 5 'Calf births expected', 6 'Cow deaths expected', 7 'Change due to farming', 8..11 the four crowding levels, 0x10..0x12 the weather change, 0x13..0x17 disease/wolves/put down/over expectations, 0x1B 'Change due to eating' and 0x1C 'Overall change'. Group 77 mixes grain and herd text, so its index-0 label 'from' says nothing about which half a caller draws - only the indices do.

functions.name: TileInfo_DrawCastle
functions.comment: The castle block of TileInfo_Draw - the tile panel, not the build screen. Reads county +0x1C0 (castle type) into g_castleTaxBonus for group 71 string 0x10 'Boosts tax revenues by' and into g_castleGarrisonCap for 0xB 'Barracks for' + 0xC 'troops.'; that is the same cap FUN_004A79A3 tests a garrison against, which is what identifies the branch. With a garrison present it adds the unit's men (+0x168) and 0xD 'currently stationed here.', or 0x13 'Enemy troops are barracked here.', plus 0xE 'View these troops?' and a widget. Note the tables are one-based: DAT_004D8A0C is g_castleGarrisonCap - 4.

functions.name: Castle_DrawStatusBlock
functions.signature: void Castle_DrawStatusBlock(int county, int x, int y, int row)
functions.comment: The castle-under-construction block, drawn at a caller-chosen origin. L2.eng group 71: 0x10 tax bonus, 0xB/0xC barracks capacity, then county +0x1D0 with 6 'of stone needed,' and +0x1D4 with 7 'of wood needed.'; county +0x1A6 zero gives 0x11 'No castle building in progress.', otherwise county +0xE8 with 8 'will take'. Shared by TileInfo_DrawCastle and the county screen.

functions.name: Screen_DrawConquest
functions.comment: Screen 0x1C, the campaign interstitial: gateway.256, gateway.pl8 and a panels2.pl8 window 26 cells wide at x=0x70, 14 cells tall for the two short outcomes and 18 for the long one. [V] Draws L2.eng group 36 in three branches - won (0..3 around the map name), lost (4..8) and, when g_campaignMap has reached 8, the end of the campaign (0, 1 then 9..15). The country just fought over is group 101 indexed by g_campaignLastMap, and on a win the next one is group 101 indexed by the already-advanced g_scenarioIndex.

functions.name: Screen_LordsOfMagicAd
functions.comment: Screen 0x45. Loads lom.256 and lom.pl8 and installs the palette: the Lords of Magic advertisement the front end links to, and nothing else.

functions.name: ScenarioList_Draw
functions.comment: The five-row scenario list box, with the selected row inverted and a proportional scrollbar thumb whose three segments are computed from the scroll offset, 5, and the total. Row text is L2.eng group 101, the 60 map slot names, but indexed *through* the byte table DAT_0050A460 rather than directly, so the visible order is not the group's order. What builds that table has not been read.

functions.name: Screen_BattleMasterRatings
functions.comment: Screen 0x2E. score1.256 + score1.pl8, L2.eng group 37 "Battle Master ratings".

functions.name: Screen_BattleMasterRank
functions.comment: Screen 0x2F. score2.256 + score2.pl8, groups 37 and 38 - 38 index 0 is "Rank of Private", so this is the rank sheet rather than the ratings table.

functions.name: Screen_SiegePrep
functions.comment: The siege preparation screen (0x1D): L2.eng group 83, the seasons remaining from +0x19C, and a count plus a percent-complete bar for each of the three siege-engine records at +0x182, +0x188 and +0x18E.

functions.name: Screen_BattlePrompt
functions.comment: Screen 0x12: the 'a battle is to be fought' prompt. Draws L2.eng group 80 heading 0, or 7 'The Siege commences.' when g_battleIsSiege; then group 80 string 1 'Will you take the field?', 2 'Your opponent has the choice' or 3 'The opponents are deciding', selected by DAT_005533D0 (who owns the choice). County name from group 100 at g_scenarioIndex*20 + the battle county, the two lords' names from g_playerNames (group 99 string 0 '"The people."' for owner 6), and both army rosters via FUN_004224E7(g_battleArmyA, g_battleArmyB). Opened by FUN_004A7158 and its sibling, which play s080_01/02/03.wav on the same DAT_005533D0 - the WAV is named after the L2.eng group.

functions.name: Screen_BattleResult
functions.comment: Screen 0x13: the battle result report. Same layout as Screen_BattlePrompt with an OK button, L2.eng group 81 heading 0 'The Battle is decided.' or 8 'The siege is over.' under g_battleIsSiege, and the rosters redrawn in mode 1. Reached only after Battle_ReturnToCampaign has already been applied, so it reports rather than decides.

functions.name: Screen_BattleOutcome
functions.comment: Screen 0x2B. L2.eng group 82 as seven heading/body pairs at index 2n and 2n + 1, chosen by g_battleOutcome - won, lost, siege won, siege lost, siege lifted, castle lost, and the neutral pair 12/13 "The conflict is over." Draws a taller box with an inset animation panel when g_optAnimations is set, which is a second, independent confirmation of that flag.

functions.name: Screen_DrawBattlefield
functions.comment: Screens 0x28 and 0x29, and the frame around 0x2A: the battle sidebar - Misc sheet frames 0, 1 and 2 at x 480, the same 162-pixel column the campaign uses - the menu bar, and the field or siege palette chosen by g_battleIsSiege. The main loop treats 0x28 .. 0x2A as one range.

functions.name: BattleDebug_Panel
functions.comment: The developers' own battle debug overlay. It prints figure and unit fields beside their original labels - FIGURE / map x / map y / tg x / tg y / routed / hold it / state / on route / hits / walking / barred / target / dirc / delay / dly state / targeted / selected / selctd seen / polar dirc / mov straff, and GROUP / re targ / map x / map y / targ x / targ y / orders / firing. This is the primary evidence for the field names in docs/battle.md.

functions.name: Sound_Init
functions.comment: DirectSoundCreate(0, &g_directSound, 0), SetCooperativeLevel(hwnd, PRIORITY), then the primary buffer. Called once at start-up, immediately before the prime-and-stop of setup.wav and the pumkin measurement.

functions.name: Sound_Shutdown
functions.comment: Stops both streaming channels and releases.

functions.name: Sound_LoadBank
functions.comment: Preloads up to 20 short samples into DirectSound buffers from a char[count][16] table of file names: mmioOpenA, CreateSoundBuffer, Lock/copy/Unlock. Called twice with two different banks - see Sound_LoadKingdomBank and Sound_LoadBattleBank - so the SAME SLOT NUMBER means a different sound on the campaign than in a battle. Stores at &DAT_00522B00 + i*4 from i=0 while the players read from &DAT_00522AFC, so a SLOT is one MORE than the entry it names (docs/decisions.md C51).

functions.name: Sound_PlaySlot
functions.comment: Plays a preloaded bank slot ONLY IF THAT BUFFER IS NOT ALREADY PLAYING - it reads GetStatus and returns 0 on DSBSTATUS_PLAYING. That drop-if-busy is the whole of the original effect mixing policy: Unit_MoveInFacing asks for a movement sound on every step of every moving unit and gets one continuous march rather than a stack. SLOT NUMBERS ARE 1-BASED: this reads &DAT_00522AFC + slot*4 while Sound_LoadBank writes &DAT_00522B00 + i*4, so slot n is bank entry n-1 (docs/decisions.md C51). Gated on g_optSoundEffects.

functions.name: Sound_RestartSlot
functions.comment: SetCurrentPosition(0) then Play, unconditionally - the other verb, and the one that does NOT drop when busy. Widget_Test (0x0040DA1E) uses it for slot 1, click3.wav, on every widget press. Slot numbers are 1-based; see Sound_PlaySlot.

functions.name: Sound_FreeSlot
functions.comment: Stop and Release one bank buffer.

functions.name: Sound_RewindSlot
functions.comment: SetCurrentPosition(0) on one bank buffer.

functions.name: Music_Play
functions.signature: undefined4 Music_Play(char * name, DWORD_PTR channel, undefined4 loop)
functions.comment: Start a STREAMED track on a channel: channel 0 is music and is gated on g_optMusic, channel 1 is a looping effect and is gated on g_optSoundEffects. Stops whatever the channel held, copies the 16-byte name into g_musicChannelName, opens the stream and starts the refill timer. Both music pickers end here.

functions.name: Music_IsActive
functions.comment: Whether a streaming channel is playing, with the same two option gates in front of it.

functions.name: Music_OpenStream
functions.comment: Opens the RIFF through the mmio helpers and sizes a DirectSound buffer to a fixed number of slices. The streaming half of Music_Play.

functions.name: Music_StartRefill
functions.comment: Play(LOOPING) then timeBeginPeriod + timeSetEvent(Music_Refill, channel) - a multimedia timer drives double-buffered refill. This is why the original can stream 3.8 MB tracks in 1996.

functions.name: Music_Stop
functions.comment: timeKillEvent, timeEndPeriod, Stop, close the mmio handle.

functions.name: Music_Refill
functions.comment: The timeSetEvent callback that refills the streaming buffer behind the play cursor.

functions.name: Sound_PlayFile
functions.signature: undefined4 Sound_PlayFile(char * name, int isSpeech, int loop)
functions.comment: One-shot: loads a whole .wav into a DirectSound buffer and plays it. isSpeech = 1 gates on g_optSpeech, 0 gates on g_optSoundEffects. Every fanfare, every troop cry and every voice line goes through here; Msg_PlayVoice is a name lookup in front of it.

functions.name: Sound_OneShotBusy
functions.comment: GetStatus bit test on the one-shot buffer - Sound_PlayFile will not interrupt itself.

functions.name: Sound_StopOneShot
functions.comment: Stop and release the one-shot buffer. Msg_PlayVoice calls it before every voice line, so a lord cuts off the previous lord.

functions.name: Merchant_SpawnAll
functions.comment: Spawns one type-3 merchant, owner 6 (nobody), on a free road tile near each start county, stopping at the first zero start county. Sets the unit's route index (its name, L2.eng group 5) and route cursor, and counts them into g_merchantCount. 18 of the 44 shipped maps get all six merchants; one gets a single merchant.

functions.name: County_FindFreeRoadTile
functions.comment: Map_FindFreeRoadTileNear around the county's anchor tile for r = 1, 2, 3.

functions.name: County_FindFreeOpenTile
functions.comment: Map_FindFreeOpenTileNear around the county's anchor tile for r = 1, 2, 3.

functions.name: Merchant_AdvanceAll
functions.comment: Turn phase 6, step 1. For every type-3 unit awaiting a destination, walks row (unitIndex - 1) of g_merchantRoutes cyclically from the unit's route cursor, skipping entries above g_countyCount, and sends the merchant to the next county on its route. It indexes the table by unit index, not by the unit's stored route number - which only works because the merchants occupy unit slots 1..6.

functions.name: Merchant_ResetStall
functions.comment: Reloads the live stall at 0x005532A0 - 16 goods of 16 bytes - with the base prices from g_goodsPrice and zeroes each good's second word. Sheep and wool are copied in with their price of zero like everything else, so the stall carries rows for two goods Merchant_Trade has no branch for. [V] IT IS CALLED EXACTLY ONCE IN THE BINARY, from Game_New's setup, and nothing else writes either word of any row - so the stall price of every good is the g_goodsPrice entry for the whole game, and the second word stays 0. The only thing that moves a merchant's price is the markup in Trade_BeginGood.

functions.name: Merchant_Trade
functions.signature: void Merchant_Trade(undefined4 unused, int qty, int good, int buyPrice, int sellPrice, int realm, uint county)
functions.comment: The one function that moves a good between a merchant and a player. Positive qty buys at buyPrice, negative sells at sellPrice, and every good is refused if the stock or the treasury will not cover it. The good ids are L2.eng group 6: 1 grain and 2 cattle live in the county, 4 ale is spent immediately through Ale_Apply and never stored, 6/7/8 are the realm's iron, stone and timber, and 9..14 map to realm weapons[3],[4],[1],[0],[2],[5]. A realm of 0 - an unowned county trading with itself - pays out of county +0x1F4 instead. The tail re-runs the county's herd crowding, rations, estimates and labour twice. [V] Two things fall out that could each have gone the other way. The weapon mapping read through group 6 gives weapons = crossbow, mace, sword, pike, bow, mail, which is independently what docs/armies.md derived from g_weaponCost; and the starting-armoury table at 0x004DC070 row 2 reads {0,0,50,50,50,0} under it, which is exactly the England fixture's armoury - 50 swords, 50 pikes, 50 bows. [V] There is no case for good 3 (Sheep) or good 5 (Wool) in either direction. A price of zero would still let a good be sold for nothing; the absence of a branch means nothing can move them at all.

functions.name: Ale_Apply
functions.comment: The ale happiness rule, and the only writer of county +0x219 that ADDS to it. Its ladder is on crowns spent against population/10: one point per tenth of the population's worth of crowns, five at most, then clamped again to 5 minus +0x219 - the happiness ale has already given this county. The gain is added to happiness, to +0x219, and to the shownAle display field. CORRECTED: this entry said "nothing in the binary resets +0x219, so the cap is for the life of the game". Happiness_UpdateAll (0x0044BAEA) zeroes it every season for every county, beside shownAle, so the five points are a SEASONAL allowance - which is also what Readme.txt's "Ale Limitations" says. docs/decisions.md C53. Note the argument is the money, not the barrels: Merchant_Trade passes buyPrice * qty.

functions.name: Trade_BeginGood
functions.comment: HOW A MERCHANT'S PRICE IS SET, and the whole of it. Runs when a good is picked on the stall. Zeroes the pending quantity (0x00554170), the crown total (0x00553F64) and the ale preview; picks the icon page from the good id (<6, <9, else); sets the arrows' floor (0x0053E9E4) to MINUS what the seller holds - county grain or herd for goods 1 and 2, the local player's realm iron/stone/wood or weapons[3],[4],[1],[0],[2],[5] for 6..14, and an explicit 0 for ale, which is why ale cannot be sold; then sellPrice(0x0057C8C0) = g_merchantStall[good], markup = max(1, Pct(sellPrice, g_units[DAT_00553C64].morale)), markup = 0 if the good is ale, buyPrice(0x0055CD70) = sellPrice + markup, and the arrows' ceiling (0x0057A0FC) = buyPrice == 0 ? 0 : realm gold / buyPrice. [V] So THE SELL PRICE NEVER MOVES - Merchant_ResetStall runs once a game - and the buy price is the base plus the CLICKED MERCHANT'S OWN MORALE as a percentage of it. Merchant_SpawnAll writes morale 100 into every merchant and nothing in the binary ever writes a merchant's morale again, so in the shipped game the buy price is exactly twice the sell price - which is the manual's "such as 30/60" and the published guides' doubled table, both, as the morale=100 case of one formula. Ai_BuyGood and Ai_SellGood apply the identical markup off the county's own stall slot, so this is the price for everybody.

functions.name: Merchant_ResetRoutes
functions.comment: Zeroes the 6x16 g_merchantRoutes table and the 6-byte g_merchantStartCounty array, at the top of Map_LoadPlanes.

functions.name: Merchant_RouteAppend
functions.comment: Appends `county` to the first free cell of row `route - 1` of g_merchantRoutes. Called from Map_LoadPlanes for every castle tile with a non-zero plane 4. See docs/formats/plane4.md.

functions.name: Merchant_PickStartCounties
functions.comment: For each of the six routes, picks a start county no earlier route has claimed: entry 0, then entries 2, 4, 6..., then 3, 5, 7... after running off the end; entry 1 is never tried and it gives up after five retries. Because g_merchantStartCounty starts zeroed, a row with no free candidate stores 0 - which stops Merchant_SpawnAll dead. On slot 15 (Rorschach) the dedup fails and two merchants share county 8.

functions.name: Merchant_StartCountyTaken
functions.comment: 1 if `county` already appears in g_merchantStartCounty. Note it also returns 1 for county 0, because unset entries are 0.

functions.name: Transport_Spawn
functions.signature: void Transport_Spawn(int owner, int county, byte dest)
functions.comment: Creates a type-4 transport near `county` and deducts the cargo from that county's stores.

functions.name: Transport_RetargetAll
functions.comment: Turn phase 3, step 1. For every type-4 unit, unconditionally: destX/destY = the anchor of the unit's cargo county (+0x167), destCounty = that county, hasNoDestination = 0, then the two-pass path (Move_FloodFill mode 1, retried at mode 0 if the road route needs 150 or more waypoints) and moving = 1. It does not test hasNoDestination, which is what lets a transport resume a journey it could not finish last season. The destination is the anchor itself, not a free tile near it - that is the merchant's rule and the two differ.

functions.name: Transport_Deliver
functions.comment: If the type-4 unit's destination county matches, adds its cargo to that county's stores.

functions.name: Map_LatticeCellForTile
functions.comment: Reverse lookup: scans the screen lattice for a given tile-array offset to find its screen cell.

functions.name: Map_BuildLattice
functions.comment: Clears g_screenLattice, reloads the tail with Map_LoadLattice, then projects all 64x64 tiles into it for rotation 0/2/4/6. Rotation 0 is row = 1+y+x, col = (64-y+x)/2, value = (64*y+x)*8 - exactly the mapping docs/formats/maps-layers.md section 4 verifies against a live process.

functions.name: Map_ClampScroll
functions.comment: Clamps g_mapStartCol to 0..0x40-g_mapViewCols and g_mapStartRow to 0..0x80-g_mapViewRows. At the far zoom that is col <= 24 and row <= 0, i.e. no vertical scroll at all.

functions.name: Map_PickTile
functions.comment: Screen -> lattice hit test for the campaign map. Rejects x outside [g_mapViewX, g_mapViewX + pitch*cols) and y outside [viewY + rowStep, viewY + rowStep*(rows+1)), then divides by g_mapTileHalfStep and g_mapRowStep and resolves the diamond with a parity and remainder test. Returns 0 when the cell is off-map.

functions.name: Map_RotateCW
functions.comment: g_mapRotation += 2 (mod 8), rebuilds the lattice and re-projects the scroll origin into the new orientation.

functions.name: Map_RotateCCW
functions.comment: g_mapRotation -= 2 (mod 8), the inverse of Map_RotateCW.

functions.name: Map_DrawSurroundTile
functions.signature: undefined8 Map_DrawSurroundTile(undefined4 x, undefined4 y, int mode)
functions.comment: Draws an off-map surround cell: base bank, frame = the lattice cell value minus 0x0FFF0000, which is the background byte the map file stores in its 65x129 tail.

functions.name: Troops_Load
functions.comment: Parses TROOPS.ENG / TROOPS2.ENG / TROOPS3.ENG into g_troopsTable. The in-memory layout is short[35][2][5][11] - side outer (stride 0x6E), difficulty inner (stride 0x16) - and difficulty groups 0,1,3,4 are then overwritten with Normal at +16%, +8%, -8% and -16% on troop types 0..6 only.

functions.name: Skirmish_Setup
functions.comment: Sets up a stand-alone skirmish: army records 1 and 2, loads BATTLES.ENG and the TROOPS table, fills both armies.

functions.name: Skirmish_FillArmies
functions.comment: Copies one row of g_troopsTable into the two army records used by the battle, choosing the side by whether the player is the attacker and the difficulty column per player, then recomputes each army total men (+0x168) and autocalc strength.

functions.name: Skr_ReadMap
functions.comment: Reads one .skr terrain layer: 0x1900 bytes at file offset index * 0x1900 + 0x1674. See docs/formats/skr.md.

functions.name: Smk_Play
functions.signature: int Smk_Play(int path, int x, int y, int mode, int returnScreen)
functions.comment: Plays a Smacker movie. Calls Smk_Open and, if it opened, parks g_screenId at 0x22 - the movie screen - after stashing returnScreen in g_smkReturnScreen for Smk_OnFinished; if it did not open, it goes straight to returnScreen. Seven callers, and they are the game's whole video inventory: the setup chain, CastleBuild_Confirm, Msg_DrawWindow, Battle_CheckOutcome and Smk_ReplayIntro.

functions.name: Smk_PlayThenClose
functions.signature: int Smk_PlayThenClose(int path, int x, int y)
functions.comment: Smk_Open followed immediately by SmackClose and Restore_WorkingDir - a movie played to completion inside the call rather than driven by the screen loop. NO CALLERS in the decompiled corpus, so what it was for is not established.

functions.name: Smk_Open
functions.signature: int Smk_Open(int path, int x, int y, int mode)
functions.comment: Opens a .smk: Smk_BindDirectSound, then Cd_PathForFile or Hd_PathForFile depending on File_Exists' verdict, then SmackOpen(path, flags, -1) with flags 0x2000 when DirectSound is up and 0x2400 when mode == 1. Sets g_smkPlaying, calls SmackToBuffer(smack, x, y, 640, 480, g_backBufferBits, 0) and hands off to Smk_PlayLoop. Logs "OK :SMK starting smack " or "ERR:SMK Could not open " and then "MEM:Max alloc after = " with Mem_AvailPhysical.

functions.name: Smk_PlayLoop
functions.comment: The movie's own frame loop: SmackWait, SmackDoFrame, SmackToBufferRect, SmackNextFrame, locking and unlocking the surface around each frame ("ERR:DD surface lock error:"), applying the movie's palette through Smk_ApplyPalette, and ending on "OK :SMK natural end of " into Smk_OnFinished.

functions.name: Smk_Skip
functions.comment: The player skipped the movie: closes it and runs Smk_OnFinished. Its log line is the game's own word for the case - "OK :SMK user ends ". Called from Screen_FrameInput, from 0x0043AD25 and from Net_LeaveGame.

functions.name: Smk_CloseQuiet
functions.comment: Closes a playing movie WITHOUT running Smk_OnFinished and without logging - the teardown path, called only from App_WndProc's WM_DESTROY.

functions.name: Smk_OnFinished
functions.comment: What happens when a movie ends, and it is where the title sequence is chained: during startup (g_appPhase == 1) intro.smk hands to imptitle.smk at (0x50, 0x50) and imptitle.smk hands to credits.smk at (0, 0), each returning to screen 0x1F; otherwise it restores g_screenId from g_smkReturnScreen, reloads the county or battle art and repaints. The chain is driven by strcmp against the stored path, not by a table.

functions.name: Smk_IsPlaying
functions.comment: Returns g_smkPlaying. Read by exactly two callers and both matter: Gfx_Present skips presenting while a movie is up, and App_WndProc's WM_PAINT routes to Smk_OnPaint instead of the ordinary repaint.

functions.name: Smk_CopyPalette
functions.comment: Copies 256 RGB triples out of the Smack structure at +0x6C into g_paletteRgb. That fixes SmackBuf's palette at offset 0x6C, read out of the running game rather than from a header.

functions.name: Smk_BindDirectSound
functions.comment: Calls SmackSoundUseDirectSound (imported as _SetDirectSoundHWND_4) with g_directSound, once, guarded by a latch. Always returns 1.

functions.name: Smk_ApplyPalette
functions.comment: Smk_CopyPalette then Palette_Upload - the movie's palette becomes the screen palette every frame.

functions.name: Smk_ReplayIntro
functions.comment: Stops the music and replays one of the intro movies, chosen by g_smkTestIndex into the 16-byte filename table beginning at 0x004D4D60 ("Intro.smk"). Its only caller is SmackTest_Close, so this is the debug movie viewer's replay button.

functions.name: Smk_OnPaint
functions.comment: WM_PAINT while a movie is up: BeginPaint, PatBlt the movie's own width and height (SmackBuf +4 and +8) with BLACKNESS (0x42), EndPaint, then SmackSoundOnOff/SmackGoto/SmackSoundOnOff to re-seek to the frame we were on. Independently fixes SmackBuf +4 and +8 as width and height.

functions.name: Gfx_BlitRectToWindow
functions.signature: void Gfx_BlitRectToWindow(int x, int y, int w, int h)
functions.comment: Copies one rectangle of the back buffer to the primary surface, offset by the window's client origin. Windowed it is IDirectDrawSurface::Blt (vtable +0x14) with DDBLT_WAIT|DDBLT_ASYNC (0x1000200); full-screen it is BltFast (+0x1C) with DDBLTFAST_WAIT (0x10). Both vtable offsets are the documented IDirectDrawSurface slots and all six calls in the binary agree.

functions.name: Gfx_BlitScreenToWindow
functions.comment: Gfx_BlitRectToWindow for the whole 640x480 frame. Called from App_WndProc when the window moves or resizes while a movie is on screen (g_screenId 0x22).

functions.name: Display_Init
functions.comment: Sets g_desktopBpp = GetDeviceCaps(BITSPIXEL) * GetDeviceCaps(PLANES) and FORCES g_optFullScreen = 1 whenever that is not 8. On any modern desktop the Display panel's 'Full screen' row is therefore a permanent Yes that Opt_ToggleFullScreen also refuses to change (it raises message 260 instead). We do not reproduce it: this engine is a winit window. See crates/l2-game/src/screens/options.rs.

functions.name: Display_ReleaseSurfaces
functions.comment: Releases the clipper, the back buffer and the primary surface, in that order, and - only when alsoReleaseDirectDraw is set - the IDirectDraw object itself, logging "OK :DD Released.". Also zeroes g_backBufferBits, which is why any pointer into the back buffer held across a mode change is stale.

functions.name: Display_ClearSurfaces
functions.comment: UpdateWindow, then a DDBLT_COLORFILL|DDBLT_WAIT (0x1000400) Blt of colour 0 over the primary surface (windowed) or over back buffer and primary in turn (full-screen). Its three failure messages number themselves - "ERR:DD Clearing(W) Fill failed ddrval:", "... failed no:" 1 and 2 - which is how the two full-screen calls are told apart in a log.

functions.name: Display_CreateSurfaces
functions.comment: Creates the drawing surfaces and says so in its own words. Windowed: one primary surface, one system-memory back buffer through Display_CreateSurface(g_screenStride, g_screenHeight, 1), an IDirectDrawClipper (IDirectDraw vtable +0x10) bound to the game window and attached to the primary with SetClipper (+0x70) - "OK :DD Creating one Vram and one system surface." ... "OK :DD Surfaces created and clipper attached.". Full-screen: primary plus back buffer and no clipper - "OK :DD Creating one Vram only." ... "OK :DD Surface created.". Locks each surface once at creation to capture g_backBufferBits.

functions.name: Display_CreateSurface
functions.signature: int Display_CreateSurface(int width, int height, int inSystemMemory)
functions.comment: IDirectDraw::CreateSurface (vtable +0x18) for an offscreen plain surface of the given size, in system memory when the third argument is set. Returns the surface or 0 after logging "ERR:DD ExtraSurface failed.".

functions.name: Palette_Create
functions.comment: Builds the 256 PALETTEENTRYs (Palette_ToWindowedEntries or Palette_ToFullScreenEntries), releases any existing palette, creates a new one with IDirectDraw::CreatePalette (vtable +0x14, flags 0x44 = DDPCAPS_8BIT|DDPCAPS_ALLOW256) and attaches it with IDirectDrawSurface::SetPalette (+0x7C). When resetSystemUse is set and we are windowed it first toggles SetSystemPaletteUse to SYSPAL_NOSTATIC and back, the standard trick for reclaiming the twenty system colours.

functions.name: Palette_ToFullScreenEntries
functions.comment: Expands g_paletteRgb into g_paletteFull as PALETTEENTRYs. Index 0 is forced to the RGB at 0x004D50F0 and index 255 to the one at 0x004D4E2E+765, both with peFlags 0; indices 1..254 carry peFlags 4 (PC_RESERVED). So full-screen the game keeps 254 of the 256 slots.

functions.name: Palette_ToWindowedEntries
functions.comment: The windowed twin of Palette_ToFullScreenEntries, and the asymmetry is the point: indices 0..9 and 0xF6..0xFF are read BACK from the system palette into g_paletteRgb rather than written to it, and only 10..0xF5 are ours with peFlags 4. That is Windows' twenty static system colours, and it is why our own palette handling must reserve the same twenty if a windowed screenshot is ever to match.

functions.name: Palette_Upload
functions.comment: Rebuilds the entry table for the current mode and pushes all 256 entries with IDirectDrawPalette::SetEntries (vtable +0x18). The per-frame path; Palette_Create is the once-per-mode path.

functions.name: Screen_FrameInput
functions.comment: The FOURTH function that switches on g_screenId, and the one nothing had read: 8,140 bytes, 49 hand-written arms covering 50 screen ids, 150 g_screenId writes. Called once per frame from Battle_Frame (0x004B99C0) as the LAST thing in the frame, after every draw pass - so its navigation lands one frame late by construction. Its shape: FUN_0047685D (right-release dismisses the message scroll, and swallows the click) then Screen_HandleInput (the widget tables, LEFT BUTTON ONLY - it names no right-button global anywhere) and then, only if neither consumed the input, the per-screen arms. It is where the right mouse button lives: DAT_004E6900 (right RELEASED this frame) is tested 48 times and is how nearly every screen in the game is left, which is what L2.eng group 12 index 0, 'Click Right to Exit', tells the player. It also runs the OK-button hit test 26 times (FUN_0040E7E4), force-closes every open panel when DAT_0055403C (Turn_End) or DAT_00553FC8 (the multiplayer sync latch) says the turn is no longer the local player's, owns a falling-edge 'the map scrolled' latch across the frame boundary (DAT_0057CAC4 -> DAT_00565488), clears the WM_KEYDOWN edge DAT_004EABB4, and in individual arms sends Net_SendCommand(6, 0), calls Setup_StartGame, Map_ConfirmMoveOrder and Battle_Decline, and loads vill_gd8.pl8 and demo1.pl8. So it is not only navigation and 'HandleBack' would be far too narrow: right-close is 19 of the 49 arms and 36% of the body. INFERRED rather than verified: every line of the body has been read and the census, the state writes and the call-site placement come from the code, but the ~35 callees the arms dispatch to have not been read and the g_screenId -> screen mapping was not re-derived here. docs/screens-county.md 1 and 2.6. WHERE THE WRITES GO, from the decompilation: 100 g_screenId writes in the body (the '150' above counts the disassembly's stores, not the C statements), of which 57 are the literal 0 - the campaign map - and only 15 restore a screen the game remembered: 11 g_menuPrevScreen, 2 g_screenIdSaved, 2 g_sliderPrevScreen. So a screen's exit is a CONSTANT compiled into its own arm and not a memory of where it was opened from, which is why a panel opened over the village exits to the map and takes the village with it. The job popup is the apparent exception and is a constant too: 0x0F's arm is 'if (DAT_005533F4 == 0) g_screenId = 0x02; else g_screenId = 0', a flag the two call sites set. docs/bugs.md B63.

functions.name: Map_ScrollStep
functions.comment: Applies g_mapScrollDir 0..7 (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, NW) to the scroll origin: row moves by +/-2*g_mapScrollStep and col by +/-g_mapScrollStep, which is one map tile per step. Reverts the move when Map_ScrollThrottle says it is too soon. In battle it moves the battle view origin instead.

functions.name: Map_EdgeScroll
functions.comment: Turns the desktop cursor position into g_mapScrollDir: an edge is the outermost pixel of the desktop (x == 0, x == GetSystemMetrics(0)-1, likewise for y), and 8 means no edge. Returns 0 without scrolling when the campaign map is at the far zoom, so the far view never moves.

functions.name: BattleMap_Click
functions.comment: Battle overview click. Accepts x in 480..639 and y in 24..183 and maps it to a battlefield cell by (x-480)/2, (y-24)/2 - a 160x160 panel at 2 pixels per cell over an 80x80 battlefield.

functions.name: Minimap_Click
functions.comment: Campaign minimap click. Accepts x in 480..607 and y in 25..152, reads g_minimapCounty[(x-480) + (y-25)*128] and, for a non-zero county, selects it and calls Map_CentreOnTile. That 128x128 rectangle is exactly the raster Minimap_Load filled.

functions.name: Screen_HitRegion
functions.comment: Classifies the cursor: region 1 is y < 24 (the menu bar), region 2 is the overview panel rectangle g_overviewX/W by g_overviewY/H, whose top is raised by 24 in campaign mode - so campaign region 2 is x 480..639, y 24..207.

functions.name: Map_CentreOnTile
functions.comment: Scans the 129x65 lattice for the cell holding tileOffset and, only at zoom 0, sets g_mapStartCol = col-4 and g_mapStartRow = (row & ~1) - 12. The row is forced even because the render walk alternates aligned and half-offset lattice rows from the origin.

functions.name: Minimap_ModeButtonClicked
functions.comment: The four icons in the strip beside the minimap: return Hotspot_Test(0x262, 0x20, &g_minimapModeButtons, 4) != 0. [V] First of Screen_FrameInput's six sidebar guards on both the campaign map (screen 0) and the village (0x02). The table it tests is g_minimapModeButtons at 0x004DC620.

functions.name: Sidebar_ButtonClicked
functions.comment: The six buttons along the bottom of the county sidebar, and the whole of it: return Hotspot_Test(0x1DE, 0x1AE, &g_sidebarButtons, 6) != 0. [V] It is the SECOND of the six guards Screen_FrameInput runs on screen 0x02 - the village - before it reaches a single village verb, which is what makes the sidebar clickable with the town square open. The other five are Minimap_ModeButtonClicked, CountyStrip_Click, Labour_SplitSliderDrag, CountyStrip_JobClick and FUN_00439079, and every one of them hit-tests x >= 0x1DE. The village's two drag screens, 0x05 and 0x06, test none of them, so the whole column is dead for the length of a peasant drag. docs/screens-county.md 6.4.4a; docs/decisions.md C59.

functions.name: Battle_ButtonClicked
functions.comment: Hotspot_Test(0x1E0, 0x1C0, &DAT_004DC710, 5) -- the five 32x32 battle buttons in a row at (480, 448): pause, retreat, the siege gate, charge, autocalc. The table records are (0,0)..(128,0) at size 32, so the strip is exactly the right panel width.

functions.name: Setup_StartGame
functions.comment: The Start button. [V] In a single-player game it calls Game_NewGame and drops to g_screenId 0. It is also what the OK button on the conquest screen reaches while the campaign counter is below 8, which settles what carries across a campaign map boundary: nothing does. Each map of a campaign is a whole new game, and the only state that survives is g_campaignMap, g_campaignTrack and g_gameOutcome.

functions.name: Setup_ChooseCampaign
functions.comment: Setup page 4. [V] Stores the clicked hotspot in g_campaignTrack and starts the campaign counter at 2 for hotspot 1 and 0 otherwise - which is why the second campaign is six maps and the first is eight, and why both still end on the same "counter < 8" test.

functions.name: Setup_SetOption
