functions.comment: The custom game's twelve drop-downs, all of them: one if/else if chain on the option index writing one of g_setupOpt* at 0x0053F288..0x0053F2B4. Called from FUN_00433A23 with the clicked row minus one, then calls Setup_RecountAiLords. NOT the g_opt* block - these are the twelve selections, and Setup_CommitOptions turns them into what a game runs on.

functions.name: Setup_RecountAiLords
functions.comment: g_aiLordCount = (g_setupOptNobles + 2) - g_netHumanPlayers, then Realms_AssignLords. Run after every option change and after every scenario change, so the lord count always agrees with the Nobles drop-down and the lobby.

functions.name: Menu_NewGame
functions.comment: File > New Game (L2.eng group 1 index 1). Opens the confirmation box with prompt 1, "Start a new game?", whose yes branch is FUN_00433deb.

functions.name: Menu_LoadGame
functions.comment: File > Load (group 1 index 2). Globs *.sav, or *.svb / *.sva in a network game, saves g_screenId into g_screenIdSaved and opens screen 0x35.

functions.name: Menu_SaveGame
functions.comment: File > Save (group 1 index 3). The same glob as Menu_LoadGame, then screen 0x36.

functions.name: SaveLoad_Cancel
functions.comment: The cross of the save/load box (record 1 of g_saveLoadWidgets, frame 31). On the front end it restores g_setupPage; anywhere else it restores g_screenId from g_screenIdSaved, which is the value Menu_LoadGame and Menu_SaveGame put there.

functions.name: SaveLoad_Scroll
functions.comment: The scroll arrows of both file lists, and the reason their hotspot fields hold odd numbers: the widget's hotspot id is the row delta and its hotspot arg is which list. The save/load box passes -3 / +3 with arg 1 and a 15-row window; the skirmish box passes -1 / +1 with arg 2 and a 5-row window. Clamped at 0 and at g_fileListCount minus the window.

functions.name: Menu_Quit
functions.comment: File > Quit (group 1 index 4). Opens the confirmation box with prompt 0, "Exit the game?", whose yes branch FUN_0043441c leaves for screen 0x1F.

functions.name: Menu_AdvancedOptions
functions.comment: Options > Advanced (group 2 index 1) -> screen 0x39. Refused during a network game unless DAT_00553248 is set, with message 0xE3 instead.

functions.name: Opt_ToggleAdvancedFarming
functions.comment: Row 1 of the advanced options, "Advanced farming": flips the already-named g_optAdvancedFarming. In a network game it refuses, shows tip 0x32 and drops back to g_menuPrevScreen - all four advanced rules are frozen once play is deterministic.

functions.name: Opt_ToggleArmyForaging
functions.comment: Row 2, "Army foraging": flips g_optArmiesEat and then re-runs Ration_Apply and County_RefreshEstimates for every county, because the rule changes this turn's food.

functions.name: Opt_ToggleExploration
functions.comment: Row 3, "Exploration": flips g_optExploration.

functions.name: Opt_ToggleFightHumansOnly
functions.comment: Row 4, "Fight humans only?": flips g_optFightHumansOnly, which the painter displays inverted - 0 shows "Yes".

functions.name: Opt_ToggleTipScreens
functions.comment: Help options row 1, "Tip screens": flips g_optTipScreens.

functions.name: Opt_ToggleToolTips
functions.comment: Help options row 2, "Tool tips": flips g_optToolTips.

functions.name: Menu_HelpHowDoI
functions.comment: Help > "How do I..." (group 3 index 2). Enqueues message 0x123 and returns to g_menuPrevScreen. The five topics use five consecutive ids, 0x123 .. 0x127.

functions.name: Menu_HelpGrowGrain
functions.comment: Help > "Grow grain?" (group 3 index 3): message 0x124.

functions.name: Menu_HelpBuildCastle
functions.comment: Help > "Build a castle?" (group 3 index 4): message 0x125.

functions.name: Menu_HelpMakeWeapons
functions.comment: Help > "Make Weapons?" (group 3 index 5): message 0x126.

functions.name: Menu_HelpManageTurn
functions.comment: Help > "Manage each turn.?" (group 3 index 6): message 0x127.

functions.name: Opt_GameHelpContents
functions.comment: Help options row 3, "Start game help": WinHelpA(hwnd, "l2help.hlp", HELP_CONTENTS, 1). The only WinHelp call reached from the interface.

functions.name: Menu_SoundOptions
functions.comment: Options > Sounds (group 2 index 2) -> screen 0x42.

functions.name: Menu_DisplayOptions
functions.comment: Options > Display (group 2 index 3) -> screen 0x43.

functions.name: Opt_ToggleMusic
functions.comment: Sound options row 1, "Music": flips g_optMusic and either stops the music or restarts it for the current g_battlePhase.

functions.name: Opt_ToggleSoundEffects
functions.comment: Sound options row 2, "Sound effects": flips g_optSoundEffects and re-opens the sample device per g_battlePhase.

functions.name: Opt_ToggleSpeech
functions.comment: Sound options row 3, "Speech": flips g_optSpeech.

functions.name: Opt_ToggleAnimations
functions.comment: Display options row 1, "Animations": flips g_optAnimations.

functions.name: Opt_ToggleFullScreen
functions.comment: Display options row 2, "Full screen". Leaves the panel first - to g_screenId 0 on the campaign, 0x29 in battle - then either refuses with message 0x104 or 299 or flips g_optFullScreen and resets the display mode.

functions.name: Menu_GameSpeed
functions.comment: Options > Game Speed (group 2 index 4). Opens the slider dialog on g_optGameSpeed, step 10, range 0..100, prompt 1 = "Adjusting game speed".

functions.name: Menu_ScrollSpeed
functions.comment: Options > Scroll Speed (group 2 index 5). The same slider on the already-named g_optScrollSpeed, prompt 2 = "Adjusting scroll speed" - the check that fixed the whole table.

functions.name: Menu_GameHelp
functions.comment: Help > Game Help (group 3 index 1) -> screen 0x31, the help-options panel, which is where the WinHelp button lives.

functions.name: Menu_About
functions.comment: Help > About (group 3 index 7) -> screen 0x25.

functions.name: Ui_ConfirmClicked
functions.comment: Both buttons of the confirmation box. Publishes the widget hotspot id - 1 for the tick, 0 for the cross - into g_confirmAnswer and calls g_confirmCallback, which reads it.

functions.name: Ui_SliderUp
functions.comment: The slider dialog's up arrow: adds g_sliderStep while the value is below g_sliderMax.

functions.name: Ui_SliderDown
functions.comment: The slider dialog's down arrow: subtracts g_sliderStep while the value is above g_sliderMin.

functions.name: Map_ToggleZoom
functions.comment: The campaign zoom button: 0 -> Map_ZoomOut, 2 -> Map_ZoomIn. There are only two campaign zooms.

functions.name: Map_ZoomOut
functions.comment: Saves the scroll origin, sets col 0x0E row 0x0C, Map_SetZoom(2), clamps, reloads the 10x6 tile sets through Gfx_LoadCountyMode and plays S033_02.wav.

functions.name: Map_ZoomIn
functions.comment: Restores the saved scroll origin, Map_SetZoom(0), clamps and reloads the 58x30 tile sets.

functions.name: Map_ZoomInAtTile
functions.comment: Zooms in centred on the last picked tile, using the same col-4 / (row & ~1)-12 centring as Map_CentreOnTile.

functions.name: Ale_PreviewGain
functions.comment: The same ladder as Ale_Apply, run on the trade screen's pending crown total at 0x00553F64 into the preview at 0x0053E8C0, so the panel can show what the purchase would buy before it is made. Duplicated code, not a shared helper - which is worth knowing, because a mod that changes one must change both.

functions.name: Merchant_StallHit
functions.comment: Screen 0x08's hit test, and the reason the merchant screen has no rectangles anywhere: good = grid[(mouseX>>3) + (mouseY>>3) * 0x50] out of mercgrid.pl8, which Screen_Merchant read whole into the village's grid buffer. 0 means the pointer is on no ware; otherwise a left press opens screen 0x0C on that good. [V] mercgrid.pl8 is 4,824 bytes = a 24-byte .pl8 header plus an 80 x 60 byte map of 8-pixel cells over the whole 640x480 screen, and the SHIPPED FILE HOLDS EXACTLY TWELVE IDS - 1,2,4,6,7,8,9,10,11,12,13,14. Sheep (3) and wool (5) are on no cell, so there is nowhere on the stall to click for either: the artwork's own statement of what Merchant_Trade's missing branches and g_goodsPrice's two zeros already said.

functions.name: Armoury_GridClick
functions.comment: Screens 0x0A and 0x0D: the armoury hit test. Reads arm_grid.pl8 as grid[(x >> 3) + (y >> 3) * 0x50] at &DAT_00542CF8 - the shared region buffer plus the 24-byte .pl8 header - and treats a non-zero cell as g_uiHotspotId before calling Armoury_ClickRack. So the weapon hanging on the wall is the button. [V] It runs BEFORE Hotspot_Test in both arms. It accepts ANY non-zero cell, and 26 cells of the shipped file hold 60..63: docs/bugs.md N13.

functions.name: Armoury_ClickRack
functions.comment: Open one weapon's rack, from the grid or from a rectangle of g_armouryHotspots. Refuses when g_levyBasket[id].available <= 0, so an empty rack is inert; otherwise it fires the walking-soldier animation (FUN_004AABD8), sets g_armourySelectedType, sets g_screenId = 0x0D, latches g_levyBasket[id].+0x0C to the current chosen count, and calls Armoury_LoadScreen. [V]

functions.name: Levy_EquipOne
functions.comment: Screen 0x0D, g_armouryBuyWidgets record 0 (frame 68): one man picks the weapon up. `if (chosen < remaining && peasants != 0) { chosen++; peasants--; }`. [V] docs/hypotheses.json called this Armoury_BuyLess on the strength of tools/oracle/widgets.js's note that frames 68/66 are minus and plus; the body is a plus, and the diplomacy gift row 0x004DD9D0 settles the frame the same way - its frame-68 record carries hotspot id 1 and FUN_00436372 adds ten crowns for id 1. Nothing on either armoury screen is bought. docs/decisions.md C61.

functions.name: Levy_UnequipOne
functions.comment: Screen 0x0D, g_armouryBuyWidgets record 1 (frame 66): one man puts the weapon down. `if (chosen > 0) { chosen--; peasants++; }`. [V] Was Armoury_BuyMore; see Levy_EquipOne.

functions.name: Levy_UnequipAll
functions.comment: Screen 0x0D, g_armouryBuyWidgets record 2 (frame 58): every man of the selected type puts the weapon down, in a while loop over the same two counters. [V] Was Armoury_BuyPrev, which was a guess from table position alone.

functions.name: Levy_EquipAll
functions.comment: Screen 0x0D, g_armouryBuyWidgets record 3 (frame 60): `while (peasants != 0 && chosen < remaining)`, so it stops at whichever of the men and the weapons runs out first. [V] Was Armoury_BuyNext.

functions.name: Armoury_Button
functions.comment: Screen 0x0A, and record 6 only on 0x0D: the three words down the armoury's right-hand edge, L2.eng 69/6, 69/7 and 69/8. Hotspot id 1 'Create' sets g_confirmAnswer = 1 and calls Army_RaiseConfirm; id 2 'Change' sets g_screenId = 0x17; id 3 'Cancel' sets g_confirmAnswer = 0 and calls Army_RaiseConfirm, whose no-arm is g_screenId = 0 plus Gfx_LoadCountyMode. [V] THIS IS THE ONLY CALLER OF Army_RaiseConfirm A PLAYER CAN REACH: there is no confirm anywhere on the raise-army screen. docs/decisions.md C61.

functions.name: Army_RaiseConfirm
functions.comment: The raise-army screen's yes-callback, and the only door to Army_Create a player has. Two size guards, both &&-ed with the hire flag DAT_0055446C so that hiring a mercenary band bypasses BOTH: a levy total of zero raises message 0xA8 (group 168) and a total under 0x32 raises 0x94 (group 148). Then Army_Create(g_localPlayer, g_selectedCounty, hireMercs, g_levyHappinessCost), with message 0xDD (group 221) when it returns 0 because there was nowhere in the county to stand.

functions.name: RaiseArmy_HireToggle
functions.comment: Screen 0x17, DAT_004DD340 records 1 and 2 - the tick (frame 29, hotspot id 1) at (352, 256) and the cross (frame 31, id 0) at (400, 260): DAT_0055446C = (g_uiHotspotId == 1). [V] The 'Yes'/'No' word the painter prints at (0x1D0, base + 0x98) is a READ-OUT of the flag, 32 pixels clear of the cross, and nothing tests it.

functions.name: RaiseArmy_Continue
functions.comment: Screen 0x17, DAT_004DD340 record 0 (frame 33 at 480, 336), labelled L2.eng 69/9 'Continue': g_screenId = 0x0A then Levy_Seed(g_selectedCounty, g_levyMen). [V] The re-seed is why walking back to the levy screen and forward again strips the men - the slider does not do it, this does.

functions.name: Levy_SliderClick
functions.comment: The levy slider on screen 0x17. Its hit band is x in [0x80, 0x176) and y in [base + 0x10, base + 0x40), where base is 0x80 with a mercenary offer in the county and 0xA0 without - the same local Screen_RaiseArmy lays the whole screen out from. Inside it: x < 0xC4 decrements, x < 0x129 sets g_levyPercent = x - 0xC4, and beyond that increments. Clamps 0..100 and calls Levy_SetPercent. The track's 0xC4 is the exact inverse of the knob's own x, g_levyPercent + 0xC4, over 101 pixels.

functions.name: Levy_SetPercent
functions.comment: The raise-army slider: men = Pct(population, pct), happiness cost = g_armyHappinessCost[pct] plus county +0x2F4, clamped 0..100, then the percentage is walked back until county happiness minus the cost is at least 1. This is what indexes g_armyHappinessCost.

functions.name: Diplo_OpenGift
functions.comment: Widget 0 of the diplomacy screen, group 72 index 2 "Dispatch a gift": screen 0x1A with g_diploKind 0.

functions.name: Diplo_OpenCompliment
functions.comment: Widget 1, index 3 "Send a compliment": g_diploKind 1, and clears the letter draft g_diploLetterDraft.

functions.name: Diplo_OpenInsult
functions.comment: Widget 2, index 4 "Send an insult": g_diploKind 2.

functions.name: Diplo_OpenAlliance
functions.comment: Widget 3, index 5 "Offer an alliance" or 6 "Terminate alliance" - one widget for two rows, and the code picks g_diploKind 4 over 3 exactly when the target is already this realm's ally.

functions.name: Diplo_OpenAskHelp
functions.comment: Widget 4, index 7 "Ask ally for help": g_diploKind 5, county cleared.

functions.name: Diplo_OpenAskAttack
functions.comment: Widget 5, index 8 "Ask ally to attack": g_diploKind 6, county cleared.

functions.name: Diplo_SendClicked
functions.comment: The diplomacy screen's Send button. Validates the county for kinds 5 and 6 (refusals are L2.eng groups 240-244) and the target's existing alliance for kind 3 (group 219), copies the drafted letter into the player's g_diploLetter slot, then calls Diplo_Post - or, in multiplayer, issues net command 0x48 or 0x49 instead.

functions.name: Diplo_PayHelpClicked
functions.comment: The pay-for-help prompt's accept button: Diplo_PayForHelp(myAlly, me, g_diploHelpCounty, g_diploHelpPrice).

functions.name: Castle_OpenScreen
functions.comment: The campaign sidebar's castle button. Refuses a county that is not g_localPlayer's with message 0x70; otherwise seeds DAT_0056D898 (the chooser's 0..4 selection) from castleType - 1, or 0 for a bare plot, and sets g_screenId = 0x1B.

functions.name: CastleBuild_Select
functions.comment: Handler of g_castleTypeWidgets' five rectangles: DAT_0056D898 = g_uiHotspotId, redraw, set the panel's dirty flag. A bare assignment - there is no guard here, so a player may select a castle smaller than the one he has and learns otherwise only from the OK button.

functions.name: CastleBuild_Confirm
functions.comment: g_castleBuildWidgets' handler for both the tick (hotspot 1) and the cross (hotspot 0). Hotspot 0 closes to the map. Hotspot 1 has exactly two guards, both of which also close: castleType == selection+1 sends message 0x93 (L2.eng 147, 'already of the type you are proposing'), selection+1 < castleType sends 0x122 (L2.eng 290, 'your current castle is stronger'). Otherwise Castle_Order(g_selectedCounty, DAT_0056D898) - or Net_SendCommand(0x2B) in multiplayer - and then plays Castle1.smk .. Castle5.smk when g_optAnimations is on.

functions.name: Castle_Order
functions.comment: THE ONLY WRITER of county +0x1C3 to 1, and the whole castle-ordering rule. level is 0-based. If castleType != 0 it copies castleType into castleBuilding (so +0x1C1 is the castle that WAS there, not the one being built) and subtracts g_castleMaterial[castleType-1] from the new cost, refunding a negative difference into the realm. Then castleType = level+1 IMMEDIATELY, castleRuined = 0, castleDegraded = 1, +0x1B0 = 1, +0x1CC = +0x1D8 = g_castleWorkforce[level], +0x1DC = stone total, +0x1E0 = wood total, +0x1C4 = 0; Castle_StampTile, Castle_EvictTile, Labour_ToggleIndustryShare(county, 3, 1); then it takes what the realm HAS and leaves the rest owing in +0x1D0 (stone) and +0x1D4 (wood). THERE IS NO AFFORDABILITY GUARD.

functions.name: Panel_MoveButton
functions.comment: The unit panel's move button. Goes straight to Map_BeginMoveSelection unless the unit is besieging, in which case it asks L2.eng 10/13 'Lift the siege?' first. Map_Click reaches the same place by a different route - it runs Siege_ValidateLink, calls this if the siege link died and opens the siege-preparation screen 0x1D if it did not - so from the map a besieging army never sees the prompt.

functions.name: Map_BeginMoveSelection
functions.comment: Enters the campaign map in move-order mode for g_selectedUnit: rebuilds the cost map, screen 0x10, resets the preview, sets 0x00553ECC to 40 (a counter Map_HoverUnitTarget decrements each frame), CLEARS unit +0x14E (ignoreSettlements) and runs Move_FloodFill from the unit. Also the yes-callback of L2.eng 10/13 'Lift the siege?'. It does not itself break the siege - Unit_OrderMove does, when the order is actually placed.

functions.name: Panel_DisbandButton
functions.comment: Picks the county the army would disband into - its home county, or the county it is standing in if the home county is no longer the owner's - and asks L2.eng 10/6 'Disband army?' only when that county is the owner's. Otherwise message 0x91 = L2.eng group 145: 'Your army must disband to its county of origin. If you no longer rule the county, the army must then disband inside a county that you do rule.' The string states the two-step rule the code implements, clause for clause, which is what makes this [V].

functions.name: Army_DisbandConfirm
functions.comment: The 'Disband army?' yes-callback: Army_Disband, or network command 0x2E under g_multiplayer.

functions.name: Panel_SplitButton
functions.comment: The unit panel's split button, and the gate the Readme states: 'An army normally can only be split only at the start of its movement in a turn.' Refuses with message 0x95 = L2.eng group 149 when movesUsed >= 1 and the screen never opens. Otherwise it seeds the levy basket from the army - slot[t].chosen = troops[t], slot[t].available = 0, slot 7 = mercMen with its available at 0 - sums the two totals into DAT_00554468 and DAT_00554040, and sets g_screenId = 0x11. FUN_004376BB is the same seeding reached from the move-order confirm, for a split INTO a castle.

functions.name: Army_SplitConfirm
functions.comment: The army-division screen's OK. Recomputes both totals, then: with no destination county the minimum a side is 0x32 and the cap 5000; with one, the minimum is ZERO and the cap is that castle's garrison limit less the garrison already inside - which is the Readme's 'When splitting into castles, you may split off less than 50 men.' An empty column cancels silently, a side under the minimum raises message 0x94 (group 148) and a daughter over the cap raises 0x11A (group 282). Then Army_Split, or network command 0x2D.

functions.name: SplitScreen_ToParent
functions.comment: Moves one man from the daughter's column back to the parent's on the army-division screen: slot[hotspot].available -= 1, slot[hotspot].chosen += 1, then both totals are resummed over all eight slots. Hotspot 7 is the mercenary band and swaps it whole rather than by one. SplitScreen_ToDaughter (0x00437E9E) is the same function the other way.

functions.name: SplitScreen_ToDaughter
functions.comment: The twin of SplitScreen_ToParent: one man from the parent's column into the daughter's, and hotspot 7 moves the whole mercenary band.

functions.name: Army_Split
functions.signature: void Army_Split(int realm, int army, int destCounty, int destTileOffset)
functions.comment: The army-division screen's yes-arm. Finds a free tile within five of the parent (FUN_0046733C), spawns a daughter army there and gives it the parent's morale, shield and county but NOT its homeCounty - Unit_Spawn has just zeroed that, so a split army's county of origin is 0 and Army_Disband falls through to wherever it is standing. Each side's troops come from one half of the levy basket: parent from slot[t].chosen, daughter from slot[t].available, and menTotal is the sum of all EIGHT slots so the mercenary band is counted. Both halves get moving = 2. With no destination county both pay movesUsed += 5 - the Readme's 'splitting does not use all the movement for a turn' - and with one, the daughter is given the destination tile and a flood-filled path instead. A band the daughter's column holds moves whole, g_mercBands[band].hiredBy included.

functions.name: Army_Disband
functions.comment: Releases any mercenary band, returns troops[1..6] to the realm's weapons[0..5] - troop type t maps to weapon slot t-1, the same off-by-one Levy_Init uses in the other direction - and returns the men to the county's population, its labour[8].workers and its popArmy. Then Army_Destroy, clear the garrison link, recompute the realm wage bill and re-run the labour allocator and Ration_Apply three times over. The county is the home county, or the current one when the home county has changed hands.

functions.name: Field_SetType
functions.signature: void Field_SetType(uint county, int tile, int brush)
functions.comment: Repaints one map tile's field type for a county and re-runs its food passes. Called from a map click with the brush in g_uiHotspotId; this, not any county panel, is how fields are assigned.

functions.name: CountyStrip_Click
functions.comment: The 2x2 hotspot over the county strip, and the only way to any of the four county panels: x 488..547 / y 182..211 population, x 568..629 / y 182..211 happiness, and the same two columns below y 212 for tax and rations. The dead band 548..567 is where the health thermometer is drawn.

functions.name: CountyStrip_JobClick
functions.comment: The sidebar's lower plate: farm jobs left of x 560, industry right of it. Sets g_jobPanelJob and opens screen 0x0F.

functions.name: Labour_SplitSliderDrag
functions.comment: The farm/industry split slider on the county strip, and it is a DRAG rather than a click: it acts while g_mouseLeftDown is set and g_mouseInputChanged says the pointer moved, and returns 1 without doing anything on the release. Hit box x 0x1DE..0x27F, y 0x101..0x128; left of x=0x213 steps the share down by four, right of x=0x252 up by four, on the track it is ((x - 0x213) * 2) & 0xFC, clamped 0..100. Tested on screens 0 and 0x02, so it works with the village open.

functions.name: Labour_SetIndustryShare
functions.signature: void Labour_SetIndustryShare(int county, unsigned char share)
functions.comment: Writes county +0x08 and re-runs Labour_Allocate, Ration_Apply and County_RefreshEstimates. The slider's only writer in single player; multiplayer sends command 0x27 instead.

functions.name: Village_BandStart
functions.comment: Arms the rubber band on a press inside x 0..0x1FF, y top..top+0x178, and returns 1 - moving the interface to screen 0x05 - once the pointer is 9 or more pixels from where it went down. Below nine it is still a click.

functions.name: Village_BandRelease
functions.comment: Screen 0x05 leaves on the button being released: 2 to screen 0x06 when the band caught somebody, 1 back to the village when it did not.

functions.name: Village_BoxSelect
functions.comment: Marks every peasant icon inside the rubber-band box, and abandons the whole selection if the box reaches into a second cluster. Leaves the cluster in g_villageDragCluster and the count in g_villageDragCount.

functions.name: Village_ClusterAt
functions.comment: Which of the eight clusters the pointer is over, 1-based, or 0.

functions.name: Village_GridAt
functions.comment: Which peasant cluster a point on the village is over, 1-based and clamped to 8, from an 8-pixel grid: (&DAT_00542CF8)[((x-0x40)>>3) + ((y-g_villageTopY)>>3) * 0x2D]. That is vill_gd8.pl8 plus its 24-byte header - 45 x 40 cells covering x 0x40..0x1A8 and y top..top+0x140, and the shipped file is 1,824 bytes exactly.

functions.name: Village_Drop
functions.comment: Screen 0x06's drop. Village_GridAt names the target cluster, the carried icon count is multiplied by county +0xB8 and clamped to what the source job holds, and Labour_Move does the rest. Dropping on the source cluster puts them back.

functions.name: Labour_Move
functions.signature: void Labour_Move(int county, int fromCluster, int toCluster, int workers)
functions.comment: Moves workers between two labour slots of one county and re-runs the county's food and industry passes twice. The caller's count is selected icons times county +0xB8 (popBand), clamped to what the source slot holds - so one icon is one twenty-fifth of the population, rounded up.

functions.name: Village_DoubleClick
functions.comment: The ONLY reader of g_mouseLeftDoubleClick in the binary. On a left double click inside x 0x40..0x1FF, y top..top+0x178, Village_GridAt names the cluster and Village_BalanceAll reassigns its labour. It sits between Village_BandStart and Village_ClickJob in Screen_FrameInput's screen-0x02 ladder; the job popup is deferred 300 ms precisely so this can pre-empt it.

functions.name: Village_BalanceAll
functions.comment: Cluster 6 - Idle townsfolk - runs Village_BalanceJob over every cluster twice, shedding first (fill = 0) and filling second (fill = 1), so no job takes people a later one needs. Any other cluster balances just that one. NOTE: both loops run i < 10 over the eight-entry g_jobClusterToSlot; the two words past the end are 4 and 6, which is what brings slot 4 (iron mining) into the gesture. docs/bugs.md B21a.

functions.name: Village_BalanceJob
functions.signature: int Village_BalanceJob(int county, int cluster, int fill)
functions.comment: One job against the idle pool, in PEOPLE rather than icons. shortfall = wanted < 1 ? 0 : wanted - workers; surplus = useful < 99999 ? workers - useful : 0. With a shortfall and fill set it draws min(idle, shortfall) out of cluster 6; otherwise it pushes the surplus back into cluster 6. The surplus branch is the blue outline's own test seen from the input side.

functions.name: Village_ClickJob
functions.comment: A click that never became a drag: Village_GridAt names the cluster and g_jobPanelJob becomes its labour slot plus one, which opens the job popup (screen 0x0F). FUN_0045183A refuses only cluster 0, and only for a county with neither a quarry nor a mine.

functions.name: Ration_Increase
functions.comment: The ration panel's up arrow. Guards rationWanted < 5.

functions.name: Ration_IncreaseCounty
functions.comment: Raises one county's wanted ration by one, capped at 5, then re-applies rations and redraws.

functions.name: Ration_Decrease
functions.comment: The ration panel's down arrow. Guards rationWanted > 0.

functions.name: Ration_DecreaseCounty
functions.comment: Lowers one county's wanted ration by one, floored at 0.

functions.name: Ration_SliderClick
functions.comment: The grain-to-livestock slider's hit test: (200,220,24,24) steps down, (325,220,24,24) steps up, and (224,220,102,24) jumps to mouseX - 224. Clamped 0..100, and refused outright unless the county's owner is g_localPlayer.

functions.name: Ration_SetSplit
functions.signature: void Ration_SetSplit(int county, int split, int sweep)
functions.comment: Sets county +0x15F and re-runs the food pass; if the new split changes nothing it walks back towards the old value looking for one that does.

functions.name: Panel_OpenRation
functions.comment: Opens the ration panel (screen 0x19).

functions.name: Panel_OpenPopulation
functions.comment: Opens the population panel (screen 0x14).

functions.name: Panel_OpenHappiness
functions.comment: Opens the happiness panel (screen 0x16).

functions.name: Panel_OpenTax
functions.comment: Opens the tax panel (screen 0x15).

functions.name: Tax_Increase
functions.comment: The tax panel's up arrow. Guards taxRate < 0x32 - the player's tax ceiling is 50, and this is where it lives.

functions.name: Tax_IncreaseCounty
functions.comment: Raises one county's tax rate by one, capped at 50, then Tax_RecomputePreview and a redraw.

functions.name: Tax_Decrease
functions.comment: The tax panel's down arrow. Guards taxRate != 0.

functions.name: Tax_DecreaseCounty
functions.comment: Lowers one county's tax rate by one, floored at 0.

functions.name: Minimap_ModeButton
functions.comment: Acts on g_uiHotspotId. THE FOUR BUTTONS ARE NOT RADIO BUTTONS, and this entry used to say they were. In mode 0: 1..3 set g_minimapMode and 4 calls Map_ToggleZoom. In any other mode: 4 turns the overlay off and 1..3 do nothing at all - so food to happiness takes three clicks. The artwork says the same thing from the other side: Misc_cty frame 0x5C, drawn in mode 0, carries four buttons and frame 0x5B, drawn while a mode is up, carries a colour bar and one. docs/decisions.md C59.

functions.name: Turn_End
functions.comment: The sidebar's full-width bottom button: ends the local player's turn by writing 999 into the realm record's +0x00.

functions.name: Sidebar_Button
functions.comment: The five buttons in the 162x30 strip at y 430, on g_uiHotspotId 1..5: the county's army (screen 0x17), the court (screen 0x09), send supplies (screen 0x18), and two more.

functions.name: Battle_PromptAnswered
functions.comment: The handler behind both widgets of DAT_004DDBB0, screen 0x12's whole input. Hotspot id 1 calls Battle_Start; hotspot id 0 calls Battle_Decline. The table holds EXACTLY TWO records -- g_sliderWidgets begins 48 bytes on at 0x004DDBE0 -- and its count DAT_00554408 is written by Battle_ChooseSettlement as 2 when g_battleChoiceOwner == 1 and 0 otherwise, so a bystander's prompt has no widgets at all. Screen_FrameInput's own 0x12 arm is entirely multiplayer (the sync latch and FUN_004BBEA7, which returns 0 unconditionally when g_multiplayer is clear), so IN SINGLE PLAYER THESE TWO WIDGETS ARE THE ONLY WAY OFF THE SCREEN. docs/decisions.md C67. Promoted from docs/hypotheses.json, where it was Screen_BattlePromptClick with the caveat 'whether this is the whole click handler or one arm of it was not checked' -- it is the whole of it, because the table it is the handler for holds exactly two records.

functions.name: Battle_Decline
functions.comment: Answering 'no' to the prompt screen's 'Will you take the field?'. Guarded on g_screenId == 0x12 so it is idempotent, it runs Battle_AutoResolve, Battle_ReturnToCampaign(0) and raises the report screen 0x13. So DECLINING A BATTLE IS EXACTLY THE AUTOCALC - a way out of watching the battle, not out of fighting it. The multiplayer answer timeout and an end-of-turn sync both route here as an auto-decline; in single player the prompt waits forever.

functions.name: SiegePrep_OrderMore
functions.comment: Siege-preparation screen, the increment half of an engine row. Picks its ceiling from g_uiHotspotId - 4 for hotspots 0 and 1 (catapults, siege towers) and 2 for anything else (battering rams) - and refuses to increment at it. Under g_multiplayer it sends network command 0x37 instead. The ceiling is the screen's and not the record's: Siege_Prepare writes 4 towers for the Knight and 3 catapults plus 2 towers for the Countess without consulting it. Ceiling times g_siegeEngineWork is 800 man-seasons for all three rows, which is a second statement that the table is 200/200/400 in record order.

functions.name: SiegePrep_OrderFewer
functions.comment: Siege-preparation screen, the decrement half of an engine row. Refuses at zero; network command 0x37 under g_multiplayer.

functions.name: SiegePrep_AdjustOrder
functions.signature: void SiegePrep_AdjustOrder(int unit, int engine, short delta)
functions.comment: Adds delta to the engine record at unit +0x182 + engine*6 and runs Siege_RecomputeBuildTime, so the seasons-remaining line moves as the player clicks. The tail of both SiegePrep_OrderMore and SiegePrep_OrderFewer.

functions.name: SiegePrep_Button
functions.comment: The siege-preparation screen's two buttons. Hotspot 1 is L2.eng 83/6 'Lift siege': it closes the screen and calls Siege_Break (network command 0x38). Hotspot 2 is 83/7 'Proceed': it closes the screen and launches the assault ONLY IF unit +0x19C is already zero (network command 0x39), so proceeding with work outstanding simply leaves turn phase 2 to carry the build on.

functions.name: Siege_Break
functions.comment: Lifts a siege: clears the besieger's +0x199 and the garrison's +0x19A. Its three callers are together the whole answer to docs/armies.md section 9's 'the lift-siege handler was not traced'. Unit_OrderMove calls it on every successful type-1 move order, so giving a besieging army anywhere to go lifts its siege; Siege_LaunchAssault calls it when the castle is too strong to assault without engines; and the siege-preparation screen's 'Lift siege' button (L2.eng 83/6) calls it directly. L2.eng 10/13 'Lift the siege?' is the confirmation the move-order path asks first.

functions.name: SiegePrep_Proceed
functions.comment: A one-line thunk to Siege_LaunchAssault, called by SiegePrep_Button when the engines are ready.

functions.name: Battle_PauseButton
functions.comment: Battle button 0. DAT_0053F238 = ~DAT_0053F238, and Battle_Start seeds that word 0xFFFFFFFF -- so A BATTLE STARTS PAUSED and the first thing a player does is press this to unpause. While it is set, Battle_OrderClicked and BattleMap_Click both refuse to order and Battle_Frame paints L2.eng group 32 index 0 through FUN_00423B4F. The sound branch under it tests == 1, which a word alternating between 0 and -1 can never be: docs/bugs.md D38.

functions.name: Battle_RetreatButton
functions.comment: Battle button 1, guarded on g_battleChoiceOwner == 1. Ui_OpenConfirm(12) 'Retreat from field?', or Ui_OpenConfirm(11) 'Surrender castle?' when g_battleIsSiege and the local player owns army B. Both callbacks reach FUN_0043BE65, which is Battle_AutoResolve and Battle_ReturnToCampaign(1) -- and neither calls Battle_WriteBackCasualties, so RETREATING DISCARDS EVERY CASUALTY THE BATTLE HAS PRODUCED and the result is computed from the armies as they walked on.

functions.name: Battle_GateButton
functions.comment: Battle button 2. Four guards: g_battleChoiceOwner != 0, g_battleIsSiege (else message 0x6E), the local player owns army B and g_castleLevel >= 3 (else 0x6F), and DAT_0052AF9C not already set (else 0x9D). On a pass it calls FUN_00496B9F, which finds the first cell flagged 0x40, lays a 7x4 patch of surface 3 over it from DAT_004D9E18, adds 4 to both g_siegeApproachScore and g_siegeBreachScore and rebuilds the pathfinding template.

functions.name: Battle_ChargeButton
functions.comment: Battle button 3, and it fires ONCE per battle -- DAT_0055322C is set on the first press and never cleared. Calls FUN_0047A76D.

functions.name: Battle_AutocalcButton
functions.comment: Battle button 4, guarded on g_battleChoiceOwner == 1: Ui_OpenConfirm(9) 'Autocalc battle?'. Same destination as the retreat button.

functions.name: Battle_GiveUp
functions.comment: What all three battlefield confirms do when answered yes: Battle_AutoResolve, then either the report screen 0x13 and Battle_ReturnToCampaign(1) or, in a skirmish, the ratings screen 0x2E. It does NOT call Battle_WriteBackCasualties -- see Battle_RetreatButton.

functions.name: Battle_DragSelect
functions.comment: The battlefield's selection box, and FOUR arms in one function. Gated on DAT_00568964 == 1 (input armed by Battle_Start) and DAT_00553C6C == 0. (1) Left PRESS with g_battleHoverOnField and g_screenId != 0x2A: record the anchor cell in _DAT_0055CE60/64 and the anchor pixel in DAT_0057A0F4/0E8, set g_screenId = 0x2A, and point g_debugSelectedMan at whatever figure is under the press. (2) Button held on 0x2A with g_mouseInputChanged: FUN_0043C247(player, 0, ...) clears and re-boxes the selection live, the 0 being what stops it regrouping units on every pointer motion. (3) g_mouseLeftReleased OR g_mouseLeftDoubleClick on 0x2A: back to 0x29, then FUN_00479CF7 classifies the gesture -- 1 commits the box, 2 nudges the anchor by -8,-8 and the pointer by +8,+8 and commits THAT (so a click on a man selects a 16-pixel square), 0 does nothing at all and in particular does NOT clear the selection. (4) anything else declines and the ladder falls through. THIS IS THE SECOND READER OF g_mouseLeftDoubleClick; docs/decisions.md C61 predicted one and C67 found it. docs/battle.md section 15.5.

functions.name: Battle_CommitSelection
functions.signature: void Battle_CommitSelection(uint player, int commit, int camX, int camY, int ax, int ay, int bx, int by)
functions.comment: Clear, box, and -- only when commit is 1 -- regroup. FUN_00479A71 then FUN_00479B58, and on the committing call FUN_00478987, FUN_00478F0B and Battle_CountMenByType. Battle_DragSelect passes 0 on every frame of a drag and 1 on the release, which is why the highlight follows the box live while the UNITS are only rearranged once.

functions.name: Battle_UnitPanelClicked
functions.comment: The right column's two arms. LEFT PRESS: walk the local player's selected figures in index order against rectangles from DAT_004D31F4 (28-byte records whose first four ints are x, y, w, h for FUN_004B1DEB), with a base offset chosen by DAT_00553078 -- 0 under 13 figures, 12 under 19, 30 otherwise, so three layouts of 12, 18 and 50 slots. A hit calls FUN_0043C4C6, which DROPS that figure from the selection rather than selecting it. The loop breaks at 0x31 < index, so only the first FIFTY banners are clickable whatever the layout. RIGHT RELEASE: FUN_0043C55C clears the whole selection, refused inside x >= 0x1E1 && 0x18 <= y <= 0xB7 -- the overview panel MINUS ITS LEFTMOST COLUMN, because the panel starts at 0x1E0 and the guard tests 0x1E1.

functions.name: BattleMan_Deselect
functions.comment: One banner click: clear that figure selected and selectedSeen bits and regroup. Not a selection verb -- the panel is a grid of the men you already hold.

functions.name: Battle_DeselectAll
functions.comment: BattleMen_ClearSelection plus a redraw request. What the right button does on the battlefield -- see docs/decisions.md C61 on right-click being the systematically missed gesture.

functions.name: Battle_OrderClicked
functions.comment: Five guards, all refusals: g_battleHoverOnField, then NOT g_battleHoverFriendlyPicked, then NOT g_battleHoverFriendly (which is what makes a click on one of your own men a selection and never a destination), then g_mouseLeftReleased, then DAT_00553078 != 0, then DAT_0053F238 == 0 -- the pause. Calls Battle_OrderSelection(DAT_00553F88, DAT_00553F94).

functions.name: Battle_OrderSelection
functions.comment: The click that gives an order. Plays a troop cry -- 2 with an enemy under the cursor, 3 on hover surface 2, else 1 -- sets a 30-frame cooldown in DAT_00553F84 (10 in multiplayer), bumps the per-player order counter DAT_00553100, and calls BattleUnit_Order(DAT_0053E984, x, y, g_battleHoverEnemy, DAT_0053E874, 0). ONE unit, because BattleUnits_RegroupSelection has just made the selection be one unit.

functions.name: Battle_FormationKey
functions.comment: The H and V keys, from the window procedure's WM_CHAR arm while g_battlePhase == 2. Re-issues DAT_0053E984 a BattleUnit_Order at the unit's OWN position with facing = mode + 1, which stores mode in unit +0x09. Formation_ComputeRect (0x0048A1C9) is the only reader of that byte and its whole use of it is `if (field_0x9 == 1) g_formationCols = 2` -- so H is a LINE (the troop's own figures-per-row) and V is a COLUMN (two wide). Settles docs/battle.md section 1's 'unnamed and untraced' for +0x09. Note it does not regroup first, so H after men have died reforms whatever unit the selection last became.

functions.name: Battle_StoreGroup
functions.comment: Ctrl and a digit. Guarded on g_battlePhase == 2 and 0x30 < vkey < 0x3A, so nine slots; copies the live selection bitmap into DAT_00553400 + (vkey - 0x31) * 0x18 and marks the slot used. Battle_Start clears TEN slots. Reached from the window procedure's digit arm when DAT_004DF3A8 (the VK_CONTROL latch) is set.

functions.name: Battle_RecallGroup
functions.comment: A digit with no Ctrl. Copies a stored selection back, regroups it, and then PUTS THE CAMERA ON IT -- the function ends by scanning for the first selected figure and setting DAT_0055CE70 / DAT_005678A0 to its position minus seven. The camera jump is part of the arm, not a convenience.

functions.name: Map_Click
functions.comment: The campaign map's left-click dispatcher, and the only writer of g_screenId = 2 in the whole binary. Map_PickTile then Map_ResolvePick, then: a picked unit of type 1 that is yours opens its orders or siege preparation (screen 0x1D); one of type 3 that is yours opens the merchant (screen 0x08); otherwise the tile's own flags decide - g_pickedTileFlags bit 0x80 toggles the industry the building belongs to (Industry_ToggleFromMap), bit 0x40 opens the VILLAGE (screen 0x02), bit 0x20 opens screen 0x04. A county that is not yours gets Msg_Enqueue group 0x70 instead. The village branch centres the map on the county's town tile (+0x70) and runs one Map_DrawFrame before setting the screen - which is only worth doing because the map stays visible behind the village. docs/decisions.md C22.

functions.name: Industry_ToggleFromMap
functions.comment: Clicking an industry building on the campaign map switches that industry on or off: it XORs the enable byte at +0x297 + industry*0x18 - the byte Labour_Allocate gates each mining job on - and maps the industry to its labour slot (0 wood -> 6, 1 iron -> 4, 2 weapons -> 7, 3 stone -> 5). Argument 4 is castle building instead, and toggles +0x1B0. Map_Click picks the argument from a ladder on g_pickedTileGraphic: 0..3 iron, 4..6 stone, 7..9 weapons, 10..12 wood, 13..20 nothing, 21+ castle. [V] The last statement is Msg_Enqueue with id 0xE6 + industry*2 + on, and L2.eng groups 228..237 are ten consecutive ONE-STRING groups that land in exactly that order: 230/231 Forestry, 232/233 Mining, 234/235 Blacksmith, 236/237 Quarrying - which confirms the industry numbering 0 wood, 1 iron, 2 weapons, 3 stone independently of the labour ladder. The castle arm does not use industry*2 at all; it writes -2 or -1 by hand, landing on 228 Building off and 229 Building on. A player described this mechanic unprompted the day it was found - 'you can click on the forest or mine on the main map to turn them off for that county. Forestry off. Forestry On.' - and the shipped Readme.txt describes it a third time. See docs/kingdom.md 7.4.1.

functions.name: Net_Fail
functions.comment: Logs "ERR:Network:" followed by the caller's own message, shuts the transport down with Net_Shutdown(1) and posts WM_CLOSE to the game window. The single exit for an unrecoverable transport error.

functions.name: Net_OnSessionEvent
functions.comment: [V] The nine session events, named by their own log lines: 0 connect, 1 add player, 2 delete player, 3 session lost, 4 host, 5 add player to group, 6 delete player from group, 7 set player or group data, 8 set player or group name - the DirectPlay system-message set, spelled "OK :DP netsys - ...". Only 2 and 4 do anything: a departing player is removed from the realm table and, once fewer than two realms remain, the game leaves the session and returns to the setup screen; 4 marks the session started.

functions.name: Net_ApplyPacket
functions.comment: [V] The receive half of Net_SendCommand. Validates a packet in g_netRecvPacket: byte 0 is the opcode, byte 1 the payload length checked against g_netCmdLength, byte 2 an 8-bit checksum recomputed over the packet, byte 3 the sequence number in its low six bits and a resend flag in the top two. Then it points g_netReadCursor at the payload and calls g_netCmdHandlers[opcode]. Its four rejections are logged verbatim: "ERR:Corrupt packet from ", "ERR:Resend Forced from ", "ERR:Bad packet CRC from ", "ERR:Wrong size packet from ".

functions.name: Net_SendCommand
functions.comment: The multiplayer command sender, and the reason every campaign action in the binary is written twice - once as a direct call and once as Net_SendCommand(op, 0) under g_multiplayer. Looks the opcode up in g_netCmdLength (0xFF is not a command and errors), calls g_netCmdWriters[op] to serialise the payload, stamps opcode, length, checksum and a sequence number that wraps 1..39 into the matching 0x104-byte slot of g_netSendRing, and sends the packet once for eleven listed opcodes and three times - with flag bits 0x40 then 0x80 - for all the others. Two invariants close: all 112 entries of g_netCmdWriters are real function starts, and opcode 0x29's writer emits 1+4+1+2+2 bytes, exactly the 10 g_netCmdLength records for it. The campaign-map opcodes are 0x29 move order, 0x2C move-and-combine, 0x2E disband, 0x34 garrison, 0x35 begin siege, 0x3A toggle industry from the map.

functions.name: Sync_Rollback
functions.comment: Multiplayer divergence recovery, promoted from hypotheses.json where it was Battle_ReplayFrame with the caveat 'whether it is a replay, a demo loop or a network resync was NOT established'. [V] It is the network resync: FUN_00440666 calls it on the branch where Sync_BlockAgrees(0) reports a divergence, and Sync_ResendState calls it after pushing the whole snapshot. It restores the last agreed snapshot - g_battleMen, g_missiles, g_battleUnits and both PRNG states - bumps the 'divergances' counter the shipped debug overlay draws, and after four consecutive failures reloads lastturn.sva/.svb and posts L2.eng group 259, 'Com-link error.' See docs/formats/eng.md 5.2.

functions.name: Sync_ResendState
functions.comment: The full-state resync L2.eng group 14 index 16 calls 'The master machine will resync the game.' [V] Sends the current snapshot as 400 net commands of 200 bytes - 80,000 bytes - then calls Sync_Rollback.

functions.name: Sync_CompareState
functions.comment: Multiplayer desync detector: walks three of the g_syncBlocks descriptors and reports the first record and byte that differ between the two state snapshots.

functions.name: Sync_Checksum
functions.comment: Sums the same descriptor-selected bytes into a per-frame checksum for the network layer.

functions.name: Sync_RecordDigest
functions.signature: uchar Sync_RecordDigest(void * base, int size, int skip)
functions.comment: The multiplayer state checksum's kernel: an 8-bit truncating sum of every byte of one record from offset `skip` to `size`. [V] Its six (size, skip) call sites - (0x300,5) counties, (0x160,6) realms, (0x1A4,0) units, (0x1B0,0x12) battle men, (0x4C,4) missiles, (0x34,0) battle units - are byte-for-byte the six descriptors in g_syncBlocks (0x004D5B10) read out of the exe. So the original's digest is a whole-record hash minus a fixed prefix, not a field list; see docs/formats/eng.md 5.2 and correction C30.

functions.name: Net_WriteField
functions.comment: Appends len bytes to the command packet being built. Its reader twin is Net_ReadField, and the two come as matched pairs: the writer for opcode N is g_netCmdWriters[N] and its reader is the next function in address order, ending where g_netCmdWriters[N+1] begins. That pairing plus the length table is what makes a command's payload readable without running anything.

functions.name: Net_ReadField
functions.comment: Reads len bytes back out of a received command packet. See Net_WriteField.

functions.name: Sync_BuildDigest
functions.comment: Fills the local player's 10-byte g_syncDigest record: byte 1 counties, 2 realms, 3 units in the campaign phase; 5 battle men, 6 missiles, 7 battle units in battle; byte 0 the sum of bytes 1..8 and byte 9 a (tick & 0x7F) + 1 frame tag. [V] L2.eng group 14 indices 2..9 name those eight slots COUNTY PLAYER PIECE 'CTY MAP' FIGURE ARROW 'AI GROUP' 'BAT MAP', and the two slots this function never writes - 4 and 8 - are exactly the two the strings call maps. Its last statement before the total overwrites byte 7 with the constant 1, so the battle-unit block's divergences are silenced in the shipped build.

functions.name: Sync_DrawRecordDigests
functions.comment: Debug overlay: per-record Sync_RecordDigest values for 16 counties, 5 realms and 24 units, using the inline literals "cty ", "plyr " and "pce ". [V] It is the shipped replacement for L2.eng group 14's COUNTY/PLAYER/PIECE labels, which is why nothing in the binary draws that group. Gated on DAT_0056D690 and a non-zero divergence timestamp.

functions.name: Sync_BlockAgrees
functions.comment: Compares byte `block` of g_syncDigest across every live human realm. [V] Returns 2 - wait, not divergence - unless every peer's byte 9 frame tag is equal and non-zero; 0 and sets a per-block flag in the ten-entry array at 0x0053F090 on a mismatch; 1 on agreement. The flag array is one entry per L2.eng group 14 block name.

functions.name: NetCmd_WriteMoveOrder
functions.comment: g_netCmdWriters[0x29]: g_localPlayer (1), a 4-byte value from FUN_00446E21, g_selectedUnit (1), g_moveTargetX (2), g_moveTargetY (2) - ten bytes, matching g_netCmdLength[0x29] exactly. Its reader at 0x00443A2D deserialises the same five fields in the same order and both then call the command journal at 0x00447136 with sub-opcode 0x0C. This is the whole payload of a campaign move order, and therefore the whole input a lockstep peer needs to reproduce one.

functions.name: Net_DiploPost
functions.comment: Network command handler - it has no callers in the decompilation, so it is dispatched from a command table. Calls Diplo_Post from the arguments the net layer unpacked; FUN_00448339 is the gold-transfer half.

functions.name: Season_Advance
functions.comment: The end-of-season pipeline. Rolls g_seasonPrev/g_season/g_seasonNext and the year (when the season that ended was 4 = Winter), bumps g_turnCount, then calls 28 subsystem passes in a fixed order. This is the whole kingdom economy for one turn.

functions.name: Panels_RefreshAll
functions.comment: End of the season pipeline: Ration_Apply, the next-season preview and Tax_RecomputePreview for every county. This is the second Ration_Apply call docs/decisions.md C20 identified from the save.

functions.name: County_RefreshEstimates
functions.comment: The seven estimate passes that fill every labour record's floor and ceiling: crowding, Field_ReclaimEstimate, Grain_LabourEstimate, Herd_LabourEstimate, four Industry_LabourEstimate calls and Castle_BuildEstimate.

functions.name: Realm_SnapshotLedger
functions.comment: Season pass 2. For each realm copies gold to +0x11C, the weapon total +0x138 to +0x13C, iron to +0x124, stone to +0x12C and wood to +0x134, then calls Realm_RecountWeapons - which immediately recomputes +0x138. The whole 0x118..0x13C region is a {value, value-as-of-this-snapshot} interleave, which is how every ledger panel draws a change. [V] The order of the two writes to the weapon pair is what the England turn-one fixture settles: all five realms carry +0x13C = 0 and +0x138 = 150. That is only reachable if the shadow is taken before the recount and this was the first season the pass ever ran; had the calls been the other way round both would read 150.

functions.name: Realm_RecountWeapons
functions.comment: realm +0x138 = sum of the six weapon stocks at +0x140. [V] The fixture's five realms each hold weapons {0,0,50,50,50,0} and +0x138 = 150. It is a maintained total, not a display cache: Merchant_Trade and the weapons branch of Industry_Produce both call it after moving a stock.

functions.name: Event_RollAll
functions.comment: Draws a random-event id from g_eventTable for each human-owned county after year 1268 and dispatches one of 24 handlers (0x87..0x8E, 0x12E..0x13D) that write the modifiers at county +0x1FB..+0x1FD or move happiness/health directly.

functions.name: Event_ClearCountyModifiers
functions.comment: Season pass 25: clears eventPopulationPct, eventGrainPct, eventHerdPct and taxSuppressed in every county. A random event's swing therefore lasts exactly one season, and it is cleared after Population_UpdateAll has read it and before Event_RollAll deals the next one - which is why taxSuppressed's gate looked unfindable: nothing sets it except an event, and nothing clears it except this.

functions.name: Weather_UpdateAll
functions.comment: Dryness (+0x21D) += seasonal delta (Spring +8, Summer +24, Autumn +12, Winter -12) minus rand/8, doubled for one random county and half again for its neighbours; banded into +0x21B: <5 Flooding, <20 Storms, <70 Cloudy, <95 Sunny, else Drought, with Drought becoming Frost in Winter and Spring. Forced to Cloudy when Advanced Farming is off.

functions.name: Population_UpdateAll
functions.comment: births = Pct(pop, Pct(g_birthRateLadder(pop), happinessFactor)); deaths = Pct(pop, g_deathRateByHealth[band] + g_deathRateBySeason[season]); pop += births - deaths - emigrants + immigrants. Reproduces the shipped lastturn.sav exactly.

functions.name: Migration_UpdateAll
functions.comment: Emigration to the happiest adjacent county: pct = Pct(dHappiness, (100 - happiness)/3), movers = min(100, Pct(pop, pct)), halved for unowned counties. Fills county +0x3C/+0x40/+0x58 and the 16-byte source list at +0x48.

functions.name: Unrest_UpdateAll
functions.comment: Counts county +0x20 up while happiness is low and down while it recovers; at 4 it calls FUN_004AC185, which raises the revolting-peasant army. Human-owned counties get warning messages 0x96..0x99 as the counter climbs.

functions.name: Realm_SecedeIsolatedCounties
functions.comment: Season pass 10, and a whole mechanic that was not written down anywhere: Territory_BuildBlocks then Territory_SecedeMinorBlocks. A realm keeps only its largest contiguous block of counties by population; every county in any other block declares independence that season. [V] The two messages the pass sends name it exactly - L2.eng group 127 "Deeming itself too far from the heart of your empire, this county has declared independence and thrown out your officials." for one county and group 128 "Your lands divide." for several. See docs/kingdom.md.

functions.name: Territory_SecedeMinorBlocks
functions.comment: For each realm 1..5 with a non-zero strength, finds its most populous block in g_territoryBlocks and calls County_MakeIndependent on every county in each of its other blocks. Ties go to the HIGHEST block index: the comparison is `best <= block.population` and the scan runs upward, so an equal population overwrites the incumbent. (This comment said 'lowest' - the operator was read correctly and the conclusion drawn backwards; docs/decisions.md C34.) Only the local player is told, and only when the realm held more than one block: message 0x7F when exactly one county went, 0x80 when more. An AI loses its outlying counties in silence. Reproduced in l2-kingdom::territory.

functions.name: Territory_BuildBlocks
functions.comment: Partitions every owned county into contiguous same-owner blocks in g_territoryBlocks. Clears the 17 slots, then loops - at most 100 times - trying Territory_ExtendBlock on each unassigned county and, if no block could be extended in a whole sweep, opening a new one with Territory_NewBlock. Finally sums each block's member populations into its +0x00, which is the key Territory_SecedeMinorBlocks ranks on. The 100-iteration cap is a real bound, not a loop guard: it is compared against the count of counties already placed.

functions.name: Territory_NewBlock
functions.comment: Opens the first free slot in g_territoryBlocks with this county's owner and the county as its only member. Always returns 1; it does not bounds-check the 17th slot, which cannot be reached because there are at most 16 counties.

functions.name: Territory_ExtendBlock
functions.comment: Adds county to the first block of the same owner that already holds one of its neighbours (County_IsNeighbour), and returns 1; returns 0 if no block will take it. It never merges two blocks that this county would join, so a shape whose parts are discovered in the wrong order stays split for that sweep - which is exactly why Territory_BuildBlocks sweeps repeatedly instead of once.

functions.name: Territory_BlockContains
functions.comment: 1 if this county is already a member of some block of its own owner. Scans until the first block slot with owner 0, so the block list is dense and zero-terminated.

functions.name: Tax_CollectAll
functions.comment: Per county: rate = 320 + castle bonus (480/560/640/720/800 for castle types 1..5, i.e. +50/75/100/125/150%); take = Pct(Pct(population, rate), taxRate); credited to the owner realm's gold. Also writes the tax happiness delta 5 - taxRate + realm[+0x28] into county +0x0E.

functions.name: Tax_RecomputePreview
functions.comment: Recomputes one county's tax display: +0xC0 taxShown from population, the castle multiplier and the rate; +0x0F = 5 - rate; and +0x16 from g_taxHappinessOther[rate]. It is the only writer of +0x16 anywhere in the binary, so the empire tax happiness term is a table lookup rather than 5 - rate.

functions.name: Tax_SumEmpireHappiness
functions.comment: realm[+0x28] = sum over the realm's counties of county +0x16 - the "Other counties" term of the tax happiness effect (L2.eng group 86 index 4). Sums signed bytes into a signed byte, so a large empire can overflow.

functions.name: Happiness_UpdateAll
functions.comment: happiness(+0x0C) = last(+0x0D) + tax(+0x0E) + health(+0x10) + ration(+0x11), copied to the display fields +0x12..+0x14, clamped 0..100, accumulated into +0x1C and averaged into +0x18. Unowned counties below 75 get a flat +5 recorded as "From events". [V] It is also THE RESETTER OF +0x219, the ale allowance, which it zeroes beside shownAle in the same run of display-field clears - so Ale_Apply's cap of five is per season and per county, not for the life of the game as four documents said. docs/decisions.md C53.

functions.name: Health_UpdateAll
functions.comment: health meter (+0x0B) += g_healthDeltaTable[rationLevel][healthBand], clamped 0..100; band (+0x09) = Table_Lookup(meter, g_healthBandLadder); happiness contribution (+0x10) = g_healthHappiness[band].

functions.name: Ration_ApplyAll
functions.comment: Season pass 6, the pass that actually spends the food: Ration_Apply(county, g_seasonPrev) for every county, then copies grainEaten (+0x178) into +0x18C and herdEaten (+0x17C) into +0x190. Panels_RefreshAll runs Ration_Apply again with g_season at the tail of the same pipeline, so +0x178/+0x17C end the turn holding next season's forecast while +0x18C/+0x190 hold what was eaten. [V] In the fixture every unowned county has herdEaten 13 against a shadow of 0, so the shadow cannot be a copy of the surviving call's result - which is docs/decisions.md C20 seen from the writing side.

functions.name: Fields_SeasonTick
functions.comment: Season pass 12: Fertility_Update, Field_ReclaimTick and Field_ReclaimEstimate for every county, in that order. docs/rules.md counted fertility and reclamation as two passes; they are one function and reclamation's next-season estimate is refreshed inside it.

functions.name: Fertility_Update
functions.comment: county +0x208 += 6 * fallowFields(+0x1FF) - 3 * grainFields(+0x201), clamped to -100..100, forced to 0 when Advanced Farming is off. One fallow field per two grain fields is exactly break-even; cattle fields do not enter it.

functions.name: Field_ReclaimTick
functions.comment: SPENDS labour record 2's worker count as a budget, one unit of progress a worker. Starts at Field_ReclaimLeadSlot's field - the most advanced one under reclamation - walks the twenty slots wrapping, gives each at most 200 (the manual's "never more than a quarter of a field in a single season"), refunds any overshoot past 800 to the budget, repaints the tile at each quarter, and returns the moment the budget runs out. So a county with NOBODY on reclamation reclaims nothing, 200 workers is one field a season, and a field finished with labour to spare hands the remainder to the next field in the rota. The stored progress is not clamped to 800; the overshoot is written back and is inert because the tile is already fallow. Reproduced in l2-kingdom::land::reclaim_fields.

functions.name: Field_ReclaimEstimate
functions.comment: The same walk without committing: fills +0xE4 (work remaining) and +0x214 (seasons to the next completed field) for the county panel.

functions.name: Field_ReclaimLeadSlot
functions.comment: Writes county +0x210: the field slot, among those whose terrain is reclamation (> 0x18), with the HIGHEST progress - ties to the lowest slot. The gang finishes the nearly-done field before starting the next. Leaves 0 when nothing is being reclaimed. FUN_0044C5FC at 0x0044C5FC is the same three lines with 99 as its no-work value instead, which is what Field_ReclaimEstimate tests to decide whether there is any work at all; Field_ReclaimTick calls both and the second overwrites the first.

functions.name: Field_ReclaimLeadSlotOr99
functions.comment: Field_ReclaimLeadSlot with 99 rather than 0 as the value written to +0x210 when no field is under reclamation. Field_ReclaimEstimate's `if (+0x210 < 99)` is the only reader that cares.

functions.name: Field_OrderReclamation
functions.comment: Orders want of a county twenty field tiles put under reclamation: walks them in slot order, paints terrain 0x19 on a wasteland tile (terrain 0) and skips a tile already in use. [V] A tile already reclaiming (terrain >= 0x19) is NOT repainted but still spends a place in the quota - the goto skips the decrement for an in-use field and falls through to it for a reclaiming one - so a county told to add one while one is already under way adds nothing. This is what the AI field ladder in Ai_ManageCountyFarms and AI_ManageFields actually calls.

functions.name: Grain_SeasonTick
functions.comment: The grain cycle. Entering Spring it sows (Grain_Sow, store -= seed); entering Summer and Autumn it grows; entering Winter it harvests into the store. Weather scales each stage. Also applies the rats/surplus random-event modifier at +0x1FC.

functions.name: Grain_Sow
functions.signature: int Grain_Sow(int county, int labour, int grainStore)
functions.comment: Largest sacksPerField in 10..1 such that grainFields*sacks fits both the grain store and the available labour (g_grainYieldPerSack * sown / labourDivisor). Sets county +0x1A7 when it had to fall back to a single field.

functions.name: Grain_Grow
functions.signature: int Grain_Grow(int county, int labour, int crop)
functions.comment: Mid-season crop step, entering Summer and Autumn: crop = FertilityBonus(min(GrainFieldShare(crop), labour * perWorker)), clamped at 0. perWorker is 10 with Advanced Farming (0x00553538) and g_grainLabourDivisor's 2 without - the SAME global Grain_Sow uses as a divisor, used here as a multiplier. The labour cap is the reason the grain labour ceiling exists at all: a county that puts nobody on the fields grows nothing whatever it sowed. Reproduced in l2-kingdom::land::grow_step.

functions.name: Grain_Harvest
functions.signature: int Grain_Harvest(int county, int labour, int crop)
functions.comment: Harvest step, entering Winter: min(max(GrainFieldShare(crop), 0), labour * perWorker), and with Advanced Farming on the labour is HALVED first. perWorker is 3 with it on (0x00553218) and 2 without. No fertility here - it was spent at the two Grain_Grow steps. Reproduced in l2-kingdom::land::harvest_step.

functions.name: Grain_FieldShare
functions.comment: First line of both Grain_Grow and Grain_Harvest. If the county now has FEWER grain fields than it sowed (+0x202), scales the crop by Pct(crop, PctOf(fieldsGrain, fieldsGrainSown)); otherwise returns it unchanged. So ploughing a wheat field under in midsummer costs a share of the year's crop, and painting new grain buys nothing until the next sowing.

functions.name: Grain_FertilityBonus
functions.comment: crop + Pct(crop, fertility / 2). The whole of fertility's effect on grain, applied by Grain_Grow only - twice a year - and AFTER the labour cap, so it multiplies what the farmhands could tend rather than what the field could have grown. The -100..100 scalar is therefore worth -50%..+50% a step and a perfectly fertile county reaps 2.25 times a neutral one. The decompiler shows an if whose two arms are identical; that is a signed divide, not a rule.

functions.name: Grain_LabourEstimate
functions.comment: Walks workers = 0..population calling Grain_Sow / Grain_Grow / Grain_Harvest, and stores the first count that reaches the best result in both the wanted floor (+0xC8) and the useful ceiling (+0xCC) of labour record 0. Also fills the grain panel's forecast fields.

functions.name: Herd_SeasonTick
functions.comment: Herd (+0x250) growth: births/deaths from Herd_BirthsAndDeaths, plus Pct(herd, g_herdWeatherPct[weather]) and the disease/wolves random-event modifier at +0x1FD.

functions.name: Herd_UpdateCrowding
functions.comment: Sets county +0x25C from herd / fieldsCattle, banded at 11/21/31 into 10/20/30/40, with no pasture forced to 40. L2.eng group 77 slots 8-11 name the four bands: Low herd crowding, Average herd crowding, Herd overcrowded, Massive overcrowding. The same bands pick a map graphic 0x13..0x16, so crowding is visible on the field art. docs/kingdom.md 13.1.

functions.name: Herd_BirthsAndDeaths
functions.signature: void Herd_BirthsAndDeaths(int county, int herd, int labour, int crowding, int season)
functions.comment: Calf births and cow deaths. Staffing is PctOf(labour, herd * 3) capped at 200, so three labourers a head is full tending, and below 100 the term goes negative and cattle die. The labour argument comes from county +0xD0, inside the +0xC4 job records. Crowding (+0x25C, from Herd_UpdateCrowding) selects 1/3/5/7 from the values 10/20/30/40. The branch above all of it tests fieldsCattle (+0x200): with no pasture the county loses half its herd, or all of it below six head. Found because a player said cattle need tending. docs/kingdom.md 13.

functions.name: Herd_LabourEstimate
functions.comment: Walks workers = 0..population through Herd_BirthsAndDeaths. Writes the first staffing at which births less deaths stops being negative - or the least-bad one if it never does - to the cattle record's wanted floor (+0xD4), and the staffing that maximises it to the useful ceiling (+0xD8).

functions.name: Ration_Apply
functions.comment: Picks the highest affordable ration level 0..5 (None/Quarter/Half/Normal/Double/Triple) by descending from the wanted level, requirement = DivCeil(pop, g_rationTable[l].div) * g_rationTable[l].mul plus garrisons when Armies Eat is on; spends dairy first, then splits the rest between livestock and grain by county +0x15F; writes the ration happiness delta 3*level - 8 to +0x11.

functions.name: Food_FromDairy
functions.comment: herd * g_dairyPerHead (5). The standing herd feeds five people per head per season without being slaughtered.

functions.name: Food_HeadsForPeople
functions.comment: DivCeil(people, g_foodPerHead) - one slaughtered animal feeds ten people.

functions.name: Food_SacksForPeople
functions.comment: DivCeil(people, g_foodPerSack) - one sack of grain feeds six people.

functions.name: Food_Available
functions.comment: herd*5 + slaughterable*10 + grain*6, the county's total feeding capacity this season.

functions.name: Industry_ProduceAll
functions.comment: Season passes 14-17, the whole of industry. Snapshots every realm's iron, stone and wood into +0x124/+0x12C/+0x134, then makes weapons in a complete pass over all counties (record 2, labour slot 7 - the blacksmith) before a second pass mines iron (1, slot 4), quarries stone (3, slot 5) and cuts wood (0, slot 6). Each Industry_Produce is followed by Industry_UpdateSiteTile and a fresh Industry_LabourEstimate, and each record's +0x0E is left holding the worker count that produced it. [V] So the shadow at +0x134 is not last season's wood, it is wood immediately before this season's forestry - and in the fixture realm.wood minus +0x134 equals the sum over that realm's counties of industry[0] +0x10 minus +0x14, exactly, for all five realms (0, 66, 66, 132, 166). That confirms the snapshot point, the +0x10/+0x14 running-total pair, and the record-to-labour-slot mapping in one arithmetic identity. Weapons really are made before the ore is mined.

functions.name: Industry_Produce
functions.signature: void Industry_Produce(int county, int commodity, int job, int baseEfficiency, int divisor)
functions.comment: One industry pass. output = min(resourceLimit, Pct(workers / divisor, efficiency)); commodity 0 wood (job 7, divisor 1, base efficiency 20), 1 iron (job 5, divisor 1, 15), 2 weapons (job 8, divisor 4, 15), 3 stone (job 6, divisor 2, 15). Weapons debit g_weaponCost from the realm's wood and iron.

functions.name: Industry_UpdateSiteTile
functions.comment: Repaints an industry's map tile after it has produced. If the site exists (+0x05) and is not disabled (+0x06) it writes g_tiles[tile] = base + (running flag +0x07 != 0), where base is 1 iron, 4 stone, 7 weapons, 10 wood - so an idle mine and a working mine are two adjacent graphics. When this season's output (+0x10 minus +0x14) is not positive it also writes the attribute plane at g_tiles+3, which is how an exhausted or unstaffed site is drawn differently again.

functions.name: Industry_ResourceLimit
functions.signature: int Industry_ResourceLimit(int county, int industry, uint realm, int useShadow)
functions.comment: The resourceLimit term of Industry_Produce and Industry_LabourEstimate. For wood, iron and stone it is a flag test rather than a quantity - enabled (+0x297) and has-resource (+0x295) and not counting down a disablement (+0x296) gives a literal 999, anything else 0. For weapons it is a real quantity: min over wood and iron of (stock * cost / share) / cost, where share is Industry_WeaponShares and stock is the realm's own wood/iron when useShadow is 0 and realm +0x134/+0x124 when it is not. Reproduced in l2-kingdom::industry::resource_limit.

functions.name: Industry_WeaponShares
functions.comment: Writes the two denominators Industry_ResourceLimit divides the weapons stockpile by: 0x0057C904 = the sum of g_weaponCost[weaponType].wood and 0x0056D628 = the sum of its .iron, over every county of this realm whose blacksmith is switched ON and STAFFED (labour[7].workers > 0), each clamped to at least 1. They are summed COSTS, not a count of counties - so two smithies forging different weapons split the stockpile in proportion to what each weapon costs, an idle smithy takes no share at all, and a realm with one smithy divides by that weapon's own cost, making its limit exactly the number of weapons the stockpile can pay for. This answers a [D] that l2-kingdom::industry carried; it is now l2-kingdom::industry::weapon_shares.

functions.name: Industry_EfficiencyRamp
functions.signature: int Industry_EfficiencyRamp(int county, int industry, int workers, int baseEfficiency)
functions.comment: This season's efficiency for one industry. A flat 80 with Advanced Farming off; 0 with no workers; otherwise lastEfficiency (+0x29C + industry*0x18) plus the base, where the base is first scaled by PctOf(capacity, workers) if the workers exceed the capacity (+0x29E), capped at 100 and floored at the unscaled base. Reproduced in l2-kingdom::industry::efficiency_ramp.

functions.name: Industry_LabourEstimate
functions.signature: void Industry_LabourEstimate(int county, int industry, int slot, int baseEfficiency, int divisor)
functions.comment: Fills one industry's labour record: wanted floor -1 always, useful ceiling 0 when the county is UNOWNED or the resource limit is 0 or popBand is 0, the output-maximising worker count for weapons, and 100,000 - effectively unbounded - for iron, stone and wood. The weapons search steps by popBand, one peasant icon, not by one person. Called four times from FUN_004485A5 as (1,4,15,1) (3,5,15,2) (0,6,20,1) (2,7,15,4), which is the same job-and-divisor mapping l2-kingdom::tables holds. The owner test is why the shipped save's owned counties are full of foresters and its neutral ones full of idlers. Reproduced in l2-kingdom::industry::labour_estimate.

functions.name: Labour_AllocateAll
functions.comment: Labour_Allocate for counties 1..g_countyCount. Season_Advance calls it twice: after Castle_BuildTick and before Migration_UpdateAll, and again after FUN_00448D16 before Panels_RefreshAll.

functions.name: Labour_Allocate
functions.comment: The labour allocator, and the only writer of the nine job records. Splits the population into a farm half and an industry half by county +0x08, gives each job Pct(half, +0x130 + job*4) people or as many as its useful ceiling (+0xC4 + job*12 + 8) allows, walks the leftovers round the jobs with room - grain twice and cattle three times before reclamation once; wood, stone, iron and blacksmith once each before castle building - and drops the remainder into Idle townsfolk. Reproduced in l2-kingdom::labour; all fourteen counties of lastturn.sav come back exactly.

functions.name: Labour_RecomputeIndustryShare
functions.comment: Rewrites county +0x08 from what was actually assigned: PctOf(pop - grain - cattle - reclamation - idle + idle/2, pop). Half the idle count is treated as industry.

functions.name: Labour_RecomputeShares
functions.comment: Rewrites the eight percentages at +0x130 + job*4 from the worker counts, in two groups - jobs 0..2 and jobs 3..7 - each renormalised to exactly 100 by giving the rounding remainder to the group's largest share. Its two indexed loops are what fix the array layout.

functions.name: Labour_ToggleIndustryShare
functions.signature: void Labour_ToggleIndustryShare(int county, int share, int on)
functions.comment: The five-member twin of Labour_ToggleShare, over labourShare[3..7] - castle, iron, stone, wood, blacksmith - with no divisor and its residue defaulting to share 6, wood. [V] The two functions are what settle which index is which job, because each ends by forcing its own group to sum to 100: this one computes 100 minus shares 6, 5, 4, 7 and 3, and Labour_ToggleShare computes 100 minus shares 0, 1 and 2. The groups are therefore {0,1,2} and {3,4,5,6,7} exactly, and the England turn-one fixture then reads them off - every county carries farm {33, 50, 17} and every unowned county carries industry {0,0,0,100,0} with all its spare people idle, which is the wood share pointing at a job whose ceiling is 0. So labourShare is grain, cattle, reclamation, castle, iron, stone, wood, blacksmith, and it is Idle Townsfolk that has no entry - docs/records.json says grain has none, and that is the wrong end.

functions.name: Labour_ToggleShare
functions.signature: void Labour_ToggleShare(int county, int share, int on, int divisor)
functions.comment: Switches one of the three farm labour shares at county +0x130 in or out and renormalises the group to 100. Turning one on gives it g_shareTable[n] / divisor, where n is how many of the three are currently non-zero, and scales the others by 100 minus that; turning it off scales the survivors up by 100 / (100 - its share). Either way the rounding residue is dropped on whichever of the three is largest, defaulting to share 1. Its only caller is Field_SetType, which passes share 2 - field reclamation - and turns it on exactly when county +0x204 is non-zero, so painting a field is what puts reclamation into the labour split. [V] Established by the field-brush work; restated here because the name was living in Rust doc comments and docs/kingdom.md only. The five-member industry twin is Labour_ToggleIndustryShare.

functions.name: Castle_BuildTick
functions.comment: Season pass 3.4, over every county. castleDegraded == 0 just refreshes the estimate; otherwise, for an owned county: Castle_DeliverMaterials, then percent = 100 - Pct(workLeft, workTotal), and if Castle_MaterialsPercent > 99 spend min(labour[3], workLeft) off +0x1CC and recompute - clamping the percentage to 99 whenever work remains, so rounding can never finish a castle. Above 99 it zeroes +0x1E4..+0x1F1, raises Castle_RaiseFreeGarrison into Army_GarrisonApply unless castleDegraded == 2 or castleBuilding >= castleType, sends message 0xA3 (variant 1 for a repair, L2.eng 163/7), clears castleDegraded and switches the castle job share off. It does NOT promote castleType - Castle_Order already did. Ends with Castle_StampTile(county, castleType - 1) and Castle_BuildEstimate.

functions.name: Castle_DeliverMaterials
functions.comment: The season's cart of wood and stone, called first thing in Castle_BuildTick's degraded branch. Takes as much of county +0x1D4 (wood owed) and +0x1D0 (stone owed) out of the realm's stores as they hold and leaves the remainder owing. THE MATERIALS ARE DRAWN DOWN OVER SEASONS, NOT PAID UP FRONT - Castle_Order takes only what the realm had at the moment of the order.

functions.name: Castle_BuildEstimate
functions.comment: Fills the castle panel: work left (+0xF0) and seasons remaining (+0x1A6) from the outstanding work and the labour assigned.

functions.name: Castle_MaterialsPercent
functions.comment: min(100 - Pct(woodOwed, woodTotal), 100 - Pct(stoneOwed, stoneTotal)), or 0 when castleDegraded is 0. The gate on all castle work: Castle_BuildTick spends no labour and Castle_BuildEstimate gives a ceiling of 0 until this is above 99. It is whole-percent integer arithmetic, so a build a fraction of a percent short of its bill reads as fully delivered.

functions.name: County_RecountMerchants
functions.comment: Season pass 22. Zeroes +0x15C, +0x1A4 and +0x1A5 in every county, then walks all 150 unit slots and, for each merchant (kind 3), bumps that county's merchant count +0x1A4 and its lifetime visit counter +0x1A0 and stores the unit index in +0x1A5. +0x1A0 is deliberately not cleared. [V] Four fixtures agree: the counties with +0x1A4 non-zero are exactly the counties holding kind-3 units, +0x1A5 holds distinct unit indices, and +0x1A4 reaches 2 where two merchants share a county. And across three successive turns of one saved game +0x1A0 rises by exactly that turn's +0x1A4 (county 3: 3 -> 5 -> 6 against counts 1, 2, 1).

functions.name: County_Reset
functions.comment: Sets every county up for a new game: population 150, popBand, ration 3, split 100, dryness 0x32, industry share 25, then Labour_DefaultShares, clears all nine labour records to {0,0,0}, and runs the estimates and Labour_Allocate. CORRECTED: this said "tax 50" and it writes NO TAX RATE AT ALL - the 0x32 is dryness, read one line off. A new game therefore opens at ZERO tax in every county: the record was zeroed wholesale by FUN_0046EA28 in Game_NewGame preamble and nothing else puts a rate there, and the England turn-one fixture own bytes agree - taxRate is 0 in all fourteen counties. See decisions.md C62.

functions.name: Labour_DefaultShares
functions.comment: Farm 33/50/17 and all of the industry share on wood. Both halves sum to 100, which is the invariant that identifies the array.

functions.name: Labour_DefaultSharesBuilt
functions.comment: The same farm 33/50/17, with industry 40/15/15/15/15 - castle building favoured. Also sums to 100 in both halves. [V] It is the AI setter: all five of the farming styles call this one and none calls Labour_DefaultShares at 0x004514F8.

functions.name: Village_RebuildIcons
functions.comment: Rebuilds g_peasantIcons for one county: workers divided by popBand icons per cluster, with the surplus or shortfall against the slot's +0x04 and +0x08 drawn in a different frame.

functions.name: Job_SlotForCluster
