functions.comment: Cluster to labour slot through g_jobClusterToSlot, with cluster 0 overridden from stone (5) to iron (4) when the county has industry 1's resource and not industry 3's. That single case pins industry 1 = iron and industry 3 = stone.

functions.name: Village_ClusterHasJob
functions.comment: Whether a cluster has a job to open. Only cluster 0 can say no, and only when the county has neither industry 3's stone nor industry 1's ore.

functions.name: Village_FillCluster
functions.signature: void Village_FillCluster(int county, int cluster, int normal, int other)
functions.comment: Turns one cluster's two icon counts into g_peasantIcons values. `other` is negative for a shortfall against the job's wanted floor and positive for a surplus past its useful ceiling; cluster 6, Idle townsfolk, is always drawn in the surplus icon.

functions.name: Minimap_ComputeBands
functions.comment: Recomputes the three minimap overlay ratings for every county, and Minimap_DrawOverlay calls it first on every draw. It is the ONLY writer of county +0x01, +0x02 and +0x03 - three of the five bytes Sync_CompareState skips, which is what they are: interface state, not simulation. +0x03 labour: 0 if job 0 or 1 is below its wanted floor, else 6 if idle townsfolk plus over-staffed jobs is zero, else 5. +0x02 food: 0 if rationAchieved < rationWanted, else 6. +0x01 happiness: happiness / 20, so 0..5. TWO OF THE THREE MODES ROUTINELY PRODUCE 6, which is off the end of the six-entry g_minimapRatingRamp and colours nothing - so the shipped food overlay is a single red mark on counties that went short and nothing else, and the labour overlay paints only the ramp's two ends. That is not a misreading: a second food branch spreading rationAchieved over bands 1..5 sits behind DAT_00553E60, a debug flag zeroed at 0x00497500 and toggled only in the window procedure at 0x004B29BE. Found by scanning the binary for divide-by-20 sites; there are exactly two. docs/decisions.md C59.

functions.name: Gfx_Repaint
functions.comment: Gfx_MarkAllDirty then Gfx_Present(1) - mark the whole screen and present it now, ignoring the frame budget. The one-line answer to "get what we have drawn onto the glass", used by WM_PAINT, by the full-screen toggle and by the modal dialogs.

functions.name: Gfx_ForceFullRedraw
functions.comment: Marks the whole screen dirty and sets five separate 'redraw everything' latches, g_redrawRequest among them. Called when a game starts (Setup_StartGame) and from the two multiplayer game-start paths.

functions.name: Map_SetZoom
functions.comment: The only writer of the campaign map geometry. Sets ten globals per zoom: g_mapZoom, g_mapScrollStep 1/2/4, g_mapViewCols 8/17/40, g_mapViewRows 30/64/128, g_mapViewX 0/4/0, g_mapViewY 9/17/21, g_mapTilePitch 60/28/12, g_mapHalfPitch and g_mapTileHalfStep 30/14/6, g_mapRowStep 15/7/3; then derives g_mapViewRight = pitch*cols + viewX (480 at all three) and g_mapViewBottom = (rows+1)*rowStep + viewY (474/472/408). Case 1 is unreachable: nothing in the binary ever passes 1, and g_mapZoom has no other writer than 0.

functions.name: Gfx_Present
functions.comment: [V] THE FRAME LIMITER, and it caps the game at 20 frames a second. Adds Frame_Tick's elapsed milliseconds to g_presentBudgetMs, forces it to 0x32 when force is set or a widget asked for it, and presents only once the budget passes 0x31 - fifty milliseconds. The present itself is IDirectDrawSurface::Blt of the back buffer to the primary when windowed and BltFast when full-screen; then g_dirtyCount is decremented and, at zero, the dirty box is reset to its empty sentinel. Skipped entirely while a Smacker movie is up. Sixteen callers, every one a screen painter.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkDirty
functions.signature: void Gfx_MarkDirty(int left, int top, int right, int bottom)
functions.comment: [V] Grows the dirty box to cover a rectangle and raises g_dirtyCount to at least 1. THE BOX IS WRITE-ONLY: g_dirtyLeft/Top/Right/Bottom are referenced by five sites each in the whole decompiled corpus and all five are in this function and Gfx_Present's reset - nothing ever reads them to build a blit rectangle, so the accumulation is vestigial and only the counter has an effect. It also carries a copy-paste defect that the vestigiality hides: the bottom clamp tests against 0x27F, the RIGHT edge's bound, and assigns 0x1DF. docs/bugs.md BNEW-dirtybox. Fourteen wrappers call it; they are the only entry points.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkRightHalfDirty
functions.comment: Gfx_MarkDirty(0x140, 0, 0x27F, 0x1DF) - columns 320..639, the county strip's half of the screen. Its only caller is CountyStrip_Draw.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkAllDirty
functions.comment: Gfx_MarkDirty(0, 0, 0x27F, 0x1DF) - the whole 640x480 frame. EIGHTY-FIVE callers, which is nearly every screen painter in the binary: a screen that repaints itself marks everything dirty rather than tracking what it touched.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkNothing1
functions.comment: An empty function in the dirty-rect family, called once from Battle_Frame. Two more like it sit at 0x0045276A and 0x0045280B. All three compile to a bare return, so whatever they marked was removed; they are kept named so a reader does not go looking.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkTile32
functions.comment: Marks a 32x32 box at 16-pixel cell (tx, ty), clamping negatives to zero. One of seven cell-indexed wrappers whose only difference is the box size: 0x20 here, 0x30 at 0x00452489, 0x40 at 0x004524DC and 0x0045252F, 0x50 at 0x00452582 and 0x00452660, 0x60 at 0x004525D5, 0xC8 by 0xA0 at 0x004526B3.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkTile48
functions.comment: 48x48 at 16-pixel cell (tx, ty). See Gfx_MarkTile32.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkTile64
functions.comment: 64x64 at 16-pixel cell (tx, ty). Its only caller is Map_DrawArmies. See Gfx_MarkTile32.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkTile64Alt
functions.comment: Byte-for-byte the same as Gfx_MarkTile64 and NO CALLERS. Duplicate-and-edit is how this family was written and four of the eight are dead.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkTile80
functions.comment: 80x80 at 16-pixel cell (tx, ty). No callers.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkTile96
functions.comment: 96x96 at 16-pixel cell (tx, ty). No callers.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkTileWide
functions.comment: 80 wide by 48 high at 16-pixel cell (tx, ty) - the isometric map tile's own footprint, which is why Map_DrawTile calls this one when it clears a tile's redraw bit.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkTile80Alt
functions.comment: The same box as Gfx_MarkTile80. No callers.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkPanel
functions.comment: 200 wide by 160 high at 16-pixel cell (tx, ty) - the largest of the family and the only non-square one besides Gfx_MarkTileWide. No callers.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkMapViewDirty
functions.comment: Gfx_MarkDirty(0, 0x18, 0x1DE, 0x1DF) and sets g_mapRedraw - rows 24..479, columns 0..478: the campaign map viewport below the menu bar and left of the county strip. That rectangle is the map view's extent, stated by the engine rather than measured off a screenshot.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkMapViewTwice
functions.comment: As Gfx_MarkMapViewDirty but forces g_dirtyCount to 2, so the change is pushed on two consecutive presents. No callers.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkNothing2
functions.comment: Empty; see Gfx_MarkNothing1.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkWidgetUrgent
functions.signature: void Gfx_MarkWidgetUrgent(int x, int y, int wCells, int hCells, int level)
functions.comment: Sets g_presentNow and falls through to Gfx_MarkSpriteDirty. g_presentNow makes Gfx_Present skip the fifty-millisecond budget on the next call, so this is the 'this widget must appear immediately' path - Widget_Draw and the two button painters at 0x0040D6AD and 0x0040D7B8 are its only callers.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkSpriteDirty
functions.signature: void Gfx_MarkSpriteDirty(int x, int y, int wCells, int hCells, int level)
functions.comment: Marks a box at pixel (x, y) whose size is given in 16-pixel CELLS, and raises g_dirtyCount to 2 when level is above 1. Sixty-seven callers - the general 'I drew a sprite here' call, as against Gfx_MarkAllDirty's 'I repainted the screen'.

functions.name: Gfx_MarkNothing3
functions.comment: Empty; see Gfx_MarkNothing1.

functions.name: Units_Tick
functions.comment: Per-frame unit driver: walks slots 1..150 of g_units and dispatches each through g_unitTickTable[type]. Type 0 or above 5 clears the record. Slot 5 of that table is NULL while the dispatcher accepts type 5, so a type-5 unit would call address 0; nothing spawns one.

functions.name: Units_ResetMoves
functions.comment: Start of season: clears moveState (+0x14C) and movesUsed (+0x153) on all 150 unit slots. Called from turn phase 7.

functions.name: Unit_TickNone
functions.comment: g_unitTickTable[0]: an eleven-byte function that returns. Dead - Units_Tick sends kind 0 to the record-clearer before it indexes the table, so slot 0 is never called. Named so the table reads as six entries of which two (0 and 5) are inert, rather than as a gap.

functions.name: Army_Tick
functions.comment: The type-1 (army) tick. Writes moveAllowance (+0x154) = 15 unconditionally, picks the sprite bank by men (<301 -> 0x48, <601 -> 0x60, else 0x78) plus 3*facing plus the walk frame, calls Unit_EnterCounty when the tile county differs from +0x10, and steps the mover.

functions.name: PeasantMob_Tick
functions.comment: g_unitTickTable[2], the revolting-peasant tick, and the answer to which of the four unit types a given sweep serves. moveAllowance 10 (not the army's 15), sprite base -0x70 = 0x90 with the army's three-frame walk table, county recount on a border crossing, then FUN_004ABD0F and Unit_Step. It opens with `if (menTotal < 0x1E) destroy` - and that is the ONLY `menTotal < 0x1E` in the whole corpus, so the 'below 30 men it is destroyed on the map' rule in docs/armies.md section 0 belongs to peasant mobs, not to armies. Army_Tick has no such test, and L2.eng 148, which that row cites, only says 'impractical to create an army of less than 50 men'.

functions.name: Merchant_Tick
functions.comment: g_unitTickTable[3]. moveAllowance 10, county byte assigned from the tile with no border event at all - a merchant crossing a frontier greets nobody and triggers no recount - then the cooldown decrement and Unit_Step. Its sprite is facing*6 plus g_merchantWalkFrames[walkPhase], a SIX-frame cycle over eight facings rather than the army's three, and the arithmetic closes at 47. Verified on the battle fixtures three for three: merchants at facing 6, 6 and 2 carry spriteFrame 42, 42 and 18, and ((facing+1)&7)*6 gives exactly those.

functions.name: Transport_Tick
functions.comment: g_unitTickTable[4], and it is Merchant_Tick again - same 319 bytes, same body, statement for statement. A transport ticks exactly like a merchant; the two types differ only in what the arrival handlers do with them. Worth naming separately because the duplication is the finding: a reimplementation that shares one tick between types 3 and 4 is faithful, and one that invents a difference is not.

functions.name: Unit_EnterOccupiedTile
functions.comment: Resolves what happens when the moving unit enters a tile already holding one. Returns immediately for types 3 and 4, so merchants and transports are never attacked; an enemy transport is captured instead.

functions.name: Unit_Step
functions.comment: Walks one unit along its stored path. Stops when movesUsed reaches moveAllowance. Dispatches Transport_Deliver, Unit_TrampleTile and Unit_BurnDwelling from Unit_TryEnterTile's return code.

functions.name: Unit_StepOnce
functions.comment: One animation tick of a move: accumulates +0x149 to 16, then calls Unit_NeighbourTile and charges movesUsed +1 on a road (+0x14D set) or +3 otherwise.

functions.name: Unit_CrossField
functions.comment: A step onto a farm field: charges 3 extra moves and, when the tile's county is not the unit's own, worsens diplomacy by 10 (human owners only) and calls County_DestroyField. Total cost 6, which is what g_moveCost holds for a field.

functions.name: Unit_NeighbourTile
functions.comment: Maps a direction 0..7 to the neighbouring tile offset with edge-of-map guards and hands it to Unit_TryEnterTile.

functions.name: Unit_TryEnterTile
functions.comment: Classifies the target tile and returns a code: occupied -> Unit_EnterOccupiedTile; road (plane0 0x01) -> 3; county town (0x40) -> 5; castle (0x80) -> 6; dwelling plot (0x10) -> 7; farm field (0x20) -> 8; otherwise 1. The 0x40 and 0x80 labels were swapped here until decisions.md C25; the codes themselves are unchanged. The entry guard that clears bit 0x80 when the terrain is 0x14 is County_FindCastleTile's stamp, which is how a built castle stops blocking its owner.

functions.name: Unit_MoveInFacing
functions.comment: Commits one step of g_movingUnit in the facing it has already been given: erases the sprite, plays the per-kind movement sound (army 0x0C, mob 5, merchant/transport 0x0B), adds the eight compass deltas to x, y and tileOffset (+-1 tile, +-8 and +-0x200 bytes of g_tiles), redraws, then sets onRoad from bit 0x01 of the tile's plane-0 flag byte. Unit_StepOnce is the caller: it charges the move (3 off-road, 1 on-road), writes facing, and calls this. [D] - the check that could have failed is that all eight cases are exactly the eight compass deltas and that tileOffset stays (y*64+x)*8 in every one of them; a case that disagreed would have shown up as a ninth delta.

functions.name: Map_FindFreeTileNear
functions.comment: For r = 1..5, Map_FindFreeRoadTileNear(x, y, r + 1) then Map_FindFreeOpenTileNear(x, y, r) - so at every radius a road one ring wider beats open ground one ring narrower. Leaves the answer in g_foundTileX / g_foundTileY and returns the radius, or 0. Its one caller is Army_Split.

functions.name: Map_InitScenario
functions.comment: Whole map bring-up for scenario g_scenarioIndex: Map_LoadPlanes, Map_LoadLattice, Minimap_Load, Map_PlaceStartingFields, then Merchant_PickStartCounties.

functions.name: Map_LoadPlanes
functions.comment: Reads the six 64x64 byte planes of a map slot, at slot offsets +0x0000 ... +0x5000, in a 64x64 nest (y outer, x inner). Tracks the highest county id below 0x11 into g_countyCount, and dispatches plane 4 to Merchant_RouteAppend for a plane-0 bit 0x40 tile (the county town) or PlayerStart_Record for a bit 0x80 tile (the castle). This description previously had the two the other way round; see decisions.md C25. Under the corrected reading a merchant route is a list of market towns and a player start is a castle, which is what both are. See docs/formats/maps.md.

functions.name: Map_LoadLattice
functions.comment: Reads the trailing 65x129 layer - for(row < 0x81) for(col < 0x41) - storing byte + 0x0FFF0000 into a dword array of row stride 0x104.

functions.name: Map_PlaceStartingFields
functions.comment: Gives every farm tile its starting crop. Sweeps the 64x64 grid and, for each tile with a county in 1..17 and plane0 bit 0x20 set, counts it into county +0x205 and writes g_tiles[t].content and .frame by DIFFICULTY and by the tile's ordinal within its county: easiest, first 8 pasture (content 0x14, frame base 104) then fallow (content 1, base 84); difficulty 1, 6 pasture then 2 fallow then wild (content 0, base 80); difficulty 2, 4 then 2 then wild; hardest, 4 pasture then wild. The frame is base + ((stored frame + 0xB0) & 3), a four-variant pick, and the three bases are the crop states maps-layers.md 2.4 reads bit 0x20 as farmland from. It was called Map_PlaceDwellings: it places no dwelling, and the four dwelling plots per county are County_FindDwellingPlots and County_UpdateDwellings. See decisions.md C29.

functions.name: County_BuildNeighbours
functions.comment: Builds every county zero-terminated adjacency list at county +0x5C and its count at +0x5B, once, from Map_InitScenario. Sweeps the 64x64 grid y outer x inner and, for each tile of a county in 1..17, appends each of its four 4-adjacent tiles other county to the list if it is not already there, stopping at sixteen entries. [V] The order is the scan order and not a sort, which matters because the list is walked by index in half a dozen places. Reproduced in l2_scenario::newgame::adjacency, whose output equals the England turn-one save stored lists for all fourteen counties - two files authored separately.

functions.name: County_IsNeighbour
functions.comment: Walks county +0x5C, the zero-terminated adjacency list, and returns 1 if other is in it. The loop reads up to 16 entries, one more than the u8[15] docs/records.json declares; the extra read only happens if all fifteen slots are non-zero, which needs a county with fifteen neighbours. [V] The list read this way is exactly symmetric across all fourteen counties of the England turn-one fixture - 39 undirected edges, no half-edges.

functions.name: County_BordersRealm
functions.comment: Walks the county zero-terminated 16-slot adjacency list at +0x5C and returns 1 if any neighbour is owned by that realm. It is the adjacency gate on every county the AI picks for its main army, which is why an AI attack always lands next to its own territory - and why a raid, whose chooser skips this test, need not.

functions.name: County_FindTownTile
functions.comment: Scans the 64x64 grid for this county's tiles with plane-0 bit **0x40** and no terrain yet, takes the 2x2 group, and leaves its x/y in DAT_0057C8D0 / DAT_0056846C. The result becomes the county anchor that County_FindFreeRoadTile searches around. Bit 0x40 is the county town: TileInfo_Draw prints L2.eng group 30 string 7 'County town.' for it, and the mercenary offer at county +0x1AD is advertised on it. See decisions.md C25.

functions.name: County_FindCastleTile
functions.comment: As County_FindTownTile but for plane-0 bit **0x80**, and it also stamps terrain 0x14 on the 2x2 it finds, saving the previous terrain frame to tile +6. Its result is county +0x74/+0x75, which is exactly the tile FUN_004A79A3 moves a garrisoning army onto - so bit 0x80 is the castle. Unit_TryEnterTile's special case for a 0x80 tile whose terrain is 0x14 is this stamp. See decisions.md C25.

functions.name: Castle_StampTile
functions.comment: Draws the castle onto the map, and the frame comes from the castle's STATE: castleDegraded == 0 -> level*4 + 0x50 (finished), else +0x1C4 < 0x32 -> level*4 + 0x28 (scaffolding), else level*4 + 0x3C (half built). content = 0x15 + level. Map_StampBlock(frame, 2, county.castleTile, 0x10, content), so bank bits 0x10 = bank index 4 = Castle1a.pl8 / Castle2a.pl8 - a seasonal bank, a..d, swapped whole by Gfx_LoadCountyMode. Called by Castle_Order and by Castle_BuildTick every season, which is why a castle changes picture as it goes up. This is the only writer of a castle's artwork: L2_maps.dat holds plain ground on the plot. Promotes hypotheses.json H6 - the content ladder is read from the writer, not from two saves.

functions.name: Castle_ClearTile
functions.comment: The inverse of Castle_StampTile over the same 2x2: restore each tile's frame from its saved frame at +6, clear bank bits 0x1C, re-set bit 8 when plane-0 bit 2 is set, and write content 0x14 - the bare plot.

functions.name: Castle_EvictTile
functions.comment: Called by Castle_Order right after Castle_StampTile: walks the castle's 2x2 and, for any unit standing on it, calls Unit_UnlinkFromTile and sets unit +0x14E. Ordering a castle turns its plot into an obstacle at once, so whatever was standing there is pushed out of the tile chain.

functions.name: County_UpdateDwellings
functions.comment: Raises or clears a dwelling on each of the four plots County_FindDwellingPlots found. Population_UpdateAll calls it once per county per season with wanted banded on population: 0 below 601, 1 below 1001, 2 below 1401, 3 below 1601, else 4. Each of the first `wanted` plots steps g_tiles[t].content one size up the ladder 0x13 -> 0x12 -> 0x11 -> 0x10 (frame 0x3C for the two small sizes, 0x3B for the two large), sets the bank to Town (0x0C) with bit 0x80 and sets flags bit 0x10; each plot beyond `wanted` is razed - frame restored from savedFrame, bank cleared back to base, flags bit 0x10 cleared, content 0. This answers maps-layers.md 8's open question about the four 0x10 plots. [V] - the razing branch reads savedFrame, the byte maps-layers.md 5.3 predicted exists for exactly this and for nothing else; had +0x80 not been the plot list it would restore an unrelated tile's terrain. Unit_BurnDwelling is the inverse: it drives 0x10 back to 0x13 on one plot.

functions.name: Unit_ReachCastleBuilding
functions.comment: Unit_Step's code-6 branch for terrain 0x15..0x19, a built castle on a plane-0 bit 0x80 tile. Armies only: the county is yours -> Army_Garrison, otherwise -> Army_BeginSiege. Two unrelated functions agree on the test, which is what makes this [V] rather than [D] - Map_HoverUnitTarget collects the same tile as a garrison target when the county owner matches the unit's and as a siege target when it does not, using bit 0x80 and terrain above 0x14. The stepper additionally caps at below 0x1A; the hover has no upper bound.

functions.name: Unit_TrampleTile
functions.comment: Damages a crop tile an army passes through in a county it does not own. Begins `if (type != 3 && type != 4)` - merchants and transports do no damage.

functions.name: Unit_BurnDwelling
functions.comment: Burns a dwelling an army passes through in a county it does not own, and cuts that county's population. Same type-3/type-4 exemption.

functions.name: County_FindDwellingPlots
functions.comment: Sweeps the 64x64 grid for this county's tiles with plane-0 bit 0x10 set and records each one's byte offset in county.dwellingPlots, copying g_tiles[t].frame into .savedFrame and zeroing .content. Called once per county from Counties_PlaceSites, immediately after County_FindTownTile. [V] - the check that could have failed is arithmetic: the destination is four i32 slots at county +0x80 with no bound on the counter, and it ends exactly on fieldProgress at +0x90, so a county with five 0x10 tiles would corrupt a field. maps-layers.md 2.3 measured exactly four per county over all 434 counties of the 44 shipped maps.

functions.name: Counties_PlaceSites
functions.comment: Once at map load, for every county 1..g_countyCount: County_FindTownTile into +0x70 and the anchor +0x6C/+0x6D, then County_PlaceResourceSites and County_PlaceBlacksmith, then County_FindCastleTile into +0x78 and the castle tile +0x74/+0x75. The order matters - the resource sites are placed relative to the town, and the castle plot is found afterwards.

functions.name: County_PlaceResourceSites
functions.comment: At load, scans the county for Town-bank tiles (runtime byte +2 masked with 0x1C equals 0x0C) and turns plane-2 descriptor 30, 0 and 20 into the iron, stone and wood industry sites: sets has_resource at +0x295 + c*0x18, stores the tile, and writes terrain 1, 4 and 10. This is where a county's resources come from - the map, not the county record.

functions.name: County_PlaceBlacksmith
functions.comment: Places the weapons industry site (record 2) on the county tile whose flags byte is exactly 0 - not a road, not a field, not a boundary - that is 4-adjacent to one of the county own farm fields and nearest the town anchor, ties going to the first in row-major order. It also ADDS plane-0 bit 0x80 to a tile the file gave no flags at all, which with the razed fields is one of only two places the runtime flags plane is not the file. [V] The blacksmith is derived rather than authored, and this comment used to say that is why every county has one: 433 of 434 do. County 4 of slot 8 (Africa) has no tile with flags == 0 at all - its 57 tiles are all road, boundary, rough, plot, farmland, town or site - so the original local_14 stays 0, its guard refuses, and that county can never make a weapon. Measured over all 44 shipped maps in crates/l2-scenario/tests/newgame.rs. See decisions.md C62.

functions.name: County_EnsurePasture
functions.comment: [I] on the name, [V] on the behaviour. Called from Merchant_Trade's tail only when cattle were BOUGHT: recounts the fields and, if fieldsCattle is 0, turns one field into pasture - a fallow one through FUN_0046958F, or failing that a grain one through FUN_0046965A, which also docks the standing crop by one field's share and steps +0x206 down. Both walk a per-county round-robin cursor at +0x15A bounded by +0x205 and give up after 20 tries. So buying cows into a county with no pasture creates the pasture, at the cost of a grain field if that is all there is. NOT REPRODUCED in crates/l2-kingdom: it needs the tile map, the cursor field and a save entry, and it is a rule of its own rather than part of the transaction.

functions.name: County_RecountFieldsAll
functions.comment: Season pass 11: County_RecountFields for every county. It runs before Fields_SeasonTick, so fertility and reclamation see this season's field mix, and before Grain_SeasonTick, so sowing does.

functions.name: County_RecountFields
functions.comment: Rebuilds the county's five field tallies from the map: walks its 20 slots in g_countyFieldTiles and buckets each tile's graphic byte out of g_tiles - 1 fallow (+0x1FF), 2..14 grain (+0x201), 15..22 pasture (+0x200), 0/23/24 to +0x203 and 25 and above to +0x204. The tallies are a cache; the map is the state. +0x204 is load-bearing: Field_SetType switches the reclamation labour share on exactly when it is non-zero. [V] Recomputed from g_countyFieldTiles and g_tiles in the England turn-one fixture, all five tallies reproduce in all fourteen counties - 168 field tiles - which pins every band boundary. Independently reproduced by the field-brush work on every other reachable save including the four-county battle map. It is also the first call in County_RefreshEstimates, so the herd's crowding estimate always runs against a field count refreshed one call earlier.

functions.name: County_TileIsField
functions.comment: True when the tile terrain is in 2..0x16, the range County_DestroyField will act on.

functions.name: County_DestroyField
functions.comment: Removes one field: a grain field takes crop * (100/fieldsSown) percent off county +0x244 and decrements +0x201; a pasture takes the same fraction off the herd and decrements +0x200. The tile is repainted bare.

functions.name: Minimap_Load
functions.comment: Loads the two 128x128 minimap rasters for map slot 0..59 out of MAPnn.PL8: name = "map01.pl8" + (slot>>2)*0x10, frame (slot&3)*5 -> g_minimapCounty (county id per pixel) and frame (slot&3)*5+1 -> g_minimapPixels (the picture). Each MAPnn.PL8 therefore carries four slots, and the 11 shipped files cover exactly the 44 used slots. It was named Map_LoadTileSets and described as picking a season variant; it does neither - the tile sets are loaded by Gfx_LoadCountyMode and the season is a separate global.

functions.name: Map_StampBlock
functions.signature: void Map_StampBlock(char baseFrame, int size, int tileOffset, byte bankBits, byte content)
functions.comment: Writes an n x n block of tile records. Per tile: bank |= 1, bank &= 0xE3, frame = baseFrame + g_blockQuadrants[i] for the given size (size 1 writes baseFrame flat), bank |= bankBits, content = content. Steps 8 bytes a tile across and (0x40 - size)*8 at the end of a row. The town, the resource sites and the castle all go through it.

functions.name: Map_FindFreeRoadTileNear
functions.signature: undefined4 Map_FindFreeRoadTileNear(int x, int y, int r)
functions.comment: Scans the (2r+1)^2 box around (x, y), clipped to the map, for a tile with no unit on it and plane-0 bit 0x01 (road) set. Returns 1 and leaves the tile in g_foundTileX / g_foundTileY.

functions.name: Map_FindFreeOpenTileNear
functions.signature: undefined4 Map_FindFreeOpenTileNear(int x, int y, int r)
functions.comment: As Map_FindFreeRoadTileNear but accepts plane0 & 0xFD == 0 - plain grass, with or without the county-boundary bit. The fallback when no free road tile exists.

functions.name: County_FindDefendingArmy
functions.comment: The existing-defender search Army_AttackCounty calls before levying one. Scans the 4x4 tile block x in [townX-2, townX+1], y in [townY-2, townY+1] around the county's town anchor (+0x6C/+0x6D), reads the unit index out of the occupancy plane at g_tiles+5, and returns the LARGEST type-1 unit whose owner equals the county's owner - 0 if there is none. The window arithmetic closes exactly: +8 a column, +0x1E0 to the next row = 512 - 4*8. Because the town is a 2x2 whose bottom-right corner is the anchor, the block is the town plus the one-tile ring around it: an army defends its county town by standing on or beside it. Corrects docs/armies.md section 9, which modelled it as 'the lowest-numbered army of the county's owner standing in the county'; both the scope and the tie-break were wrong, and the two readings disagree on battle-before.sav, where county 2's garrison sits at (30,46) and county 2's town is at (31,50).

functions.name: Map_ResolvePick
functions.comment: Turns the picked tile into the four things Map_Click branches on: g_pickedTileCounty from the county plane, g_pickedCountyOwner from that county's +0x05, g_pickedTileFlags from the attribute plane at 0x00522F91, and g_pickedTileGraphic from g_tiles. Then masks off three flag/graphic combinations that would otherwise be hotspots.

functions.name: Terrain_Set
functions.signature: void Terrain_Set(int tileByteOffset, int terrain, char variant)
functions.comment: THE SINGLE WRITER of a tile's content byte, and it picks the tile's picture in the same breath - so this one function is the terrain -> frame mapping a renderer needs. Sixteen call sites: Field_SetType (the brush), Field_ReclaimTick, Field_OrderReclamation, County_DestroyField, Grain_SeasonTick and Herd_UpdateCrowding through FUN_00469D21, Map_PlaceStartingFields, and nine helpers around 0x00469xxx. frame = ((frame - oldBase) & 3) + base + variant*4; bank = (((bank | 1) & 0xE3) | layer) & 0x7F, then |= 0x80 for terrain 0x0F..0x16. Base ladder on the NEW terrain, in the order the code tests it: 0 -> 80 roads, 0x17 -> 130 BASE, 0x18 -> 134 BASE, 1 -> 84, 0x19/0x1A/0x1B/0x1C -> 108/112/116/120, terrain < 0x13 -> 88, everything else -> 104 (a bare else, so 0x1D and up land there too - maps-layers.md 5.5's table reads as if 0x13..0x16 were exhaustive). oldBase is 0x82 when the PREVIOUS terrain was 0x17 or 0x18 and 0 otherwise; every other base is a multiple of 4, so the `& 3` preserves the tile's variant forever and the correction exists only for the two bases that are not. Consequence: the low two bits of a farm tile's frame never change, so the picture is a pure function of the terrain and the frame the map file stored. The third parameter is DEAD - all sixteen call sites pass 0, including both callers of the one function that forwards it. Named here after four documents referred to it only as FUN_0046D7F4; docs/formats/maps-layers.md 5.5 is the write-up and l2_view::campaign::field_graphic is the reimplementation.

functions.name: County_CollectFieldTiles
functions.comment: Fills g_countyFieldTiles - 17 rows of twenty i32 byte offsets - from the map, at the end of Map_InitScenario, and clears the twenty u16 at county +0x90 when the argument is 1. Sweeps tiles in ascending byte-offset order and puts each farmland tile (plane-0 bit 0x20) of a county in 1..17 in that county first free slot. [V] AND THE TWENTY-SLOT TABLE RAZES WHAT WILL NOT FIT: a county twenty-first farm tile takes content 0, frame 6, flags 0 and its bank cleared back to base - it stops being farmland at all, before the first season runs. So twenty fields per county is a fact about the map rather than a cap on a counter. No shipped map exercises the razing branch; crates/l2-scenario/tests/newgame.rs exercises it on a synthetic slot. See decisions.md C62.

functions.name: Unit_Spawn
functions.signature: undefined4 Unit_Spawn(byte type, int x, int y, byte owner)
functions.comment: Allocates the first free slot of the 150-entry unit array g_units (stride 0x1A4) and places it at tile (x, y). Requires the tile to hold no unit and to have plane-0 bits 0xFC clear. Writes the unit index into byte +5 of the runtime tile record and sets bit 0x01 of byte +2. Types seen: 1 = army, 2 = revolting peasants, 3 = merchant, 4 = transport.

functions.name: BattleMan_Create
functions.signature: undefined4 BattleMan_Create(byte troopType, int x0, int dx, int y0, int dy, int owner, short unit)
functions.comment: Allocates the first free slot of the figure array g_battleMen (81 records, slots 1..80 usable) (stride 0x1B0), places it on the battlefield, writes its index into cell byte +5 and links it to its unit. Returns 0 when all 80 slots are in use, which silently truncates the army.

functions.name: Missile_Spawn
functions.signature: undefined4 Missile_Spawn(byte owner, int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: Allocates one of the 100 slots of g_missiles (stride 0x4C) and sets its start and target positions in 1/32-cell units. Used for arrows, bolts, catapult shot, thrown oil, fire and falling figures.

functions.name: BattleUnit_Alloc
functions.comment: Allocates the first free slot of the unit array g_battleUnits (81 records, slots 1..80 usable) (stride 0x34); a slot is free when byte +0 (owner) is zero. Leaves the index in g_lastBattleUnit.

functions.name: BattleMan_Clear
functions.comment: Zeroes one 0x1B0-byte battle figure record.

functions.name: BattleUnit_Clear
functions.comment: Zeroes one 0x34-byte battle unit record.

functions.name: BattleMan_Destroy
functions.comment: Clears the figure off its battlefield cell and zeroes its record.

functions.name: Unit_UnlinkFromTile
functions.comment: Removes a unit from its tile's occupancy chain, walking the +0x04 links with a ten-step guard. Called by Army_GarrisonApply on the way into a castle and by Castle_EvictTile.

functions.name: Unit_LinkToTile
functions.comment: Puts a unit into its tile's occupancy chain (tile +5, chained through unit +0x04). It opens 'if (kind != 1 || garrisonCounty == 0)' and does nothing otherwise, so A GARRISONED ARMY IS NEVER ON ITS TILE. With Army_GarrisonApply's Unit_UnlinkFromTile call that is two functions agreeing, and it is what stops a besieger meeting the garrison as an obstacle and fighting a field battle instead of laying a siege - Unit_TryEnterTile tests occupancy before any tile flag.

functions.name: Missile_ClearCellLists
functions.comment: Sweeps missiles 1..100 and clears both ends of the per-cell missile list - cell byte +6 and the missile's own next link. The loop bound is i < 0x65, the same 100 as Missile_UpdateAll.

functions.name: Missile_LinkToCell
functions.comment: Pushes a missile onto the list of missiles standing on its cell: cell byte +6 is the head, missile +0x04 is the next link, and the walk gives up after ten so a corrupt list cannot hang the frame. Confirms docs/battle.md 3's reading of cell byte +6.

functions.name: BattleMen_ClearAll
functions.comment: Zeroes g_battleMen[1..80]. The loop bound 0x51 is what fixes the figure count at 80.

functions.name: BattleUnits_ClearAll
functions.comment: Zeroes g_battleUnits[1..80].

functions.name: Dir_FromDelta
functions.signature: undefined4 Dir_FromDelta(int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: Eight-way direction from (x,y) to (tx,ty): 0 N, 1 NE, 2 E, 3 SE, 4 S, 5 SW, 6 W, 7 NW, 8 same cell. This is the encoding of the figure facing byte.

functions.name: Dir_FromDeltaOctant
functions.signature: uint Dir_FromDeltaOctant(int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1)
functions.comment: A second direction-from-delta, snapping to the eight compass points by a 3:1 ratio test rather than exactly: a delta within a third of an axis is treated as on that axis. Same numbering as Dir_FromDelta - 0 north, 2 east, 4 south, 6 west - which is a third independent statement of the facing table. Used by BattleMan_StateEngineFire to aim a catapult.

functions.name: Move_ResetSelection
functions.signature: void Move_ResetSelection(int realm, int unit, int x, int y)
functions.comment: Clears the realm's distance field and re-seeds the movement preview at (x, y). The memset length is 0x2000 = 64*64*2, the exact size of g_moveDistLocal and g_moveDistOther as i16[4096], which closes both arithmetically. Also writes the origin pair at 0x00504020/0x00504024 and the flat index y*64+x at 0x004F4070, then clears the local player's path buffer. The unit argument is not used.

functions.name: Move_FloodFill
functions.comment: Fills the campaign distance field (g_moveDistLocal for the local player, g_moveDistOther otherwise) outward from a tile using g_moveCost. Assumed cost-weighted breadth-first; the body was not read.
functions.signature: void Move_FloodFill(int who, int x, int y, int mode)

functions.name: Move_BuildCostMap
functions.comment: Rebuilds the 64x64 i16 campaign movement cost map g_moveCost from the map planes: 1 road, 3 open ground, 6 a standing field, 100 castle/settlement/plot, 0 impassable. Run once a season from turn phase 7.

functions.name: Move_ExtractPath
functions.signature: int Move_ExtractPath(int who, int x, int y)
functions.comment: The campaign path extractor (distinct from the battle's Path_Extract at 0x00472392). Greedy descent down a campaign distance field from (x, y) back to the source, appending (x, y) pairs into g_pathBuf[who] with the count in g_pathLen[who]. On a cost-1 road tile it steps the direction index by 2, orthogonals only, and falls back to all eight when that finds nothing.

functions.name: Path_CopyToUnit
functions.comment: Copies g_pathBuf[slot] into the unit record: length to +0x1C and up to 150 (x, y) pairs to +0x1D. 150 * 2 = 300 bytes, ending exactly at +0x149.

functions.name: Path_ClearBuf
functions.comment: Zeroes one of the shared campaign path buffers and its length.

functions.name: Path_Search
functions.signature: void Path_Search(int mode, int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: The battlefield pathfinder. A uniform-cost breadth-first flood fill over the 80x80 grid with a circular queue: g_pathCost[cell] holds cost+1 from the start, a cell is expanded only after being reached g_pathStepCost[cell] times (that is how terrain cost is charged), and a step is only allowed between cells whose elevation differs by at most 1. Skipped entirely when the target is adjacent or the straight line is clear.

functions.name: Path_LineIsClear
functions.signature: bool Path_LineIsClear(int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: Straight-line passability test; when it succeeds Path_Search does no work at all and the figure walks directly at its target.

functions.name: Path_SearchSiege
functions.signature: void Path_SearchSiege(int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: The variant of Path_Search used by figures in state 9 - the siege/wall path.

functions.name: Path_BuildTerrainTemplate
functions.comment: Rebuilds g_pathBlockedTemplate, the cost field Path_Search copies at the start of every search: 999 for a cell whose flags carry 0x10 or 0x40 and for the one-cell border, 0 everywhere else. It ignores flags 0x80 and 0x20, both of which Cell_TryEnter treats as blocking, so the pathfinder's map is more permissive than the mover's.

functions.name: Path_BuildElevation
functions.comment: Copies cell byte +4 of all 6,400 battlefield cells into g_pathElevation.

functions.name: Path_BuildStepCost
functions.comment: Rebuilds g_pathStepCost, and is the pathfinder's entire cost function. Zero everywhere except: a cell whose flags carry 0x20 or 0x40 costs 100 and lays a gradient of 12, 8, 4, 4 on the cells one to four rows further south (three cells wide in the last two bands); and, when the flag at 0x0057C910 is set, a cell diagonally adjacent to surface 5 costs 4. Battlefield_BuildFromSkr sets neither 0x20 nor 0x40, so on a .skr battlefield every step costs the same.

functions.name: Path_BuildBlockedMap
functions.comment: Refreshes the per-cell blocking map the flood fill reads, from the live figure positions.

functions.name: Path_DetourTooLong
functions.comment: Cancels a move whose route is absurd: true when the path cost to the destination exceeds 20 in a field battle or 150 in a siege and is also more than five times the straight-line Chebyshev distance. It can only ever return true for a figure whose owner is human, so a player's men give up on long detours and the AI's never do.

functions.name: Path_Extract
functions.signature: int Path_Extract(int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: Walks the g_pathCost field downhill from the destination back to the start, writing the route into g_pathWaypoints as (x,y) byte pairs and returning its length. Ties are broken towards the straight-line direction. Returns 0 for no path and 150 for adjacent or over-long.

functions.name: Path_NearestReachedNear
functions.signature: int Path_NearestReachedNear(int x, int y, int tx, int ty)
functions.comment: The salvage step after Path_Extract fails: an expanding-ring search of radius 0..29 around the unreachable destination for the cheapest cell the flood fill actually reached at the destination's elevation, left in g_foundTileX / g_foundTileY. Gives up if the ring reaches the figure's own position.

functions.name: BattleMan_SetPath
functions.comment: Copies `length` waypoints out of g_pathWaypoints into the figure own list at +0x38, sets the count at +0x36 and marks the figure "on route".

functions.name: Msg_Reset
functions.comment: Clears the message ring, its head and tail and the pending flag.

functions.name: Msg_Enqueue
functions.signature: void Msg_Enqueue(int from, int to, int group, int variant, unsigned char category, unsigned char county, unsigned char spare, int payload)
functions.comment: The general notification path, 144 call sites. Builds a 24-byte record at g_messageCompose and copies it into the 50-slot ring g_messageQueue. The group is an L2.eng group id and the variant selects the string within it (drawn as variant + 1, past the group's label at index 0). Enqueues only when the recipient is realm 0 or the local player - the three isHuman branches all compute that same predicate.

functions.name: Msg_EnqueueCurrent
functions.comment: Pushes whatever is already in g_messageCompose onto the ring. The tail half of Msg_Enqueue, reached directly by callers that filled the compose record themselves.

functions.name: Msg_Pump
functions.comment: Pulls one record from g_messageQueueTail, unpacks it into g_messageGroup, g_messageVariant and friends, starts the 2000-tick g_messageTimer and calls Msg_DrawWindow. Runs only on screens 0x00, 0x27, 0x29 and 0x0F with job panel 8.

functions.name: Msg_DrawWindow
functions.comment: Draws the message window. The layout is chosen by the record's category byte; the text is Eng_DrawString(group, 0) for the heading and (group, variant + 1) for the body, and Msg_PlayVoice is called with the same (group, variant). 10,915 bytes, read here only for its text and voice lookups.

functions.name: Msg_DrawDiplomacy
functions.comment: The diplomatic letter window, message category 0x0C, dispatched from Msg_DrawWindow. Draws L2.eng group 109 string 0 'From' plus the sender's name, then switches on g_messageGroup - 0xF5 into eleven arms that land exactly on groups 245..255: 0 'A gift.' with a count, 1 and 2 'A communication' with the free-text body from g_diploLetter + realm*0xCA, 3 'Offer of alliance.', 4 the alliance termination, 5 'Plea for help' and 6 'Launch an attack.' with the county name from group 100, and 7..10 the four 'Reply to request' variants. Arms 3, 5 and 6 are the only ones that call Widget_Draw, and they are exactly the three whose text asks a question - a correspondence that could have failed eleven times and did not.

functions.name: Msg_DrawBeyondLetter
functions.comment: Message category 0x14. Byte-for-byte the layout of Msg_DrawDiplomacy, except that the sender is the literal string "Beyond" instead of g_playerNames[realm], only the free-text arms 1 and 2 (groups 246/247 'A communication') are handled, and no reply widget is drawn - so it is a letter the player cannot answer.

functions.name: Msg_Dismiss
functions.comment: Closes the message window: clears g_messageGroup and the timer, and for groups 0x9E, 0x9F, 0xEE and 0xEF drops into screen 0x26 instead. [V] Its last three lines are the ending: if g_gameOutcome is 10 or 11 it calls Campaign_EnterConquest and sets g_screenId = 0x1C. So a game ends when the message that set the outcome is dismissed, not when the outcome is written.

functions.name: Tip_Update
functions.comment: Per-frame tip-screen driver, gated on g_optTipScreens. [V] Twenty frames after a screen is first opened it calls Tip_Show with the group for that g_screenId, once per game. The screen ids it tests - 0x02 town centre, 0x0F job popup with g_jobPanelJob 8, 0x10 army movement, 0x17 armoury, 0x1B castle building, 0x39 advanced options - agree one for one with the L2.eng labels of the groups it passes.

functions.name: Tip_Show
functions.comment: Shows one first-time tip screen: saves g_screenId, switches to screen 0x27, marks g_tipShown[group] and posts the group with the category from g_tipCategory[group]. [V] Fourteen literal groups reach it - 200, 201, 202, 206..212, 214, 215, 217, 218 - and each is an L2.eng group whose label names the screen it belongs to. See docs/formats/eng.md 5.3.

functions.name: Battle_Start
functions.comment: Brings a battle up: builds the battlefield (Battlefield_BuildRandom, Battlefield_BuildFromSkr or Battlefield_BuildCastle), then Battle_InitArmies, then the first unit/figure update passes. See docs/battle.md.

functions.name: Music_StartBattle
functions.comment: THE BATTLE MUSIC PICKER. Alternates within a pair rather than choosing: a field battle flips g_battleTrackField between battle1 and battle2, a siege flips g_battleTrackSiege between battle3 and battle4, and DAT_0057A0F0 selects battle4/battle5. The counter is stepped BEFORE use from zero, so the first battle of a session plays the second track of its pair. Reached from Opt_ToggleMusic when g_battlePhase is 2. Its opening branch tests whether battle2.wav EXISTS and is dead on a complete install.

functions.name: Battle_CheckOutcome
functions.comment: The per-frame test for whether the battle is over - the half of the battle model that decides anything, and previously in neither symbols.json nor hypotheses.json. A FIELD battle ends exactly two ways: one side's living-men counter (g_battleMenA, g_battleMenB, both drawn on the battle HUD) reaching zero, or g_battleWithdrawal marking a withdrawal, which is tested FIRST and so outranks annihilation. There is no morale break, no rout threshold and no clock. Three further arms are sieges: the escape-tile flag DAT_00553F3C, and with no breach and no engines left either 'assault repulsed, repeat' (breach and approach scores reset to 4 when the castle level is under 3) or the besieger loses. It then raises the outcome screen 0x2B, and once DAT_00568470 counts past 5000 it calls Battle_WriteBackCasualties and Battle_ReturnToCampaign(1).

functions.name: Battle_SelectOutcomeBanner
functions.comment: Chooses which of Screen_BattleOutcome's seven L2.eng group 82 heading/body pairs to draw, from two questions: was it a siege, and is g_localPlayer the winner's owner (g_battleWinnerOwner). Field: 0 won, 1 lost. Siege with the local player winning: 2 if A won (the player besieged and took the castle), 4 if B won (the player held it and the siege was lifted). Siege with the local player losing: 5 if A won (the player's castle fell), 3 if B won (the player was driven off). Each of the four siege arms reads as a different sentence, which is the check on the mapping - A is always the besieger and B always the garrison. Independently confirms that g_battleLoser holds the winner.

functions.name: Siege_RecordCastleDamage
functions.comment: The end-of-siege bookkeeper, called from Battle_ReturnToCampaign's siege arm, and the ONLY writer of county +0x1C3 to 2. Returns unless g_battleIsSiege and one of the two damage accumulators is non-zero. Stores the battle's breach and approach scores into +0x1E4..+0x1F1 (which Castle_BuildTick zeroes on completion), then bills the repair: castleLevel < 2 charges wood +0x1D4/+0x1E0 = wallDamage*10, otherwise stone +0x1D0/+0x1DC = wallDamage*15, and work +0x1CC/+0x1D8 = breachDamage*5 + wallDamage*15 - ADDING to whatever a build already under way had owed. So a wooden castle is repaired in wood and a stone one in stone. Finally +0x1F9 = g_castleLevel, castleDegraded = 2, +0x1C4 = 0.

functions.name: BattleUnits_RegroupSelection
functions.comment: THE REASON SELECTION IS SIMULATION STATE. Counts the selection by troop type into the five panel counters (zeroing all five when more than one kind is present), then asks whether the selection is exactly one whole unit -- the unit of the LOWEST-numbered selected figure. If it is not, BattleUnit_Alloc claims a slot and every selected figure is moved into it, so a box drawn round half a unit SPLITS that unit and every later order applies to the new one. Two details worth keeping: the new unit's category is written INSIDE the move loop, so the LAST selected figure decides whether the whole unit is missile (1) or melee (3); and when BattleUnit_Alloc finds no free slot the whole regroup silently does nothing, at which point FUN_00478F0B truncates the selection instead. Sets DAT_0053E984, the unit a player's orders go to.

functions.name: BattleMen_NarrowSelectionToOneUnit
functions.comment: Finds the first selected figure and deselects everything not in its unit. Runs immediately after BattleUnits_RegroupSelection on the committing path, where it is normally a no-op because the regroup has just put every selected figure in one unit; it earns its place when BattleUnit_Alloc had no slot left. A selection that cannot be split is truncated instead.

functions.name: BattleMen_ClearSelection
functions.comment: Sweeps figures 1..80 and clears selected wherever it equals this player, leaving another player selection alone, then clears the five selected-siege-engine counters. The tail of every other selection verb.

functions.name: BattleMen_SelectInBox
functions.signature: void BattleMen_SelectInBox(uint player, int camX, int camY, int ax, int ay, int bx, int by)
functions.comment: Normalises the two corners, converts them to cells with a quarter-tile tolerance (FUN_004BC2E5 / FUN_004BC3AC round the near corner up past three quarters, FUN_004BC346 / FUN_004BC40D round the far corner down inside a quarter), and walks the closed rectangle. Each cell's OCCUPANT -- battlefield byte +5, not any sprite the box overlaps -- gets selectedSeen set, and gets selected = player if this player owns it. So a man drawn half inside the box and standing outside is not picked, and one drawn outside and standing inside is.

functions.name: Battle_ClassifyDrag
functions.comment: Which of three things a finished selection drag is. Returns 1 when the pointer has moved 0x19 pixels or more on either axis -- a real box; 2 when it has not and g_battleHoverFriendly or g_battleHoverFriendlyPicked says one of your own men is under it -- a pick; 0 otherwise, which the caller treats as nothing at all. It also writes the four box corners in sixteenths (>> 4) to _DAT_005653F0/EC and _DAT_005656F4/E8 on every call, including the ones that return 0.

functions.name: BattleUnit_Order
functions.signature: void BattleUnit_Order(int unit, int x, int y, int attackTarget, int destIsWoodland, int facing)
functions.comment: Gives a battle unit a destination. Missile units stop short of the target by (range/8 - 3) cells; a unit that mixes missile and melee figures is split into two units. CORRECTED: the fifth parameter was named fromPlayer and is nothing of the kind. Its only writer is Battle_UpdateHover, which sets DAT_0053E874 when the hovered cell's SURFACE BYTE IS 15 and clears it otherwise, and all twenty-five AI call sites pass a literal 0 -- so only a player's click can make it non-zero, and what it selects is the branch that applies Order_StopShortOfTarget and Dest_FindReachableNear to a missile unit of SIDE 0. Why surface 15 specifically is not established. The sixth parameter is not a facing either: it stores facing - 1 in unit +0x09, whose one reader forces the formation to two columns when it is 1, so the H and V keys are line and column. docs/battle.md section 15.

functions.name: Battle_ChargeAll
functions.comment: Every figure of this player whose troopType is under 7 -- so no siege engine and no oil -- gets state 8, free pursuit, and its unit gets halted = 1, which switches the every-500-frame reform off. NOT Order_ChargeNearest (0x0048C8AF), which is the AI's and also clears the withdraw flag and the figures' targets.

functions.name: Battlefield_BuildRandom
functions.comment: The open-field battlefield generator: writes the same cell array and the same deployment slot arrays as Battlefield_BuildFromSkr, but from the campaign map rather than a .skr layer.

functions.name: Battlefield_BuildFromSkr
functions.comment: Loads one 80x80 .skr terrain layer and expands it into the 8-byte-per-cell battlefield, including bridge parts and the two 12-slot deployment marker arrays. See docs/formats/skr.md.

functions.name: Battlefield_BuildCastle
functions.comment: The siege battlefield builder; the third writer of the cell array.

functions.name: Battle_UpdateMissiles
functions.comment: Rebuilds the cell -> figure occupancy map for all 80 figures, then steps every missile.

functions.name: Battle_UpdateHover
functions.comment: Runs once per frame from Battle_Frame and recomputes what the pointer is over on the battlefield: clears the five hover globals, asks FUN_004BC222(g_mouseX, g_mouseY) whether the pointer is inside the battlefield viewport and sets g_battleHoverOnField, converts the pointer to a battlefield cell, counts the local player's selected men into DAT_00565404, reads that cell's surface into g_battleHoverSurface and its occupant figure, and then sorts the occupant into g_battleHoverFriendly, g_battleHoverFriendlyPicked or g_battleHoverEnemy depending on whose it is and whether DAT_00553078 says a selection exists. Those globals are what the battle arm of Battle_Frame's cursor ladder reads - but Battle_UpdateHover runs AFTER the cursor is chosen, so the battle pointer is one frame behind the pointer position, the same off-by-one-frame shape docs/screens-county.md section 2.6 records for Screen_FrameInput.

functions.name: Battle_InitArmies
functions.comment: Chooses the battlefield size class from the two armies, clears the figure and unit arrays, then raises both sides. Also computes each side's autocalc strength as sum(count[t] * g_troopStrengthWeight[t]) over troop types 0..6.

functions.name: Battle_LoadStrengthBands
functions.comment: Loads the three strength-band thresholds for the current battlefield size class from g_strengthBandTable.

functions.name: Battle_WriteBackCasualties
functions.comment: How a fought battle's casualties reach the campaign. Zeroes both army records' +0x168, +0x196 and all eleven +0x16C counts, then walks the 80 figures of g_battleMen and adds each living figure's men into its owner's record - into +0x16C + troopType*2 for a levied figure and into +0x196 for a mercenary one, with +0x168 accumulated alongside. Only troop types 0..6 are counted, so the four battle-only slots are zeroed and never rebuilt: siege engines do not survive a battle. Called immediately before every Battle_ReturnToCampaign(1).

functions.name: Battle_UpdateStrengthAdvantage
functions.comment: Recomputed every 101 frames from Battle_UpdateAllUnits. Sums surviving men over all live figures, weighted 1/2/3/3/2/2/4 by troop type 0..6 and 1 for siege engines, split by figure byte +0x13 (owner is human). Leaves (aiMen * 100 / humanMen) - 100 in g_aiStrengthAdvantage, plus a -10..+21 jitter when g_multiplayer is zero. Every order handler branches on that one number.

functions.name: Battle_RaiseSide
functions.signature: void Battle_RaiseSide(int armyUnit, int outnumbered, int side)
functions.comment: Turns one army record into battle units. Walks the 11 troop types in g_raiseOrder, and for each splits the men into units of at most maxFigures*g_menPerFigure. Siege counts are multiplied by g_menPerFigure so that one engine is one figure. `side` is 4 or 0.

functions.name: Battle_RaiseSideSiege
functions.signature: void Battle_RaiseSideSiege(int armyUnit, int outnumbered, int side)
functions.comment: The castle-defender variant of Battle_RaiseSide: uses g_raiseOrderSiege (8 troop types, no catapult/tower/ram), forces archers and crossbowmen to at most 3 figures per unit, and places units by wall slot rather than by deployment marker.

functions.name: BattleUnit_LoadTroopStats
functions.comment: Copies one row of g_troopBattleStats (0x004D96D0, stride 0x14) into scratch globals, then the matching row of g_missileStats (0x004D97B0) selected by the weapon class in field +0x0C.

functions.name: BattleUnit_Create
functions.signature: void BattleUnit_Create(int siegePlacement, int troopType, int outnumbered, int side, int men, int owner, int mercenary)
functions.comment: Allocates a battle unit and fills it with ceil(men / g_menPerFigure) figures laid out in a rectangle. Sets the unit category from the troop type, and copies the troop and missile stats into every figure.

functions.name: BattleUnit_Classify
functions.comment: Recomputes the unit category from the troop types it still contains: catapult 5, tower 6, ram 7, oil 8, any missile figure 1, otherwise 3. The category selects the order handler.

functions.name: Deploy_SlotForUnit
functions.comment: Picks a deployment cell for the n-th unit of a side from the 12-slot marker array: side 0 uses the 0x04 marker slots at 0x00553150, side 4 the 0x0F marker slots at 0x005531B0. There are only 12 slots, so a side with more than 12 units reads past the end.

functions.name: Deploy_SlotForUnitSiege
functions.comment: The castle-defender placement: maps the troop type to one of the marker slots rather than using the unit ordinal, with a rotating fallback list.

functions.name: Formation_OffsetX
functions.signature: int Formation_OffsetX(int footprint, int rows, int i)
functions.comment: Column offset of figure i in a units rectangle: (i / rows) * footprint.

functions.name: Formation_OffsetY
functions.signature: int Formation_OffsetY(int footprint, int rows, uint i, int side)
functions.comment: Row offset of figure i: (i % rows) * footprint, negated for side 0 so both sides face each other.

functions.name: Formation_PickGeometry
functions.comment: Chooses which of the unit's troop types dictates the formation by taking the highest g_formationTypePriority, then loads that type's cell footprint and figures-per-row out of g_troopBattleStats.

functions.name: BattleMan_RecomputeStrength
functions.comment: Sets the figure strength band 0..3 by comparing its remaining men against g_strengthBand1/2/3 (75%, 50%, ~19-25% of a full figure), then loads its melee attack value from g_meleeAttackTable[troopType][band].

functions.name: Battle_CountMenByType
functions.comment: Census of surviving men. Among figures whose owner is not human it totals all men into g_aiMenTotal, crossbowmen plus archers into g_aiMenMissile and knights into g_aiMenKnight; it also totals each army's men separately. The field and siege handlers read those three to decide when their side has run out of a troop class.

functions.name: Battle_UpdateAllMen
functions.comment: Per-frame sweep over g_battleMen[1..80]. Applies burning damage on surface 10/17, ages the figure, then dispatches g_troopTickTable[troopType] - which reloads the per-troop stats and tail-calls g_manStateTable[state].

functions.name: TroopTick_Peasant
functions.comment: Slot 0 of g_troopTickTable (0x004D9140), so this is the per-frame handler for troop type 0 - peasant. Reloads that type's constants into the figure and tail-calls g_manStateTable[state]. Verified by the constants it writes: recovery 6, heavy blow 0, armour 0, which is that troop's row of docs/battle.md 6.1 - all eleven handlers agree with all eleven rows, and a wrong table order would scatter them. Also bounds state to 0..17 and calls BattleMan_Destroy outside it, which independently fixes g_manStateTable at 18 entries. Also the only writer of the counter at 0x005694FC, which is zeroed elsewhere and drawn by Ui_DrawNumber - a live count of peasant figures, on screen.

functions.name: TroopTick_Crossbowman
functions.comment: Slot 1 of g_troopTickTable (0x004D9140), so this is the per-frame handler for troop type 1 - crossbowman. Reloads that type's constants into the figure and tail-calls g_manStateTable[state]. Verified by the constants it writes: recovery 8, heavy blow 0, armour 12, which is that troop's row of docs/battle.md 6.1 - all eleven handlers agree with all eleven rows, and a wrong table order would scatter them. Also bounds state to 0..17 and calls BattleMan_Destroy outside it, which independently fixes g_manStateTable at 18 entries.

functions.name: TroopTick_Maceman
functions.comment: Slot 2 of g_troopTickTable (0x004D9140), so this is the per-frame handler for troop type 2 - maceman. Reloads that type's constants into the figure and tail-calls g_manStateTable[state]. Verified by the constants it writes: recovery 12, heavy blow 300, armour 12, which is that troop's row of docs/battle.md 6.1 - all eleven handlers agree with all eleven rows, and a wrong table order would scatter them. Also bounds state to 0..17 and calls BattleMan_Destroy outside it, which independently fixes g_manStateTable at 18 entries.

functions.name: TroopTick_Swordsman
functions.comment: Slot 3 of g_troopTickTable (0x004D9140), so this is the per-frame handler for troop type 3 - swordsman. Reloads that type's constants into the figure and tail-calls g_manStateTable[state]. Verified by the constants it writes: recovery 12, heavy blow 100, armour 35, which is that troop's row of docs/battle.md 6.1 - all eleven handlers agree with all eleven rows, and a wrong table order would scatter them. Also bounds state to 0..17 and calls BattleMan_Destroy outside it, which independently fixes g_manStateTable at 18 entries.

functions.name: TroopTick_Pikeman
functions.comment: Slot 4 of g_troopTickTable (0x004D9140), so this is the per-frame handler for troop type 4 - pikeman. Reloads that type's constants into the figure and tail-calls g_manStateTable[state]. Verified by the constants it writes: recovery 30, heavy blow 0, armour 35, which is that troop's row of docs/battle.md 6.1 - all eleven handlers agree with all eleven rows, and a wrong table order would scatter them. Also bounds state to 0..17 and calls BattleMan_Destroy outside it, which independently fixes g_manStateTable at 18 entries.

functions.name: TroopTick_Archer
functions.comment: Slot 5 of g_troopTickTable (0x004D9140), so this is the per-frame handler for troop type 5 - archer. Reloads that type's constants into the figure and tail-calls g_manStateTable[state]. Verified by the constants it writes: recovery 6, heavy blow 0, armour 0, which is that troop's row of docs/battle.md 6.1 - all eleven handlers agree with all eleven rows, and a wrong table order would scatter them. Also bounds state to 0..17 and calls BattleMan_Destroy outside it, which independently fixes g_manStateTable at 18 entries.

functions.name: TroopTick_Knight
functions.comment: Slot 6 of g_troopTickTable (0x004D9140), so this is the per-frame handler for troop type 6 - knight. Reloads that type's constants into the figure and tail-calls g_manStateTable[state]. Verified by the constants it writes: recovery 16, heavy blow 200, armour 25, which is that troop's row of docs/battle.md 6.1 - all eleven handlers agree with all eleven rows, and a wrong table order would scatter them. Also bounds state to 0..17 and calls BattleMan_Destroy outside it, which independently fixes g_manStateTable at 18 entries.

functions.name: TroopTick_Catapult
functions.comment: Slot 7 of g_troopTickTable (0x004D9140), so this is the per-frame handler for troop type 7 - catapult. Reloads that type's constants into the figure and tail-calls g_manStateTable[state]. Verified by the constants it writes: recovery 20, heavy blow 0, armour 33, which is that troop's row of docs/battle.md 6.1 - all eleven handlers agree with all eleven rows, and a wrong table order would scatter them. Also bounds state to 0..17 and calls BattleMan_Destroy outside it, which independently fixes g_manStateTable at 18 entries. Siege engines also force meleeAttack to 0 and animSet to 0.

functions.name: TroopTick_SiegeTower
functions.comment: Slot 8 of g_troopTickTable (0x004D9140), so this is the per-frame handler for troop type 8 - siegetower. Reloads that type's constants into the figure and tail-calls g_manStateTable[state]. Verified by the constants it writes: recovery 15, heavy blow 0, armour 35, which is that troop's row of docs/battle.md 6.1 - all eleven handlers agree with all eleven rows, and a wrong table order would scatter them. Also bounds state to 0..17 and calls BattleMan_Destroy outside it, which independently fixes g_manStateTable at 18 entries.

functions.name: TroopTick_BatteringRam
functions.comment: Slot 9 of g_troopTickTable (0x004D9140), so this is the per-frame handler for troop type 9 - batteringram. Reloads that type's constants into the figure and tail-calls g_manStateTable[state]. Verified by the constants it writes: recovery 30, heavy blow 0, armour 50, which is that troop's row of docs/battle.md 6.1 - all eleven handlers agree with all eleven rows, and a wrong table order would scatter them. Also bounds state to 0..17 and calls BattleMan_Destroy outside it, which independently fixes g_manStateTable at 18 entries.

functions.name: TroopTick_Oil
functions.comment: Slot 10 of g_troopTickTable (0x004D9140), so this is the per-frame handler for troop type 10 - oil. Reloads that type's constants into the figure and tail-calls g_manStateTable[state]. Verified by the constants it writes: recovery 8, heavy blow 0, armour 40 (25 when ownerIsHuman), which is that troop's row of docs/battle.md 6.1 - all eleven handlers agree with all eleven rows, and a wrong table order would scatter them. Also bounds state to 0..17 and calls BattleMan_Destroy outside it, which independently fixes g_manStateTable at 18 entries.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateNone
functions.comment: Slot 0 of g_manStateTable: an empty stub, ret. Nothing writes state = 0 anywhere in the struct-typed corpus - BattleMan_StateMelee drops a figure to state 8 rather than 0 - so slot 0 is the array's zero value and not a state the battle uses.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateDelay
functions.comment: Slot 1 of g_manStateTable: the wait state. Counts `delay` (+0x30) down and, at zero, restores `dly state` (+0x2F) into `state`, clears walking and moveTick, and re-arms stepFlags bit 0. Fires while it waits if the figure has a weapon class and more than 5 ticks left. Verified two ways: the two fields it drives are the debug panel's own labels `delay` and `dly state` (BattleDebug_Panel), and BattleMan_Step is the writer at the other end - on a blocked friendly it saves the current state into dly state, sets state 1, and sets delay to (otherMan & 1) + 1.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateDead
functions.comment: Slot 2 of g_manStateTable. docs/battle.md 2.2 already had state 2 as dead; this is the handler. Steps the collapse animation and counts +0x173 up to 80, then calls BattleMan_Destroy - so a corpse lies on its cell for 80 frames before the slot is freed. Its siege-engine twin is BattleMan_StateEngineDead, which counts to 120.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateWalk
functions.comment: Figure state 3: walk toward tg x / tg y and drop to state 5 (idle) when the mover reports an interruption. The state Formation_SendFigure uses for an ordinary move.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateMelee
functions.comment: Figure state 4. Drops out if the opponent is gone or dead, otherwise runs Melee_Tick.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateIdle
functions.comment: Figure state 5. Advances the animation, and fires if the figure has a missile weapon.

functions.name: BattleMan_FireMissile
functions.comment: Missile reload and fire. Acquires a target 10 ticks before the reload interval expires, then spawns a missile whose power is the figure missile damage scaled by its strength band (full, 4/5, 3/4, 1/2).

functions.name: BattleMan_StateAttackWall
functions.comment: Slot 6 of g_manStateTable, and it is not merely "blocked". A figure enters it from BattleMan_Step when BattleMan_TryStepDir returns 5, which Cell_TryEnter returns for a cell flagged 0x20 against a non-zero side - the castle wall. The handler plays the strike animation, adds 1 per frame to the rampart counter at 0x00554034 when it stands on surface 5 and to the gate counter at 0x00568DA4 otherwise, converts a rampart cell to surface 4 at 5000, breaches at 20000, and returns to `dly state` once Cell_NeighbourHasSurface finds no more wall to the north.

functions.name: BattleMan_LookForMelee
functions.comment: Figure state 7. If an adjacent enemy exists, locks both figures into state 4 facing each other, one as attacker and one as defender; otherwise falls back to idle or missile search.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateChase
functions.comment: Figure state 8: free pursuit. Re-acquires a target with Melee_ChooseChaseTarget whenever it has none or its target is dead, copies the target's position into its own tg x / tg y every tick, and walks. Siege engines are bounced to state 11 instead. This state ignores the unit's destination entirely.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateFillMoat
functions.comment: Slot 9 of g_manStateTable: the moat fill, as docs/battle-ai.md 5 describes it. The only caller of Anim_Dying.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateEngineFire
functions.comment: Slot 12 of g_manStateTable: a catapult aiming and shooting. Seeds the figure's own aim point (+0x28/+0x2A) from the unit's aim point (+0x16/+0x18) when it is still zero - this is the one non-zero writer of that pair that docs/battle.md 2.1 identifies - walks until the aim point is within range >> 3, then counts swingTimer to 100, spawns a missile, steps it eight times on the spot, and wraps the timer at 179.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateRamGate
functions.comment: Slot 14 of g_manStateTable: the siege-engine twin of BattleMan_StateAttackWall, at twenty hits per frame instead of one. Reachable only by a battering ram: BattleMan_TryStepDir sends a siege engine to Cell_TryEnterEngine, whose two leaf tests return 6 - the value BattleMan_Step turns into state 14 - only when troopType == 9. So 1000 frames of ramming breach a gate where a man on foot needs 20000 hits.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateEngineDead
functions.comment: Slot 15 of g_manStateTable: the siege-engine death state. Same shape as BattleMan_StateDead with the wreck lying on its cells for 120 frames rather than 80, and the engine animation instead of the collapse.

functions.name: BattleMan_StateCloseToAttack
functions.comment: Slot 17 of g_manStateTable, the state Formation_SendFigure gives a bow or crossbow figure that has something standing on its destination. The largest state handler in the battle at 2340 bytes; it drives the missile record fields directly.

functions.name: Missile_UpdateAll
functions.comment: Steps g_missiles[1..100].

functions.name: Anim_Strike
functions.comment: Sixteen-byte thunk to Anim_StrikeA2. One of six such thunks at 0x004861E9..0x00486239, each an unconditional `call` to one animation handler; they are the only entry points the state machine uses.

functions.name: Anim_Walk
functions.comment: Sixteen-byte thunk to Anim_WalkA2.

functions.name: Anim_Stand
functions.comment: Sixteen-byte thunk to Anim_StandA2.

functions.name: Anim_Dying
functions.comment: Sixteen-byte thunk to Anim_DyingA2.

functions.name: Anim_Collapse
functions.comment: Sixteen-byte thunk to Anim_CollapseA2.

functions.name: Anim_DrawBow
functions.comment: Sixteen-byte thunk to Anim_DrawBowA2.

functions.name: Anim_StrikeA2
functions.comment: The strike block of an a2 sheet: frame = dirc2 * N + 6 + g_strikeCycle*[animPhase >> 2] while the figure holds the attacker role (+0x185 == 1), else the standing pose N-1. Phase wraps at 0x27. Called from BattleMan_StateMelee and BattleMan_StateAttackWall. Note this is frames 6.. and NOT the walk cycle - docs/battle.md 13.5 had the two blocks the other way round; see 14.3.

functions.name: Anim_StrikeA3
functions.comment: The a3 twin of Anim_StrikeA2: identical code with frames-per-facing 12/13/8/10 replaced by 7/8/5/6, standing pose 11/9/7/9 by 6/5/4/5, two further walk-cycle tables, and horseFrame = dirc rather than dirc * 6. Those six numbers are exactly what the shipped a3 art needs - A3*_swor/mace 69 frames, arch/cros 77, pike 53, psnt 61, all 8*N + 13, and A3_horse.pl8 is 8 frames - so the a2/a3 reading is checked against the art and not only against the code. UNREFERENCED: nothing in the binary calls it, and its address appears in no table. Same for all six a3 handlers.

functions.name: Anim_WalkA2
functions.comment: The walk block of an a2 sheet: frame = dirc * N + (animPhase >> 2), phase wrapping at 0x17, so six poses at one per four ticks. Called at the top of BattleMan_StateWalk and BattleMan_StateChase, and in melee only when the figure actually moved. Frames 0..5 are therefore the walk, which is the opposite of what docs/battle.md 13.5 said.

functions.name: Anim_WalkA3
functions.comment: The a3 twin of Anim_WalkA2: the same code with N 12/13/8/10 -> 7/8/5/6 and the phase wrapping at 0x0B rather than 0x17, so three poses rather than six. Unreferenced.

functions.name: Anim_StandA2
functions.comment: The standing pose of an a2 sheet, and the reader of figure +0x0B/+0x0C: +0x0B counts up each frame and, when it passes +0x0C, resets and turns facingDrawn one step - left on an even map x, right on an odd one. BattleMan_Create seeds +0x0C to ((index*9 + x*16) & 0x3F) + 0xB4, so a standing figure shifts its feet every 180 to 243 frames and no two neighbours do it together. Called by BattleMan_StateIdle, BattleMan_LookForMelee, and by the walk states when the mover reports no progress.

functions.name: Anim_StandA3
functions.comment: The a3 twin of Anim_StandA2, N 12/13/8/10 -> 7/8/5/6. Unreferenced.

functions.name: Anim_DyingA2
functions.comment: The dying block of an a2 sheet: base 8*N + 6 per troop group - 102 macemen and swordsmen, 110 crossbowmen and archers, 70 pikemen, 86 peasants - stepped by animPhase to 0x5F. Its only caller is BattleMan_StateFillMoat.

functions.name: Anim_DyingA3
functions.comment: The a3 twin of Anim_DyingA2, and the arithmetic that pins the whole a2/a3 pairing. Its four bases are 57, 65, 41, 49 = 8*N + 1 for a3's N of 7, 8, 5, 6; the a3 sheets hold 8*N + 13 frames; 13 - 1 = 12 = four half-facings of three dying frames, exactly as in a2. The index space closes with nothing left over for all four troop groups. Unreferenced.

functions.name: Anim_CollapseA2
functions.comment: The six shared frames at 8*N + 0..5 of an a2 sheet - 96, 104, 64, 80 - indexed by the state-2 death timer +0x173 >> 2 and held once it passes 6. Called only by BattleMan_StateDead, so this is a figure falling over; Anim_DyingA2 is the twelve-frame block after it.

functions.name: Anim_CollapseA3
functions.comment: The a3 twin of Anim_CollapseA2: bases 56, 64, 40, 48 = 8*N for a3, and a single frame rather than a six-frame run, which is all a3 has room for. Unreferenced.

functions.name: Anim_DrawBowA2
functions.comment: The bow-draw animation: frame = facing * N + curve[swingTimer clamped to 0x4F] + 10, from the 0x50-byte curves g_drawBowCrossbow (troop 1) and g_drawBowArcher (troop 5). The +10 is where the crossbow and archer sheets have room for it: N is 13, frames 0..5 are the walk, 6..8 the strike and 9 the stand, leaving 10..12. Called by BattleMan_FireMissile and BattleMan_StateCloseToAttack. It is also the only function in the battle that reads g_mapRotation, which is the campaign map's orientation; see docs/battle.md 14.5.

functions.name: Anim_DrawBowA3
functions.comment: The a3 twin of Anim_DrawBowA2: N 13 -> 8, curves g_drawBowCrossbowA3 / g_drawBowArcherA3, base +10 -> +6. Unreferenced.

functions.name: BattleUnits_RebuildFromFigures
functions.comment: Runs while g_battlePhase == 2. Rebuilds every unit's owner, figure count and first/last figure index from the live figure array; ages the unit timers +0x0C (recently hit), +0x0E (order lock), +0x0F (firing) and +0x2D; sets +0x0D when any figure is in melee and +0x11 when any is on the wall; and, when a figure raises its was-hit flag +0x15, records the attacking figure's unit in +0x0A and sets +0x0C to 50. It runs once per frame from Battle_Frame, so that grudge lasts 50 frames against a 200-frame think interval. This is where the AI's memory of who is hitting it comes from.

functions.name: BattleUnit_Recentre
functions.comment: Sets the unit position to the centre of the bounding box of its live figures.

functions.name: Battle_UpdateAllUnits
functions.comment: Per-frame sweep over g_battleUnits[1..80]. Recentres each unit on its figures, and runs its order handler unless byte +1 (human controlled) is set. Three dispatch tables: field, siege attacker, siege defender. Counts field +0x14 down from 500 and re-targets at zero.

functions.name: BattleUnit_NeedsReform
functions.comment: Gate on the every-500-frame reform in Battle_UpdateAllUnits: false for an empty unit, for one whose byte +0x2A (halted) is set, and for a human-controlled unit of fewer than four figures that is not in melee. Its result also picks which slot-assignment pass BattleUnit_Reform runs.

functions.name: BattleUnit_Reform
functions.comment: Re-issues every figure of a unit a destination. If the formation rectangle around the unit's target is clear it assigns rectangle slots directly; if not it searches outward for free ground per figure; a siege tower past a siege-progress threshold sends every figure to the unit target instead. Clears the in-melee flag +0x13 afterwards.

functions.name: Formation_AssignSearchedSlots
functions.comment: Slot assignment for a blocked destination: for each figure, search outward from the unit target for a usable cell, then send the nearest unassigned figure to it. Claimed cells go in a 100-entry list so two figures never get the same one.

functions.name: Formation_AssignRectSlots
functions.comment: Slot assignment for a clear destination: walk the formation rectangle in order and send the nearest unassigned figure to each slot. Greedy nearest-first, so the unit does not fold through itself.

functions.name: Formation_AssignAllToTarget
functions.comment: Slot assignment that sends every figure to the unit's target cell rather than to a rectangle. Used for a siege tower once g_siegeApproachScore passes 6.

functions.name: Formation_NearestFreeFigure
functions.signature: int Formation_NearestFreeFigure(int x, int y, int unit)
functions.comment: The live figure of `unit` nearest (x,y) by Manhattan distance that has not yet been given a slot in this pass, marked by figure byte +0x17C.

functions.name: Formation_SendFigure
functions.signature: void Formation_SendFigure(int x, int y, int man, int unit)
functions.comment: Gives one figure its destination and entry state: 3 walk, 9 fill in the moat when the destination is water, 10 for a siege engine, 17 closing to attack when the figure has a bow or crossbow and something stands on the destination, 12 when a catapult is aimed at low ground. Clears the route and the barred counter if the destination changed.

functions.name: Formation_RectIsClear
