functions.comment: Tests every slot of the unit's formation rectangle for being on the map, at the destination's elevation, free of another unit's figure and not impassable. Also caches the destination cell's occupant, its is-water flag and its elevation in the three globals the slot assignment then reads.

functions.name: Formation_ComputeRect
functions.comment: Works out the unit's formation rectangle - columns, footprint, width, depth - and its top-left origin, centred on the unit target and clamped to the map. Forces the column count to 2 for units whose byte +0x09 is 1.

functions.name: Formation_FindNearbySlot
functions.comment: Expanding-ring search of radius 0..19 around the unit target for a cell Formation_SlotIsUsable accepts and that no figure of this pass has claimed. Short-circuits to the target itself on water, and on surface 4 for a catapult unit.

functions.name: Formation_SlotIsUsable
functions.signature: int Formation_SlotIsUsable(int cellOffset, uint surface, int elevation, int unit)
functions.comment: Whether one cell may serve as a formation slot: rejects an impassable cell that is also empty, accepts one holding an enemy figure, rejects one holding another friendly unit's figure, and in a siege refuses to put a side-0 unit on an empty low-surface cell.

functions.name: Dest_FindReachableNear
functions.signature: undefined4 Dest_FindReachableNear(int fromX, int fromY, int x, int y, int unit)
functions.comment: Expanding-ring search of radius 0..19 around (x,y) for a cell with the same surface type and elevation as the source, leaving it in g_foundTileX / g_foundTileY. Used to fix up a move order that lands on unreachable ground.

functions.name: UnitOrder_None
functions.comment: The empty order handler: an immediate return. Seven of the 25 dispatch-table slots point at it - field category 0, siege-attacker 0 and 8, siege-defender 0, 5, 6 and 7 - so a unit of one of those categories never acts on its own. See docs/battle-ai.md.

functions.name: UnitOrder_FieldMissile
functions.comment: Field battle, unit category 1 (archers, crossbowmen). Thinks once per 200 frames and not at all while any of its figures is in melee. Above the aggression threshold it shoots the nearest enemy unit if it was hit in the last 50 frames, otherwise advances halfway, holds, and advances again on an `orders` schedule. Below it, it shoots its attacker, answers a rally request, or sits on rally waypoint 0 every fourth think - and once it has been hit more than ten times it backs two cells away from its attacker.

functions.name: UnitOrder_FieldFoot
functions.comment: Field battle, unit category 2 (peasants, pikemen). Above the aggression threshold it marches to the enemy end of the field for ten thinks then charges. Below it, being attacked either raises g_aiCommitCounter (by 3 when the side is over its engagement budget, by 20 when missile troops fall under an eighth of the army) or makes the unit back away and call the missile units onto its attacker. It then charges any enemy unit of three or more figures within eight cells, and otherwise returns to rally waypoint 2 every fifth think.

functions.name: UnitOrder_FieldMelee
functions.comment: Field battle, unit categories 3 (macemen, swordsmen) and 4 (knights): both dispatch slots hold this one function. Identical in shape to UnitOrder_FieldFoot, with thirteen marching thinks rather than ten, a nine-cell charge radius rather than eight, a rally every eighth think, and a limit of two withdrawals per unit.

functions.name: Order_DoNothing
functions.comment: An immediate return, called from the opening `orders` phases of the field handlers: the units stand still while the battle starts.

functions.name: Order_HoldPosition
functions.comment: Sets the unit's destination to its own current position and re-issues the order, stopping the unit where it stands and reforming it there.

functions.name: Order_ToSecondTarget
functions.comment: Copies the unit's second destination pair (+0x26/+0x28) into the live destination and re-issues the order. The battering ram's default move.

functions.name: Order_StepAwayFromUnit
functions.comment: Shifts the current unit's destination two cells directly away from `unit`, along the longer axis and along both when an axis separation exceeds five. Sets the withdrawing flag +0x10 and counts the withdrawal in +0x2B. This is the whole of the AI's retreat behaviour.

functions.name: Order_StepTowardRallyPoint
functions.comment: The mirror of Order_StepAwayFromUnit: shifts the destination two cells toward g_aiRallyX / g_aiRallyY and clears g_aiRallyRequest. How a missile unit answers a melee unit that has just been attacked.

functions.name: BattleUnit_OrderToEnemyEnd
functions.comment: Sends the current unit to a slot of the opposing sides deployment marker - side 0 to the 0x0F marker, side 4 to the 0x04 marker. Together with Deploy_SlotForUnit this establishes that side 0 deploys at the 0x04 marker and side 4 at the 0x0F marker.

functions.name: Order_ToRallyWaypoint
functions.comment: Moves the unit to one of three rally waypoints for its side, from g_rallyWaypoints indexed by g_battleRallyGroup. Both field battlefield builders fill that table; a .skr map puts all three on the deployment marker.

functions.name: Order_ToWallSlot
functions.comment: Moves a siege defender onto one of sixteen wall positions in one of the groups at 0x00554180, skipping empty entries and wrapping, offset one cell west and two north of the recorded position.

functions.name: Order_ToCastleApproach
functions.comment: Moves a siege attacker to one of four approach points per index from the castle layout tables at 0x0055CD90, selected by g_battleApproachLane. Rams always use the primary table; everyone else switches on the castle orientation flag.

functions.name: Order_ToFieldCorner
functions.comment: Sends a siege attacker to a fixed corner of the field - (6,74) or (74,74) - by castle layout, or to Order_ToCastleApproach when the layout flag is neither 1 nor 2. The opening move of most siege-attacker scripts.

functions.name: Order_ToCastleObjective
functions.comment: Moves the unit onto one of the two castle cells Battlefield_BuildCastle recorded: always the primary for mode 1, otherwise the secondary unless the moat flag or the castle index says otherwise.

functions.name: Order_ToWallBelowKeep
functions.comment: Takes the primary castle cell, drops four cells south, and moves onto the nearest surface-4 cell within five. The siege defender's fall-back position.

functions.name: Order_ToKeep
functions.comment: Moves the unit onto the secondary castle cell, offset two west and one north, when there is one; onto the primary when there is not.

functions.name: Order_ToCell
functions.comment: Converts a battlefield cell byte offset back into x,y and issues the move. The common tail of most siege order actions.

functions.name: Order_ToSurface5Near
functions.comment: Moves the unit onto the nearest surface-5 cell within five cells of the given cell, or does nothing if there is none.

functions.name: Order_OntoUnit
functions.comment: Sets the destination to another unit's position and issues the move: walk straight at the enemy. The melee handlers' aggressive answer to being hit.

functions.name: Order_HalfwayToUnit
functions.comment: Advances half the separation toward another unit. It does nothing at all unless one axis is separated by eight cells or more, and then shifts only those axes separated by six or more. This is why AI missile units advance in stages and then stop.

functions.name: Order_ChargeNearest
functions.comment: Sets the halted flag +0x2A and puts every figure of the unit into state 8 - free pursuit of the nearest enemy figure via Melee_ChooseChaseTarget - clearing their routes. The AI's all-out charge, and the only thing a siege defender does once it is overwhelmingly stronger.

functions.name: Order_ShootAtUnit
functions.comment: For each figure of the current unit, finds a target within forty cells restricted to `unit` and puts the figure into state 17 aimed at it. Returns 0 if any figure found nothing, which the caller reads as "that unit is out of reach".

functions.name: Order_ToWallNearPreferredTarget
functions.comment: Picks a target with Missile_FindTargetPreferShooters, then moves the unit onto the nearest surface-4 cell within twenty of that target.

functions.name: Order_ToWallNearAvoidedTarget
functions.comment: As Order_ToWallNearPreferredTarget but choosing with Missile_FindTargetAvoidShooters, so the unit posts itself opposite enemy foot rather than enemy shooters.

functions.name: Order_ToNearestWallCell
functions.comment: Moves onto the nearest surface-4 cell within forty cells of the unit, or does nothing if there is none.

functions.name: Order_ToBreachOrStaging
functions.comment: While g_siegeApproachScore is under 16 it searches radii 12..19 for a way in and moves there; between 16 and 400 it falls back on the secondary staging table; above 400 it does nothing at all.

functions.name: Order_ToSiegeStaging
functions.comment: The siege attacker's staging move: the primary approach table when g_siegeApproachScore is below 16 or above 399, the secondary table five cells further in between, or a fixed offset from the castle when the orientation flag is set.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeAttMissile
functions.comment: Siege attacker, unit category 1. Field corner on think 0, a castle approach point every fifteenth think, and from think 11 an alternation of two staging routines on an eleven-of-sixteen rotation. Once there is a breach it shoots into it, or moves onto the castle objective when it cannot.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeAttFoot
functions.comment: Siege attacker, unit category 2. The longest of the order scripts: a ladder of `orders` thresholds (8, 18, 25, 31, 40, 51, 60, 71) alternating two staging positions, with a jump that sets `orders` to 100 when the castle layout flag is set. Charges outright once g_aiStrengthAdvantage reaches 151.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeAttMelee
functions.comment: Siege attacker, unit category 3. The same staging ladder as UnitOrder_SiegeAttFoot with different thresholds (15, 25, 30, 41, 50, 61, 70, 81), plus a six-phase rotation deciding when to move onto the castle objective and when to hold.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeAttKnight
functions.comment: Siege attacker, unit category 4. Moves to a field corner for ten thinks then cycles castle approach points until think 31. Also the only handler that raises the flag at 0x0056D5C8 - when the AI side is all knights and nothing is breached yet.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeAttCatapult
functions.comment: Siege attacker, unit category 5 (catapults). Nothing for four thinks, a field corner to think 13, a castle approach to think 21, then from think 31 the nearest surface-4 cell within twenty cells of one of its figures - twenty cells being exactly the catapult firing range in g_missileStats. Has no in-melee gate, so it keeps thinking while engaged.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeAttTower
functions.comment: Siege attacker, unit category 6 (siege towers). Moves to a field corner for eleven thinks, then - once g_siegeApproachScore passes 6 after think 60, or passes 10 at any time - widens a search from radius 10 to 30 for a surface-4 cell and moves onto it. This is the code that walks a tower up to the wall.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeAttRam
functions.comment: Siege attacker, unit category 7 (battering rams). Ignores `orders` entirely: it picks between its stored secondary destination and a castle approach point from three flags - the castle layout flag, g_siegeApproachScore, and whether the drawbridge patch has been laid.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeDefMissile
functions.comment: Siege defender, unit category 1. Rotates through nine wall slots every other think while fewer than three attackers stand on the wall, and falls back on the castle objective when more do. Its sortie branch above g_aiSortieThreshold discards the Enemy_NearestUnit result and then calls Order_HalfwayToUnit on its own unit index, so it does nothing at all - see docs/battle-ai.md 6.3.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeDefWallMissileA
functions.comment: Siege defender, unit category 9 - which BattleUnit_Create gives to the first missile unit raised for a side-0 siege defender. The handler does nothing but count its `orders` field up, so this unit holds the wall slot it was deployed on for the whole battle.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeDefWallMissileB
functions.comment: Siege defender, unit category 10 - the second missile unit of a side-0 siege defender. Moves to a wall cell beside the enemy figure its own men would rather not shoot at, and falls back on the wall below the keep once attackers reach the rampart.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeDefFoot
functions.comment: Siege defender, unit category 2. Thinks every 100 frames rather than 200 and does not check the in-melee flag, so it keeps re-deciding while fighting. Its Enemy_NearestUnit(unit, 10, 0) call discards the result. Then either charges (sortie) or holds the castle objective.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeDefMelee
functions.comment: Siege defender, unit category 3. Thinks every 100 frames. Reserves a defence post with Siege_ClaimDefencePost, moves onto an attacking unit that has reached the wall, and otherwise rotates four inner wall slots every fifteenth think - abandoning all of it for the castle objective once four or more attackers are on the wall.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeDefKnight
functions.comment: Siege defender, unit category 4. Sits on wall-slot group 2 every twentieth think until a single attacker reaches the wall, then falls back on the castle objective. The most passive of the defender handlers.

functions.name: UnitOrder_SiegeDefOil
functions.comment: Siege defender, unit category 8 (boiling oil). Calls Oil_FindPourTarget: if the unit is high enough on the wall it moves to the densest cluster of enemy figures within six cells (four if it is on the rampart proper), needing three enemies (two). Otherwise it retreats toward the keep.

functions.name: Oil_FindPourTarget
functions.comment: The cell a boiling-oil unit should move to: nothing when its own cell is below elevation 2; otherwise the densest enemy cluster within six cells needing three enemies (own surface below 6), or within four needing two (surface 6 and above).

functions.name: Oil_IsOnHighWall
functions.comment: True when the unit stands at elevation 2 or more on a cell of surface 6 or above. Decides whether an oil unit holds its post or falls back.

functions.name: BattleUnit_FewOnRampart
functions.comment: True when fewer than four of the unit's live figures stand on cells of surface 4 or above, and only once the drawbridge patch has been laid.

functions.name: Siege_ClaimDefencePost
functions.comment: A twenty-entry (cell, unit) reservation table. Returns the cell already reserved for this unit, or reserves the first free non-empty entry for it. Stops two defending units posting to the same place.

functions.name: Enemy_NearestUnit
functions.signature: int Enemy_NearestUnit(int unit, int maxDist, int minFigures)
functions.comment: Unit-level target selection: the nearest enemy unit by Chebyshev distance between the two units' centres, within maxDist cells and holding at least minFigures figures; 0 if there is none. Missile units call it with maxDist 80 - the whole field - and melee units with 8 or 9.

functions.name: BattleUnit_JoinMelee
functions.comment: Called from BattleMan_Step on both units the moment a figure walks into an enemy. Puts every other live, non-melee figure of the unit into state 8 (free pursuit). Skipped for human-controlled units, for missile units (category 1) and while the unit's order lock +0x0E is non-zero - so an AI melee unit piles in on contact and a player's unit does not.

functions.name: BattleMan_Step
functions.comment: Movement. Waits g_troopBattleStats[type].moveDelay ticks per sub-step, accumulates 2 per step until 17, then takes the next path direction and calls BattleMan_TryStepDir. Knights have delay 0 and pikemen 4, which is why knights are fastest and pikemen slowest.

functions.name: BattleMen_SwapPlaces
functions.comment: When a figure walks into a friendly figure of the same troop type it swaps places with it, carrying position, cell, hits and men across. Returns 2 on a swap.

functions.name: BattleMan_TryStepDir
functions.comment: Turns a direction 0..7 into a neighbouring cell offset, clamps at the map edge and calls Cell_TryEnter.

functions.name: Cell_TryEnter
functions.comment: Decides whether a figure may enter a battlefield cell: 1 free, 0 blocked by a friendly figure or flag 0x40, 2 impassable (flags 0x10/0x80, or an elevation change of more than 1), 5 flag 0x20 for a non-zero side, 999 enemy figure present.

functions.name: Cell_TryEnterEngine
functions.comment: The siege-engine arm of BattleMan_TryStepDir: a 3-cell-wide engine tests its whole leading edge rather than one cell. Turns a direction 0..7 into the orthogonal or diagonal leaf test and clamps two cells from the map edge instead of one.

functions.name: Cell_TryEnterEngineOrtho
functions.comment: Tests the three cells of a siege engine's leading edge for an orthogonal step, from the offsets at g_engineEdgeOrtho. Returns Cell_TryEnter's vocabulary plus one value Cell_TryEnter never produces: 6, and only when troopType == 9 - a battering ram against a cell flagged 0x20 or 0x40. That is the sole way into figure state 14.

functions.name: Cell_TryEnterEngineDiag
functions.comment: The diagonal twin of Cell_TryEnterEngineOrtho, reading g_engineEdgeDiag. Same return vocabulary, same ram-only 6.

functions.name: BattleMan_NextPathDir
functions.comment: Returns the direction towards the figure current waypoint and consumes it. The list is walked from the end, because Path_Extract builds it backwards from the destination.

functions.name: Missile_Step
functions.comment: Advances the current missile by its steps-per-tick and, when it enters a cell holding an enemy figure, applies the missile damage formula: elevation scaling, minus the target armour, minus the crossbow-vs-engine reduction, floor 2, accumulated into the target hits pool; every 100 hits kills one man. See docs/battle.md.

functions.name: Missile_StepError
functions.comment: One Bresenham error update, parameter 1 meaning "the major axis is x". Adds 2*d(minor) when the error is negative and 2*(d(minor) - d(major)) otherwise, and decrements the remaining major-axis count. Called by Missile_Step once per sub-step; g_missileStats' sub-step column is 4 for every class.

functions.name: Missile_SetupLine
functions.signature: void Missile_SetupLine(int missile, int x0, int y0, int x1, int y1)
functions.comment: Bresenham set-up for a missile's flight: |dx| into +0x20, |dy| into +0x24, and 2*min - max into the error term at +0x28, then snaps the flight direction +0x2E to the nearer of the eight octants when one axis is more than twice the other. Called by Missile_Spawn.

functions.name: Missile_OffMap
functions.comment: Returns 1 when the missile's cell coordinates (+0x14, +0x16) have left 0..79 in either axis. The battlefield bound 0x50 again, so a missile that misses everything dies at the map edge rather than flying forever.

functions.name: Missile_StepTowardTargetY
functions.comment: Moves the missile's y (+0x0C) one unit toward its target y (+0x10). The twin of Missile_StepTowardTargetX.

functions.name: Missile_StepTowardTargetX
functions.comment: Moves the missile's x (+0x0A, in 1/32 cell) one unit toward its target x (+0x0E), or leaves it alone when they are equal.

functions.name: BattleMan_BurnTick
functions.comment: Adds 3/6/9/12 hits per tick (1/3/5/7 for siege engines) by battlefield size class to a figure standing on a burning cell, +1/+2 more if the owner is human-controlled. Threshold 100 (160 for engines) kills one man.

functions.name: Melee_Tick
functions.comment: One tick of a melee duel. The attacker decrements the defender recovery counter; when it expires the defender takes the attacker melee attack value into its hits pool, and once per exchange the attacker heavy-blow bonus as well. 100 hits kills one man; the attacker role swaps when the exchange counter runs out.

functions.name: Melee_ResetExchange
functions.comment: Sets how long this figure holds the attacking role in a duel, from its animation class: 0, 40, 80, 80 or 120 ticks.

functions.name: Melee_ResetRecovery
functions.comment: Adds the figure recovery interval (+0x18B) to its recovery counter. That interval is the rate at which the figure can be hit in melee, so it is the real melee defence: peasants and archers 6 ticks, crossbowmen 8, macemen and swordsmen 12, knights 16, pikemen 30.

functions.name: Melee_FindAdjacentEnemy
functions.comment: Tests the eight neighbouring cells in the order N, NW, NE, W, E, SW, SE, S and returns the direction of the first live enemy figure, or 8. Siege engines (troop types 7..10) are never returned.

functions.name: Melee_ChooseChaseTarget
functions.comment: Figure-level target selection for state 8, and the most visible AI decision in the game. Score is the Chebyshev distance to the enemy figure, halved if that figure carries a missile weapon, plus that figure's `targeted` counter; lowest wins. Siege engines and dead figures are skipped, there is no range limit, and the winner's `targeted` is raised by 2 so the next chaser picks somebody else.

functions.name: Missile_FindTarget
functions.signature: bool Missile_FindTarget(int range, int man, int unit)
functions.comment: Nearest live enemy figure within `range` by Manhattan distance, capped at 160. The unit ordered target is forced to distance 0; siege-engine targets get a +35 distance penalty.

functions.name: Missile_FindTargetPreferShooters
functions.signature: bool Missile_FindTargetPreferShooters(int range, int man, int unit)
functions.comment: Missile_FindTarget with two extra weights: an enemy in state 9 (filling the moat) scores a quarter of its distance, and an enemy carrying a missile weapon scores half. Used by Order_ToWallNearPreferredTarget to post defenders opposite the enemy shooters.

functions.name: Missile_FindTargetAvoidShooters
functions.signature: bool Missile_FindTargetAvoidShooters(int range, int man, int unit)
functions.comment: The mirror of Missile_FindTargetPreferShooters: state 9 still scores a quarter, but an enemy with a missile weapon scores double, so it is picked last. Used by Order_ToWallNearAvoidedTarget.

functions.name: Enemy_FindCluster
functions.signature: int Enemy_FindCluster(int x, int y, uint owner, int maxSurface, int radius, int minCount)
functions.comment: Counts live enemy figures on cells of surface <= maxSurface in a square of the given radius and returns the first such cell's byte offset, or 0 if fewer than minCount were found. The boiling-oil unit's aiming routine.

functions.name: Siege_FindCellSurface4
functions.signature: int Siege_FindCellSurface4(int x, int y, int radius, int maxElevation)
functions.comment: Nearest cell of surface 4 within a square radius whose elevation is at most maxElevation, left in g_foundWallX / g_foundWallY. Distance is Manhattan when maxElevation is 4 and min(|dx|,|dy|) otherwise. How catapults, siege towers and the wall-bound defenders find the wall.

functions.name: Siege_FindCellSurface5
functions.signature: bool Siege_FindCellSurface5(int x, int y, int radius)
functions.comment: Nearest cell of surface 5 within a square radius by Manhattan distance, left in g_foundTileX / g_foundTileY. Used to put a defending unit on the rampart beside a given cell.

functions.name: Cell_NeighbourHasSurface
functions.signature: int Cell_NeighbourHasSurface(int x, int y, int cellOffset, uint surface)
functions.comment: Tests the four orthogonal neighbours of a cell for a given surface value (cell byte +7), clipped at the map edge. Verified by arithmetic: the four bases it reads are 0x00543E67, 0x00544367, 0x005440DF and 0x005440EF, which are g_battlefield + 7 offset by -0x280, +0x280, -8 and +8 - one row north, one row south, one cell west, one cell east.

functions.name: Melee_AdjacentEnemyDir
functions.signature: int Melee_AdjacentEnemyDir(int x, int y, int cellOffset)
functions.comment: Scans the eight neighbours via g_cellNeighbourOffsets and returns the direction of an enemy figure standing at the same elevation, or 8.

functions.name: Order_StopShortOfTarget
functions.signature: void Order_StopShortOfTarget(int x, int y, int tx, int ty, int range)
functions.comment: Pulls a move destination back so the unit halts (range - 3) cells from its target, leaving the result in g_foundTileX / g_foundTileY. This is how missile units stop at firing range instead of closing.

functions.name: Campaign_EnterConquest
functions.comment: The step out of a finished game and into screen 0x1C. [V] Increments the campaign counter g_campaignMap ONLY when g_gameOutcome is 10, which is the whole rule for replaying a lost map; copies g_scenarioIndex into g_campaignLastMap so the interstitial can name the country just fought over; calls Campaign_LoadEntry to bring in the next row; sets g_screenId = 0x1C. Reached from Msg_Dismiss when the dismissed message left the outcome at 10 or 11.

functions.name: Game_NewGame
functions.comment: New-game setup: year 1267/1268, g_season = 3, g_seasonNext = 4, then Map_InitScenario, Merchant_SpawnAll and one immediate Season_Advance - which is why a new game begins in Winter 1268.

functions.name: PlayerStart_Shuffle
functions.comment: Re-deals the live entries of g_playerStartTable into each other slots, from Game_NewGame between Mercenary_Init and PlayerStart_Compact. For each source entry i it draws a random offset, pos = (rand & 3) + 1 + i wrapping at the live count, then probes forward for a free destination. [V] THIS IS WHY WHICH REALM YOU PLAY IS DIFFERENT EVERY GAME: docs/environment.md records the realm-to-county assignment as rolled per game, from two independently created England turn-one saves disagreeing about it, and this is the code that rolls it. The start counties themselves never move - they are the map plane-4 markers. Its second half deals a 48-entry table into DAT_0057CAE0 and fills DAT_00553080 with 0, 100 or 6 + 5n per entry; neither destination has been traced and neither is a player start. Reproduced in l2_scenario::newgame::shuffle_starts on our own Pcg32 - the shape is the original, the stream cannot be. See decisions.md C62.

functions.name: Map_InitMode
functions.comment: Campaign map bring-up: scroll origin row 0x4A col 0x14, zoom 0, battle phase 0, overview panel rect (480, 48, 160, 160), map 64x64 with an 8-byte runtime tile record, then Map_BuildLattice(0) and Map_SetZoom(0).

functions.name: Rules_InitConstants
functions.comment: Writes the tunable economy scalars into .data at startup: g_grainYieldPerSack = 12, g_grainMaxSacksPerField = 10, g_foodPerHead = 10, g_foodPerSack = 6, g_dairyPerHead = 5, g_grainLabourDivisorAdv = 5, g_grainLabourDivisor = 2.

functions.name: Gfx_LoadCountyMode
functions.comment: Loads the campaign map artwork. base = (g_mapZoom == 2) ? 0x20 : 0, plus (g_season-1)*8; then eight consecutive g_resourceTable entries go to g_bankBase, g_bankMtns, g_bankRoads, g_bankTown, g_bankCastle, g_spriteSheetA, g_spriteSheetB and g_flagsSheet in that order - independent confirmation of the bank order in maps-layers.md section 1.1. Misc_cty.pl8 follows into g_miscCtySheet.

functions.name: Res_LoadStatic
functions.comment: Loads the thirteen records of g_preloadTable into their fixed .data buffers - three palettes, five fonts, mouse.pl8, System2.pl8, Panels.pl8, l2.eng and vill_gd8.pl8. That table is the whole interface asset list.

functions.name: Res_LoadButtons
functions.comment: Loads system2.pl8 (skin 0) or system.pl8 (skin 1) into g_systemSheet. Same size and same 84-frame layout, but 69 of System2.pl8s frames are entirely index 0 and none of System.pl8s are, and the kingdom screens ask for skin 1 - so the county panels button art is System.pl8. docs/screens-county.md section 4.2.

functions.name: Music_StartCampaign
functions.comment: THE CAMPAIGN MUSIC PICKER, and it is a progress bar. countyCount < 2 -> scroll1; then shareOfMapPct < 8 -> scroll1, < 15 -> scroll2, < 29 -> scroll3, < 43 -> scroll4, else scroll5. shareOfMapPct is PctOf(countyCount, g_countyCount) - counties over counties, armies are not in it. Reached from Opt_ToggleMusic when g_battlePhase is 0, which is the WHOLE management surface: there is no separate county track. Its opening branch tests whether scroll2.wav EXISTS and is dead on a complete install.

functions.name: Sound_PlayTroopCry
functions.comment: Indexes g_troopSounds as unit*0x100 + class*0x40 + take*0x10, where unit is DAT_0055408C and take round-robins 0..3 in g_troopCryCounter per (unit, class). Class 3 forces take 0, so three cells per block are unreachable (docs/bugs.md D34).

functions.name: Sound_LoadKingdomBank
functions.comment: Sound_LoadBank(g_soundBankKingdom, 12) - the campaign and county effects.

functions.name: Sound_LoadBattleBank
functions.comment: Sound_LoadBank(g_soundBankBattle, 17) - the battle effects.

functions.name: Setup_CommitOptions
functions.comment: The step between the setup screen and the game, called from the Start button immediately before Setup_StartGame. Reads the twelve selections at 0x0053F288.. and writes the eleven values a game is played with: five straight through (advanced farming, exploration, armies eat, difficulty, fight humans only), one by arithmetic (the AI lord count), and five through a table - g_timeLimitSeconds, g_startingGold, g_startArmoury, g_startTroops and g_countyStatus. So a drop-down wired straight to g_optDifficulty would be wrong for five of the twelve.

functions.name: Campaign_LoadEntry
functions.comment: Loads campaign row g_campaignMap out of g_campaignTableA or g_campaignTableB (g_campaignTrack picks) into g_scenarioIndex, g_optDifficulty and six option globals, then Minimap_Load, Map_LoadPlanes and Map_BuildLattice on the new scenario. [V] Forces g_optTimeLimit = 0, g_optFightHumansOnly = 1 and advanced farming, exploration and army eating off, so a campaign map ignores whatever the custom-game screen last set. On the eighth win it reads row 8, one past the eight real rows, and both tables are padded with two zeroed rows so that read is harmless.

functions.name: Turn_Tick
functions.comment: Per-frame dispatcher on g_turnPhase (1..7). Phase 1 neutral-county upkeep, 2 army movement, 3 supply transports, 4 the players' turn, 5 peasant mobs, 6 merchants, 7 end of season. Increments g_turnPhaseStep every call.

functions.name: Save_RotateAndWrite
functions.comment: Rotates safeturn.sav <- old_turn.sav <- lastturn.sav and then calls Save_Write. Called from Game_NewGame and at each turn boundary.

functions.name: AI_RunTurnStep
functions.comment: One step of one realm's turn, round-robin over realms 1..5 through 0x0057C944. Realm +0x00 is a 1..14 program counter into fourteen sub-handlers; at 15 + 2*realm the realm is marked done (999). [V] The realm +0x05 (human) test guards the fourteen handlers and the counter's increment, NOT the initialisation above them: step 0 - Realm_RecountStrength, Realm_UpdateTotals, clear +0x1C, set the counter to 1 - runs for EVERY realm, the human included. That is where a human player's own elimination is detected, and an earlier revision of this entry said the whole function was skipped for a human.

functions.name: Ai_ManageFarmsAll
functions.comment: The first thing Season_Advance does, before Rand_Advance: Ai_ManageCountyFarms for every realm that is in play and not human. It runs ahead of the whole economy, so an AI fields and labour split are already this season when tax, rations and industry read them. The human county is not touched.

functions.name: Score_RankRealms
functions.comment: Recomputes each realm's score at +0x50 from counties, population, castles, armies and treasury, bubble-sorts realms 1..5 into the ranking table at 0x00565410 and writes the rank back to realm +0x2B.

functions.name: Mp_DropDepartedPlayers
functions.comment: Season pass 1. For each realm that is marked human, has no lord, and whose slot in the 6 x 0x2C connection table at 0x00553D50 has gone to zero, calls Realm_Eliminate, decrements the player count at 0x00553F98, and sets lord = 6 - the knocked-out value. [V] Such a realm still holds its counties, so Realm_Eliminate takes the second branch and sends group 258, "This player has left the game", which is the case this pass exists to produce. The gate is g_multiplayer, whose name is only inferred and is probably a network-game flag; that reading is not settled here.

functions.name: Realm_RecountStrength
functions.comment: Rebuilds realm +0x04 as 3 * owned counties + 1 * armies (g_units slots 1..150 with type 1; merchants, transports and mobs do not count) and, if that comes out zero, the realm has just been eliminated. [V] The whole body is guarded on +0x04 already being non-zero, so it fires exactly once per realm. The message is chosen on "is this the local player", not on "is this a human": g_localPlayer gets L2.eng group 224 "Defeat!" addressed from and to itself, an AI raises group 194 "Foiled again." from itself, and a second human in a network game is told nothing at all - the voice rotation at +0x159 advances in all three cases. Then Score_RankRealms, and in multiplayer Net_SendCommand(0x24) if it was me. Four callers: AI_RunTurnStep's step 0 (EVERY realm, the human included), County_ChangeOwner - which calls it on the outgoing owner BEFORE writing the new one, so that call can never eliminate anybody - and the two arms of the post-battle resolution.

functions.name: Turn_BeginPlayersTurn
functions.comment: Resets every realm's AI program counter at the top of phase 4: aiStep = 0, or 999 for a realm at zero strength, and g_realmsActive counts the rest. [V] The counter is reset for the human too, because AI_RunTurnStep's step 0 runs for every realm.

functions.name: Turn_AllRealmsDone
functions.comment: Returns non-zero once every in-play realm's AI step counter (realm +0x00) has reached 999. The exit condition of phase 4.

functions.name: PlayerStart_Record
functions.comment: Writes {county, slot} into g_playerStartTable[slot] and counts non-zero slots into g_playerStartCount. Called from Map_LoadPlanes for settlement tiles with a non-zero plane 4: the player start table. See docs/formats/maps-layers.md 5.1.

functions.name: PlayerStart_Compact
functions.comment: Drops the player-start slots above the number of live realms by bubbling the table down, so a game with fewer lords than the map seats leaves the extra start counties unowned rather than off the end of the array.

functions.name: Game_SetupRealmsAndCounties
functions.comment: The starting position, from Game_NewGame after Map_InitScenario. Every county takes grain, herd, population, health and happiness from g_countyStatus[g_startCountyStatus]; every realm with a lord takes its start county out of g_playerStartTable, gold from g_startingGoldChosen, 50 each of iron, wood and stone, weapons from g_startArmoury[g_startWeapons] with difficulty * 20 extra in slot 4 for an AI, a garrison raised by Army_Create from g_startTroops[g_startArmySize], and the castle from g_startCastle. A realm with no lord is skipped entirely. Finally every unowned county gets 100 more grain.

functions.name: Realms_AssignLords
functions.comment: New-game lord assignment, and not a name display as first guessed - it writes g_playerNames rather than drawing it. For each realm without one it picks an unused lord from g_lordChoice (indexed by the lord id and, off the deterministic path, by g_scenarioIndex & 3), stores the title in realm +0x07 and the lord id in +0x0A, takes the two colours from g_realmColour, and copies 16 bytes of L2.eng group 7 through Eng_Seek into g_playerNames + realm*0x2C. Group 7 is 'No player' / 'The Knight' / 'The Baron' / 'The Countess' / 'The Bishop'.

functions.name: Turn_AdvancePhase
functions.comment: g_turnPhase++, wrapping 7 -> 1 (and then calling FUN_0049B6D3); resets g_turnPhaseStep and sets the next-phase preview at 0x0053F678.

functions.name: Realm_Eliminate
functions.comment: Removes a realm from the game: every county it holds goes to County_MakeIndependent, every army it has is destroyed, strength and shieldIndex are zeroed and its connection slot is cleared. [V] It picks its message on whether the realm still had anything - 3 per county plus 1 per army - and the two L2.eng groups say which case is which: 224 "Defeat!" for a realm that had nothing left, 258 "This player has left the game. All their lands are forfeit" for one that still did.

functions.name: AI_SetTaxRates
functions.comment: Sets county +0xB9 from happiness on one of four ladders (neutral counties, then three by AI personality), and grants the AI its per-turn difficulty bonus: gold from g_aiGoldGrant, plus free population, herd and grain scaled by difficulty.

functions.name: Ai_ManageCountyFarms
functions.comment: For each county this AI holds: order more fields reclaimed if it is short for its population - none at all, or under 3 with over 200 people, under 5 over 400, under 7 over 600, under 9 over 1000, all of which ask for one; over 1200 people asks for two - then copy the lord's farmStyle from g_aiPersonality into county +0x1FE and lay the fields out by it, then Labour_Allocate. [V] Only styles 0, 1 and 9 are dispatched, and county +0x1FE in the England turn-one fixture holds only 0, 1 and 9.

functions.name: AI_ManageFields
functions.comment: Turn phase 1 step 2, and its ONLY caller passes realm 0 - this is the UNOWNED counties pass, not an AI realm one. Zeroes county +0x1B0, runs the same field-reclamation ladder as Ai_ManageCountyFarms, then dispatches county +0x1FE into Ai_FarmStyleNeutralArable (style 0) or Ai_FarmStyleNeutralGrazing (style 1) and calls Labour_Allocate. [V] It never writes +0x1FE, so an unowned county farms by whichever lord held it last, and one left holding style 9 is dispatched nowhere at all. Do not confuse it with Ai_ManageCountyFarms at 0x0049DD01, which is AI turn step 5 and dispatches three different allocators.

functions.name: Ai_TradeForCounty
functions.comment: The three AI-realm farming styles run this first. Skipped entirely if the county has no merchant stall or the realm is bankrupt. For each of wood, iron and stone: a non-zero want at realm +0x70/+0x74/+0x7C buys that much, and a zero want sells everything above the lord personality reserve at +0x84/+0x88/+0x8C. Then, if gold clears personality +0x78, buys personality +0x7C of the weapon the county is making - the county weapon type 0..5 maps to market good 12/11/13/9/10/14.

functions.name: AI_BuildCastles
functions.comment: AI turn step 6. For each owned, castle-less county above personality +0xC8 population, and while the realm has fewer than personality +0x90 builds in progress, orders the largest castle type whose gold threshold at personality +0xCC..+0xDC the treasury clears. A zero threshold means that type is not offered to that lord. The Bishop reaches the royal castle at 2,000 gold where the Knight needs 10,000, and the Baron and Countess never build one.

functions.name: AI_EmergencyWeapons
functions.comment: An AI down to one county before year 1273 is handed 100 each of weapon types 3 and 4 if its lord is 4 (the Bishop), or 100 of weapon type 0 if its lord is 3 (the Countess). The Knight and the Baron get nothing. Returns 1 if it granted anything.

functions.name: AI_Diplomacy
functions.comment: AI turn step 2, and the real diplomacy driver. Heals standing by +1 a turn towards every NON-HUMAN realm, so an AI's opinion of a human player never recovers. Then ages the alliance grudge and breaks the alliance past personality +0x10; then, from year 1269 and if not ranked 1st, courts Diplo_PickAllyCandidate's pick every personality +0x14 turns - silently against an AI, with group 180 against a human. Its ally-is-winning tier ladder has its comparisons inverted, so two of its three tiers are unreachable.

functions.name: Diplo_PickAllyCandidate
functions.comment: Picks the best-ranked realm that is in play, not ranked 1st, unallied, not already being courted, not at war with this one, and above standing -10. Returns 0 for none.

functions.name: AI_Taunt
functions.comment: AI turn step 13, and NOT "offer or break an alliance" - alliances are step 2. Only a realm ranked first taunts. Stage 0: above 39 percent of the map, count to 8, then send group 193 to every live human realm, reset and go to stage 1. Stage 1: above 27 percent, and only if the last-placed realm is human and not this realm ally, count to 8, then send group 192 to it and return to stage 0. Every letter advances voiceRotation with the 3-to-0 wrap and carries variant lord*4 + rotation - 4. The share test only gates the count, so slipping below the threshold pauses the timer rather than resetting it.

functions.name: Diplo_ActionAllowed
functions.signature: int Diplo_ActionAllowed(unsigned int actor, unsigned int target)
functions.comment: Returns 0 when target is actor's ally - adding 1 to the ally's grudge instead - or when the two are the same realm; 1 otherwise. Gates the offence hook, which is why hostile acts against an ally cost grudge rather than standing.

functions.name: Diplo_FormAlliance
functions.comment: Sets pair.allied = 1 and pair.grudge = 0 both ways and realm +0x81 on both sides. Six bytes; that is the whole of what an alliance is. realm +0x81 is a single byte, so a realm has at most one ally.

functions.name: Diplo_ReconcileAlliances
functions.comment: Called from Turn_Tick. Rebuilds the allied matrix from the realms' ally bytes and drops any pairing that is one-sided or whose partner has been eliminated.

functions.name: Diplo_BreakAlliance
functions.signature: void Diplo_BreakAlliance(unsigned int a, unsigned int b)
functions.comment: Clears pair.allied and realm +0x81 on whichever sides point at the other. Does not touch standing - the caller applies that.

functions.name: Diplo_PayForHelp
functions.signature: void Diplo_PayForHelp(int ally, int payer, unsigned char county, int price)
functions.comment: Moves price gold from payer to ally if they can afford it, increments pair.helpPriceMultiple so the next purchase costs more, takes standing -4, and sets the ally's warTarget (realm +0xE8) to the county. Called with price 0 when the ally agreed for free, and from the pay prompt otherwise.

functions.name: Diplo_Init
functions.comment: Clears every inbox and every realm-pair record at new game. The one place each field of the 16-byte pair record at realm +0x84 + other*0x10 is written, which is what makes the field map in docs/diplomacy.md a reading rather than a guess: standing = 5 for an in-play AI realm and 0 otherwise, allied/grudge/warningsSent/atWar/complimentsFrom/hasMail = 0, bestGift = 0, helpPriceMultiple = 1.

functions.name: Diplo_DefaultTarget
functions.comment: Sets g_diploTarget to the first in-play realm that is not the local player, or 0.

functions.name: Diplo_Offend
functions.signature: void Diplo_Offend(unsigned int offended, unsigned int offender, char amount)
functions.comment: The single hook every relationship-damaging act goes through. If the offender was an ally: break it, set pair.atWar unless the offended lord is 4 (the Bishop), set warTarget, Diplo_OffendAll(offender, 15), send group 182, and add 15 to the penalty. Then standing -= amount, clamped to [-30,+30]. Once standing bottoms out at -30 against a human it walks pair.warningsSent: group 189, then 190, then 191 and war.

functions.name: Diplo_OffendAll
functions.comment: Lowers every other realm's standing towards this one. Only reached from Diplo_Offend when an alliance is betrayed - the one act in the game that costs reputation with third parties.

functions.name: Diplo_ClearInboxes
functions.comment: Zeroes all 6 x 5 inbox slots. Called by Diplo_Init.

functions.name: Diplo_Post
functions.signature: void Diplo_Post(int from, int to, int kind, int gold, unsigned char county)
functions.comment: The only writer of g_diploInbox. Fills the first free of five slots; bumps the recipient pair record's complimentsFrom when kind == 1; sets hasMail; and moves the gold immediately, clamped to what the sender holds - a gift is spent when it is posted, not when it is answered.

functions.name: Diplo_AnswerInbox
functions.comment: AI turn step 1. Walks the realm's five inbox slots, dispatching kind 0..6 to the seven reply handlers, then zeroes all five slots and all six hasMail bytes. An inbox is emptied every turn whether or not it was full, and a human realm never runs this because the AI turn machine is skipped for it.

functions.name: Diplo_ReplyGift
functions.signature: void Diplo_ReplyGift(int me, int them, int gold)
functions.comment: Kind 0. Three tiers against best + T/2 and best + T, where T = personality +0x08 and best = pair.bestGift: L2.eng group 173 and standing -8, group 172 and +5, group 171 and +10. Then bestGift = max(bestGift, gold), so the bar ratchets and each gift must beat the last.

functions.name: Diplo_ReplyCompliment
functions.comment: Kind 1. On pair.complimentsFrom, which Diplo_Post incremented and nothing ever resets: 1 -> group 174 and standing +15, 2 -> group 175 and +8, 3 or more -> group 176 and -4. Group 176 is 'You are boring me now with your groveling letters.'

functions.name: Diplo_ReplyInsult
functions.signature: void Diplo_ReplyInsult(unsigned int me, unsigned int them)
functions.comment: Kind 2. Breaks any alliance between the two, standing -20, replies with L2.eng group 177.

functions.name: Diplo_ReplyAllianceOffer
functions.comment: Kind 3. Refuses with group 196 if already at war, 197 if I already have an ally, 178 otherwise; accepts with 179 and Diplo_FormAlliance. Accepts outright at standing >= 11, refuses outright below -10, and in between rolls g_rand7B < standing*3 + 45 out of 128. Accept +4, plain refusal -2, 'cannot' refusal -1.

functions.name: Diplo_ReplyAllianceEnd
functions.signature: void Diplo_ReplyAllianceEnd(unsigned int me, unsigned int them)
functions.comment: Kind 4. Breaks the alliance and takes standing -15. Sends no message at all - terminating an alliance from the diplomacy screen is silent. Group 182 'Broken alliance.' comes from Diplo_Offend instead, when an act rather than a letter breaks one.

functions.name: Diplo_ReplyHelpRequest
functions.signature: void Diplo_ReplyHelpRequest(int me, unsigned int them, unsigned int county)
functions.comment: Kind 5. Refuses with group 183 (+1 grudge) unless they are my ally, my gold is at least personality +0x30, and standing is at least 10; then g_rand7B < standing*4 accepts with group 184 and marches for free, otherwise group 185 demands personality[+0x0C] * pair.helpPriceMultiple gold.

functions.name: Diplo_ReplyAttackRequest
functions.signature: void Diplo_ReplyAttackRequest(int me, unsigned int them, unsigned int county)
functions.comment: Kind 6, identical in shape to Diplo_ReplyHelpRequest but with groups 186/187/188, a +2 grudge on refusal and half the acceptance odds (g_rand7B < standing*2).

functions.name: Ai_FarmStyleNeutralArable
functions.comment: Farming style 0 for an UNOWNED county - AI_ManageFields(0) only, and no AI realm can reach it. Gives the county 100 crowns of its own purse (+0x1F4) if it is short of grain, buys grain in lots of 400/200/100/50 until it holds 100 sacks, zeroes industrySharePct, takes Labour_DefaultSharesBuilt, sets rations searching the split downward from 100 if the herd is over 100 and upward from 0 otherwise, clears every pasture, and in Winter plants grain on half the county (total-3 with Advanced Farming off). One pasture is kept if the herd is over 10. [V] Its only caller is AI_ManageFields at 0x0049DFC6.

functions.name: Ai_FarmStyleNeutralGrazing
functions.comment: Farming style 1 for an UNOWNED county. Buys 10 cattle if the herd is under 11 and grain in lots of 400/200/100/50 to 100 sacks, zeroes industrySharePct, takes Labour_DefaultSharesBuilt, sets rations with the upward split search, clears every grain field WHATEVER THE SEASON and grows the pasture towards total-1 through FUN_004A4694. [V] Its only caller is AI_ManageFields at 0x0049DFC6.

functions.name: Ai_FarmStyleArable
functions.comment: Farming style 0 for an AI REALM - the one Ai_ManageCountyFarms dispatches, which no earlier note distinguished from 0x004A3C67. Runs Ai_TradeForCounty first, tops the granary up to 600 sacks with lots of 400/200/100 and to 100 with lots of 50/25, sets industrySharePct to 50 - the highest of the five styles - takes Labour_DefaultSharesBuilt, sets rations, clears every pasture, and in Winter plants grain on half the county (total-1 with Advanced Farming off). One pasture is kept if the herd is over 10.

functions.name: Ai_FarmStyleGrazing
functions.comment: Farming style 1 for an AI REALM. Runs Ai_TradeForCounty, buys 10 cattle if the herd is under 41 - the only style that stocks forty rather than ten - and one lot of 400 grain if under 100 sacks, sets industrySharePct to 20, takes Labour_DefaultSharesBuilt, sets rations, clears every grain field in every season and grows the pasture towards total-1 through FUN_004A4694. Plants no grain at all, ever.

functions.name: Ai_FarmStyleMixed
functions.comment: Farming style 9 for an AI REALM, and the only style that farms both. Runs Ai_TradeForCounty, buys 10 cattle under 11 head and grain in lots of 800/400/200/100/50/25 up to 300 sacks - the longest shopping list of the five and the only one offering 800 - sets industrySharePct to 40, takes Labour_DefaultSharesBuilt, sets rations, plants grain on a third of the county in Winter (half with Advanced Farming off) and grows the pasture towards a third through FUN_004A4694. Ends on estimate/allocate with no closing estimate, where the other four run estimate/allocate/estimate.

functions.name: Ai_FitCattleFields
functions.comment: Nudges a county pasture count by one, in whichever direction the herd crowding meter asks for: under 11 it gives a field back, but only with more than two pastures and fewer than ten animals; at 11 or over it takes one more, up to cap. Both limbs clear every pasture and re-lay the whole count, then County_RecountFields and Herd_UpdateCrowding. The else-if re-tests 10 < crowding, which the first branch already implies.

functions.name: Ai_SetRations
functions.comment: The AI ration setter. rationWanted comes from a ladder on FUN_0044E6A3 (herd*5 + herd*10 + grain*6, the STORES, not Food_Available caps) against the people to feed: under half of them None, under them Quarter, under twice Half, then two rungs on dairy alone and two on the store, else Normal. [D] The two dairy rungs sit above the two store rungs and, because the store counts the herd twice, the Triple dairy rung can never change an answer and the Double one can only lower it - a cattle county is fed Double where a grain county with the same food is fed Triple. Then rationSplit: mode 0 sweeps 0..100 upward and mode 100 sweeps 100..0 downward, each keeping the split with the best rationAchieved on a strict improvement, so the two modes take the opposite end of a tie; any other mode is used as the split unchanged.

functions.name: Ai_SellGood
functions.signature: void Ai_SellGood(uint county, int qty, int good)
functions.comment: The selling half of Ai_BuyGood: same stall and morale markup, then Merchant_Trade with a negative quantity. Used by Ai_TradeForCounty to dump wood, iron and stone above the lord personality reserves.

functions.name: Ai_BuyGood
functions.signature: void Ai_BuyGood(uint county, int qty, int good)
functions.comment: One AI purchase from the county merchant stall: refuses unless the county has a stall (+0x1A4), prices the good at the stall price plus the merchant unit morale as a percentage markup (good 4, ale, carries no markup), and calls Merchant_Trade only if the purse covers it - the realm treasury for an owned county, county +0x1F4 for an unowned one. The farming styles call it repeatedly with falling lot sizes, re-reading the stock between calls, so a lot that arrives ends the cascade and one refused lets the next be tried.

functions.name: Ai_BuyGoodDownTo
functions.signature: void Ai_BuyGoodDownTo(uint county, int qty, int good)
functions.comment: As Ai_BuyGood but walks the price down until the purse covers the lot instead of refusing outright.

functions.name: Units_AnyMovingOfKindForRealm
functions.comment: As Units_AnyMovingOfKind but also requires owner == realm and ownerIsHuman == 0, and calls Siege_Break on any type-1 unit it starts. Two callers: turn phase 5's wait, as (2, 6) - so the phase waits only on realm 6's ownerless mobs - and the AI turn's finish test, as (1, realm), which is why a realm with armies still walking keeps stepping past its aiStep threshold. Promoted from the hypothesis Unit_AbandonOrders, whose name had it backwards: it starts orders, it does not abandon them.

functions.name: Units_AnyMovingOfKind
functions.comment: The wait predicate for turn phases 3 and 6. Walks slots 1..150 and, for every unit of this kind with moving != 0, sets moving = 2 and returns 1. It is not a read-only query: it promotes 'ordered' (1) to 'stepping' (2) as well as reporting that the phase is still busy, so one call both starts a phase's units and waits on them.

functions.name: Levy_EquipSlot
functions.comment: Moves min(unequipped men, weapons remaining in that basket slot) from basket slot 0 into slot 1..6 - it arms as many still-unarmed levies with that one weapon type as the stock allows. Called five times by 0x004A5389 in the order 5, 1, 3, 2, 6: bows, crossbows, swords, maces, mail. Pikes, slot 4, are never issued by that path.

functions.name: Castle_RaiseFreeGarrison
functions.comment: The garrison a finished castle comes with. archers = g_castleFreeArchers[castleType-1], minus g_castleFreeArchers[castleBuilding-1] when castleBuilding != 0 - so an upgrade yields only the DIFFERENCE and a motte-and-bailey to a Norman keep yields nothing. Refuses when that is <= 0 or above population/2. Otherwise clears the realm's levy basket, adds the archers to realm.weapons[4] so they cost nothing, writes them into basket slot 5 (archers) and slot 7 (the total), and calls Army_Create. Its one caller is Castle_BuildTick, which passes the result to Army_GarrisonApply.

functions.name: Ai_AdvanceArmies
functions.comment: AI turn step 11. Walks slots 1..150 and, for every type-1 unit of this realm whose mission handler (Ai_RunMission, 0x004A57AC) returns non-zero, clears +0x14E, floods from the unit in mode 0 and re-paths it to destX/destY. Byte for byte the same shape as the verified PeasantMob_AdvanceAll. Note mode 0: the AI driver does NOT prefer roads, though Unit_OrderMove does.

functions.name: Ai_RunMission
functions.comment: Dispatches on unit +0x1A, the AI mission byte: 7 to 0x004A58F4, 6 to 0x004A599D, 2 to 0x004A5B1F, 3 to 0x004A5F0A, 4 to 0x004A6270, 5 to 0x004A60B9, and anything else rewrites +0x1A to 2 and returns 0. Non-zero means the handler wrote destX/destY and wants a fresh path. docs/armies.md section 10 has the enum; this closes +0x1A, which docs/armies.md section 1.5 had as a UI feedback code.

functions.name: Ai_MissionRaid
functions.comment: Mission 7. Unless the unit is besieging (+0x199), re-aims it at the nearest STANDING CROP of its destCounty via Ai_FindStandingCropTile and clears needsDestination. It is re-aimed every turn, which is what makes a fifty-man unarmed raiding party destructive: Unit_TrampleTile fires on every field it crosses in a county it does not own.

functions.name: Ai_MissionAssistAlly
functions.comment: Mission 6. Re-validates unit +0x19B, the ally-help target county, through 0x0049FF71; a cancelled request demotes the unit to mission 2 and runs that handler in the SAME tick. Otherwise it closes on the nearest enemy army in that county, but only within Chebyshev 21 - outside that it does nothing at all this turn.

functions.name: Ai_MissionSeekEnemy
functions.comment: Mission 2, the default war mission and the one every unrecognised value becomes. Four arms in order: intercept an enemy army within Chebyshev 6 (tie-break: the more westerly gives chase, and an army already on mission 2 is not chased); keep the standing destCounty if it is still hostile and still borders the realm; else pick a new target with 0x004A0649; else attack the county it is standing in. Two defects: the last arm never updates destCounty, and an ally-owned county with no alternative aims the army at county 0. It also calls 0x00467F2E and discards the result - the two arms it was written to choose between are identical.

functions.name: Ai_MissionHoldHome
functions.comment: Mission 3. Intercepts the nearest attackable army in the unit homeCounty (+0x11) within Chebyshev 31 - five times mission 2 radius - and otherwise walks back to that county. Always returns 1 unless besieging. Its only setter is 0x0049F431, which overwrites homeCounty with the realm muster county on the abandon branch, so home means posted-to rather than raised-in.

functions.name: Ai_MissionGarrisoned
functions.comment: Mission 5, which Army_GarrisonApply writes. Does nothing while destCounty still belongs to the unit owner. Once the county is lost the garrison is ejected (0x00437535) and demoted to mission 2, and in the one case where the castle is still standing and unruined it is also sent at the county town to take it back.

functions.name: Ai_MissionJoinGarrison
functions.comment: Mission 4. Re-checks that the target castle has room for the WHOLE army (g_castleGarrisonCap tested against the unit men plus the sitting garrison), is standing, is not under construction and still belongs to the realm; failing any of those it looks for another castle with room (0x004A07F2) and disbands the army if there is none. Returns 1 even after Army_Disband, so the caller then floods from a record Army_Destroy has already cleared.

functions.name: Ai_AimAtCounty
functions.comment: The choice missions 2 and 3 make between the two county tiles: a county with no castle, or a castle with no garrison, is entered at the TOWN (Ai_FindTownTile); anything else is approached at the CASTLE (Ai_FindCastleBuildingTile), which begins a siege. L2.eng group 286 states the same rule to the player.

functions.name: Ai_FindCastleBuildingTile
functions.comment: The tile of the county carrying plane-0 0x80 with terrain 0x15..0x19 - the five BUILT castle types, excluding the 0x14 plot - nearest by Manhattan distance to the unit; falls back to the stored castle tile at county +0x74/+0x75. Stepping onto the result runs Unit_ReachCastleBuilding: Army_Garrison when the county is the mover own, Army_BeginSiege when it is not.

functions.name: Ai_FindTownTile
functions.comment: The tile of the county carrying plane-0 0x40 - the county TOWN, not the castle - nearest by Manhattan distance to the unit, into g_foundTileX/Y; falls back to the county anchor at +0x6C/+0x6D. Distinct from County_FindTownTile (0x00467FD1), which finds the same bit once at map load to place that anchor. Stepping onto the result runs Army_AttackCounty. Ties go to the lowest tile offset, and offset 0 doubles as not-found, so tile (0,0) can never be returned.

functions.name: Ai_FindStandingCropTile
functions.comment: The tile of the county carrying plane-0 0x20 with terrain 3..22 - a standing crop or a pasture, excluding wild and fallow - nearest by Manhattan distance to the unit; falls back to the county anchor. This is what the AI raiding party (mission 7) is aimed at, which is why a raid damages the harvest.

functions.name: Battle_ChooseSettlement
functions.comment: Decides which of three ways a battle is settled, and is called by all three battle entries (Army_AttackCounty, the army-versus-army path FUN_004A7158, and Siege_LaunchAssault). Returns 0 when NEITHER side's ownerIsHuman is set - an AI-versus-AI battle is autocalculated with no screen at all. Otherwise it returns 1, sets g_battleBothHuman when both sides are human, records which player owns the take-the-field choice in g_battleChoiceOwner, and copies both owners and shields for the screens; each caller then tests (g_optFightHumansOnly == 0 && !bothHuman) to autocalc straight to the report screen 0x13, or pushes the prompt screen 0x12 and asks. There is no distance test, no army-size cutoff and no separate quick-battle toggle on this path.

functions.name: Battle_BeginFromCampaign
functions.comment: The army-versus-army battle entry, and the third caller of Battle_ChooseSettlement. Reached from Unit_EnterOccupiedTile when an army steps onto a tile held by a realm Diplo_ActionAllowed permits attacking. Sets g_battleIsSiege = 0, g_battleCounty from the OCCUPANT's county, g_battleArmyA = mover, g_battleArmyB = occupant, and clears both sides' battle scratch fields. Returns 1 only when an interactive battle screen was opened (g_screenId = 0x12); the caller then sets g_battleStartedLatch and puts back the waypoint the step consumed. Otherwise it auto-resolves through Battle_AutoResolve and Battle_ReturnToCampaign and returns 0. This is the campaign side of the seam: Army_AttackCounty and Siege_LaunchAssault are the other two ways into the same machinery.

functions.name: County_ChangeOwner
functions.comment: Hands a county to a new realm: recomputes the taker's totals, raises one of the nine "we have taken" / "we have lost" letters (L2.eng 0x72..0x7E, chosen on the taker's county count and share of the map), calls Realm_RecountStrength on the OLD owner, writes the new owner, and docks the county happiness by the conquest penalty. [V] The recount happens one statement before the owner is written, so the county being lost is still counted and the losing realm cannot be eliminated here - it survives until its own AI_RunTurnStep step 0.

functions.name: Army_Garrison
functions.comment: Puts an army inside a county's castle: checks the combined men against the garrison cap for the castle type, writes county +0x1BC and unit +0x198, moves the unit onto the castle tile and charges 5 moves. Over the cap it sets unit +0x1A to 2 and refuses.

functions.name: Army_GarrisonConfirm
functions.comment: Yes-callback of the confirmation Army_Garrison stashes its arguments for: restores g_screenId from g_screenIdSaved and runs Army_GarrisonApply, or sends network command 0x34 under g_multiplayer. Its twin one function later does the same for a siege with command 0x35, and that pairing is how those two opcodes are identified.

functions.name: Army_GarrisonApply
functions.comment: The body Army_Garrison, its confirm-dialog callback and two other call sites all funnel into; Army_Garrison itself only stashes the arguments. Over g_castleGarrisonCap[castleType] it writes unit +0x1A = 2 and refuses; otherwise it links county +0x1BC and unit +0x198, teleports the unit onto the castle tile (county +0x74/+0x75), charges 5 moves and writes unit +0x1A = 5. An already-garrisoned castle takes Army_Combine instead. battle-before.sav slot 4 is a garrison and carries +0x1A = 5 at exactly county 2's +0x74/+0x75, which is the data-side confirmation docs/armies.md section 1.5 wanted for +0x1A.

functions.name: Army_BeginSiege
functions.comment: Starts a siege if the county has a garrison, its castle is not under construction and it is not already besieged. Opens screen 0x1D for a human owner.

functions.name: Army_BeginSiegeConfirm
functions.comment: Yes-callback for 'Besiege castle?': Siege_Link, or network command 0x35 under g_multiplayer.

functions.name: Siege_Link
functions.comment: Sets unit +0x199 to the besieged county and the garrison's +0x19A back to the besieger, then runs Siege_Prepare.

functions.name: Siege_Prepare
functions.comment: Clears the three siege-engine build records at +0x182. For an AI owner it also hard-codes the order from the lord's personality record at 0x004D8AF8: two towers by default, or four towers, one ram, or three catapults plus a late ram against a large castle.

functions.name: Siege_RecomputeBuildTime
functions.comment: Recomputes each engine record's percent complete from work done over g_siegeEngineWork[e] times the count, and writes ceil(remaining work / men) into +0x19C - the seasons the siege preparation screen prints.

functions.name: Siege_StartPhase
functions.comment: Start of turn phase 2: breaks garrison and besieger links that no longer agree, then re-prepares every besieging army.

functions.name: Siege_ValidateLink
functions.comment: Clears unit +0x199 when the besieged county no longer has a garrison, or when that garrison is no longer garrisoned in that county, and counts the survivors into g_siegeCount. Run over every besieging army by Siege_StartPhase, and once more by Map_Click before it decides whether clicking your own army opens its move order or the siege-preparation screen. This corrects the existing comment on Siege_StartPhase, which says it 're-prepares every besieging army': it never calls Siege_Prepare, it breaks stale links.

functions.name: Siege_TickPhase
functions.comment: Turn phase 2's pump. Walks the resumable cursor g_siegeCursor from 1 to 150 calling Siege_BuildTick, and returns 1 the moment one reports its engines finished - leaving the cursor where it is, so the turn machine can run Siege_LaunchAssault on that unit and resume afterwards. Returns 0 when the sweep is exhausted. Siege_StartPhase seeds the cursor with 1.

functions.name: Siege_BuildTick
functions.comment: One season of siege-engine construction: spreads the army's men evenly over the incomplete engine types, spills the remainder onto whichever is still short, and returns 1 when +0x19C reaches 0.

functions.name: Siege_LaunchAssault
functions.comment: Turn phase 2's payoff. Sets g_battleCounty from the besieger's +0x199, works out the castle level to fight (castleDegraded 1 with a build in progress -> castleBuilding-1; castleDegraded 2 -> county +0x1F9; else castleType-1), sums the three siege-engine counts at unit +0x182 + e*6, and fights only when the level is below 3 OR at least one engine was built. Otherwise message 0x119 - L2.eng group 281, 'Cannot siege castle' / 'Your captains advise that you must build some siege engines to besiege this castle.' - and Siege_Break lifts the siege. The engine offset closes: 0x52F232 minus g_units 0x52F0B0 is 0x182, stride 6, three records.

functions.name: Map_SelectUnitForMove
functions.comment: Points g_moveTargetX/Y at the selected unit's own tile and calls Move_ResetSelection, so a freshly selected unit starts with a zero-length path rather than inheriting the previous unit's.

functions.name: Map_HoverUnitTarget
functions.comment: Runs the campaign pathfinder to the tile under the cursor and collects what a click there would do. When moveAllowance minus movesUsed is less than the path distance it zeroes every collected target, so an out-of-range click does nothing.

functions.name: Path_MarkPreviewTiles
functions.comment: Sets bit 0x40 of byte +2 of every runtime tile record along the local player's path buffer. Map_DrawPathMarker draws the gold path balls on exactly those tiles.

functions.name: Map_ConfirmMoveOrder
functions.comment: Clicking a destination for the selected unit. Saves g_screenId into g_screenIdSaved, then picks at most one confirmation from the targets Map_HoverUnitTarget collected, in this priority: g_hoverVillageCounty -> dialog 4 'Slaughter villagers?'; g_hoverFieldCounty -> 10 'Destroy field?'; g_hoverMergeUnit -> 5 'Combine armies?'; g_hoverGarrisonCounty -> 7 'Garrison castle?'; g_hoverSiegeCounty -> 8 'Besiege castle?'; otherwise no dialog and the order goes straight through. Those numbers are indices into L2.eng group 10, which is how each of the six hover globals can be named from the text the game puts on screen when it is set. Does nothing unless g_moveOrderAvailable is 1.

functions.name: MoveOrder_ConfirmGarrison
functions.comment: The 'Garrison castle?' callback, and five L2.eng strings pin its five branches one for one. Castle under construction -> 0xA4 = 164 'This castle is undergoing construction work'; county +0x1C2 set -> 0xA5 = 165 'You cannot station men in a ruined castle'; g_castleGarrisonCap[castleType] minus the sitting garrison below 1 -> 0x11B = 283 'Castle fully barracked'; below the incoming army -> 0xA6 = 166, which offers to SPLIT the army (166/2..4 read 'Your army contains' / 'more troops can be stationed here.' / 'Do you want to split your army?', a mechanic nothing in the docs records); both armies carrying mercenaries -> 0xA7 = 167. A garrison that is itself besieged refuses ahead of all of them with 0x121 = 289, 'You cannot send men into this castle my lord. As it is currently under siege !!'

functions.name: MoveOrder_ConfirmSiege
functions.comment: The 'Besiege castle?' callback. No garrison and castleDegraded 0 -> message 0x11D = L2.eng 285, 'This castle is deserted my liege. Your enemies await you in the county town.'; no garrison and degraded -> 0x11C = 284, 'This castle is under construction my liege.'; the garrison already besieged -> 0x113 = 275, 'Your captains advise that other troops already lay siege to this castle. You must join with or dispose of the existing siegers.' - which is exactly the siege-link migration Army_Combine implements. Otherwise Unit_OrderMove, or network command 0x29.

functions.name: MoveOrder_ConfirmCombine
functions.comment: The 'Combine armies?' callback, and the third independent sighting of the 1500 cap: it tests the two armies' men against 0x5DD before the order is issued at all, and otherwise sends message 0x112 = L2.eng 274, 'The resulting army would be over their recommended limit of 1500 troops.' It is the only caller that passes a non-zero fifth argument to Unit_OrderMove, and what it passes is g_hoverMergeUnit - so unit +0x152, which docs/armies.md section 1.2 lists as an untraced 'orderMode', is the unit index to merge into on arrival. Network command 0x2C rather than 0x29.

functions.name: MoveOrder_Confirm
functions.comment: The plain move-order callback, and also the no-dialog path. Refuses with message 0x11E - L2.eng 286, 'This shire contains a garrisoned castle my lord. We must lay siege to that, to gain control of the county.' - when g_hoverCountyTownCounty names a county whose castle holds a garrison. That is the user-facing half of Army_AttackCounty's siege gate, stated in the game's own words. Otherwise Unit_OrderMove, or network command 0x29 under g_multiplayer.

functions.name: Unit_OrderMove
functions.comment: Gives a unit a destination: rebuild the cost map, flood-fill from the unit, extract the path, copy it into the record, set moveState = 2 and the destination x/y.
functions.signature: void Unit_OrderMove(int who, int unit, int x, int y, char mode)

functions.name: Army_Create
functions.comment: Spawns a type-1 unit on a free road or open tile of the county and fills it from the levy basket: men to +0x168, slots 0..6 to +0x16C, the year to +0x164, the county's happiness to +0x166 as morale, a name from Army_PickName, optionally a mercenary band; then debits happiness and county +0x15 and sets the county levy surcharge +0x2F4 to 15.
functions.signature: int Army_Create(int realm, int county, int hireMercs, int happinessCost)

functions.name: Levy_ConsumeWeapons
functions.comment: Subtracts each levy basket slot 1..6 from the realm's matching weapon stock, then re-runs the labour allocator.

functions.name: Levy_DebitPopulation
functions.comment: Subtracts the levy total from county +0x24 (population) and +0x38 (the army line on the population panel).

functions.name: Army_PickName
functions.comment: Picks the least-used of the realm's 24 army-name slots at realm +0x2D and adds 2 to its counter. The names are L2.eng groups 94..98, 24 per lord.

functions.name: Army_Destroy
functions.comment: Frees an army: releases its garrison or siege link, decrements its name-slot counter, clears the unit record and recomputes the realm's wage bill.

functions.name: Army_Combine
functions.comment: Merges one army into another when the combined men are under 1501 and at most one of them carries mercenaries (otherwise message 0xA7, L2.eng 167). Sums men, the seven troop counts and the three siege-engine records, and keeps the HIGHER movesUsed - both arms of the if select the maximum, so a reinforcement can never buy back movement. It also migrates the siege link: the survivor inherits whichever of the two was besieging and the besieged garrison's +0x19A is repointed at it, which is what L2.eng 275 means by 'You must join with or dispose of the existing siegers.' The earlier 'keeps the lower movesUsed' here was wrong and was corrected in docs/armies.md section 2.7 without being corrected here.

functions.name: Army_PrepareForBattle
functions.comment: Fills the battle-only troop slots just before a battle: mode 4 copies the three siege-engine counts into +0x17A/+0x17C/+0x17E (troop types 7, 8, 9); mode 0 sets +0x180 (oil, type 10) to 1, 2, 3, 4 or 6 by castle type 1..5.

functions.name: Army_ClearBattleSlots
functions.comment: Zeroes the battle-only troop slots +0x17A, +0x17C, +0x17E and +0x180 after a battle.

functions.name: Levy_Seed
functions.comment: The PLAYER's levy-basket seeding; Levy_Init (0x004AAA80) is the AI's. Byte for byte the same seeding plus three UI resets: g_armourySelectedType = 0, the walking-soldier flag DAT_005679D0 = 0, and _DAT_0057C8E4 = 0. Zeroes all eight slots' chosen and available, sets slots 1..6 available and remaining from realm +0x140 + (t-1)*4, and puts the levied headcount in slot 0 and slot 7. Reads the realm out of county +0x05, the owner, rather than taking it as an argument. [V] Called by Sidebar_Button, by RaiseArmy_Continue and by the 0x17 right-release arm - every door into the armoury.

functions.name: Levy_Init
functions.comment: Zeroes the realm's 8-slot levy basket, seeds slots 1..6 with the realm's weapon stockpiles (realm +0x140 + (t-1)*4) and puts the levied headcount in slot 0 (unequipped peasants) and slot 7 (the total).

functions.name: Battle_AutoResolve
functions.comment: The autocalc - the whole of a battle nobody watches, and one of only two ways a battle can end. Clears g_battleWithdrawal, takes both sides' Army_StrengthScore, multiplies the DEFENDER's by 160/200/250/320/400 per cent by castle level on a siege, forms ratio = PctOf(larger, smaller) and reads a survival percentage out of the ten-pair ladder g_autocalcSurvivalLadder (default 100). The winner is A unless strengthA < strengthB, so a TIE GOES TO THE ATTACKER. The winner keeps Pct(count, p) of each of its seven troop counts and of its mercenary band and has +0x168 rebuilt by summing rather than scaling; the loser's seven counts are zeroed, its band released and its total set to 0. Reproduces battle-after.sav exactly: 926 against 1044 is a ratio of 112, the ladder's second rung is 20 per cent, and 20 per cent of 122 peasants and 60 archers is the 36 men county 3's population gains back.

functions.name: Army_StrengthScore
functions.comment: Sum of troops[t] times g_troopStrengthWeight[t] over the seven campaign troop types plus the mercenary band, plus 20 when non-zero.

functions.name: Battle_ReturnToCampaign
functions.comment: Applies a battle result to the campaign. CORRECTED: g_battleLoser holds the WINNER, and this function is one of four sites that say so. The two branches are not mirror images. A wins: the county changes hands (County_ChangeOwner) if the loser was a garrison OR carried the +0x167 defence mark, the county's garrisonUnit is cleared, and the winner is charged +8 moves and then, if its owner is NOT human (+0x01 == 0 is the AI), set to moveAllowance - 1. B wins: the county NEVER changes hands - there is no County_ChangeOwner in that branch at all - only the attacker's garrison link is cleared, and only an AI winner pays, +7, while a winning human pays nothing. Either way the loser is destroyed and Diplo_Offend takes 20 off the loser's realm. ALSO CORRECTED: the 'except under autocalc, an army left with 50 or more men only has its siege lifted' rule this entry used to carry is wrong. Its gate is g_battleWithdrawal, which Battle_AutoResolve clears as its first statement; the flag is raised only by UnitOrder_SiegeAttKnight, so that path is a siege withdrawal and under autocalc the loser is always destroyed. See docs/decisions.md C31.

functions.name: Defence_Disband
functions.comment: Undoes a county defence after the battle, keyed on unit +0x167. Mark 1 (raised on the spot): the survivors go back into the home county's population and popArmy and the unit is destroyed. Mark 2 (an existing army pressed into the role): the mark is cleared and the army stays. Verified against the battle fixture triple - battle-during.sav slot 6 is the raised defence (owner 6, mark 1, 182 men) and county 3's population falls 728 to 582 across before/after, which is the 182 levied minus 36 survivors returned. That makes docs/armies.md section 8.1's [D] reading of +0x167 a data-side [V].

functions.name: Unit_EnterCounty
functions.comment: Called when a unit crosses a county border: sets +0x10, fires County_GreetArmy for a neutral county, and for an owned one sends message 0xAA (L2.eng group 170, the sixteen invasion taunts) when that county is the unit's declared destination.

functions.name: County_GreetArmy
functions.comment: Picks a neutral county's reaction to an army entering: happiness below 10 -> msg 0x82, below 30 -> 0x83, otherwise by the army as a percentage of the county population - 100 or more -> 0x83, 50..99 -> 0x84, 20..49 -> 0x85, under 20 -> 0x86 (L2.eng group 134, the border-violation message). The bigger the army the politer the reply.

functions.name: County_RaiseRevolt
functions.comment: What unrest 4 does. Finds a free road tile, or failing that a free open tile, spawns a kind-2 unit - revolting peasants - of 30% of the county's population at morale 50 with no shield, takes those people out of the population, and calls County_MakeIndependent. Returns 0 and leaves the unrest counter alone if there is nowhere to put the mob, so a county with no free tile can sit at unrest 4 indefinitely. All 30% land in troops[0], the peasant slot.

functions.name: County_MakeIndependent
functions.comment: Takes a county away from whoever holds it: owner = 0, +0x07 = 0, the +0x07 byte of all four industry records = 0 (every industry switched off), +0x1B0 = 0, then Labour_Allocate / Ration_Apply / County_RefreshEstimates / Tax_RecomputePreview to bring the county back to a consistent state, and hands any garrison to FUN_00437535. [V] Three callers that arrived independently all mean the same thing and all agree: Territory_SecedeMinorBlocks (the county is cut off), County_RaiseRevolt (the peasants rose), and Realm_Eliminate (the realm is gone).

functions.name: PeasantMob_AdvanceAll
functions.comment: Turn phase 5, step 1. For every type-2 unit, calls PeasantMob_PickDestination and, if it succeeds, flood-fills (mode 0, no road preference), extracts the path and sets moving = 1.

functions.name: PeasantMob_PickDestination
functions.comment: Picks a mob's destination from g_mobCountyCursor, a single counter shared by every mob: bump it, wrap past g_countyCount back to 1, and bump once more if it names the county the mob is standing in - so consecutive mobs go to consecutive counties and a mob is never sent where it already is. Re-targets only when g_season == 2 or destCounty == 0. Note the destination coordinates are read from the cursor's county while destCounty is the unit's own field, so outside season 2 a mob that kept its old destCounty walks to a different county's anchor than the one it believes it is going to.
