globals.comment: The HCURSOR Cursor_Set last passed to SetCursor. Written and read nowhere else.

globals.name: g_cursorRing
globals.comment: HCURSOR for RT_GROUP_CURSOR 104, an empty ring drawn in the top-left 19x19 of a 32x32 bitmap, hotspot (9, 9). Cursor_Set's kind 6 - one of your own figures is under the pointer.

globals.name: g_cursorArrow
globals.comment: HCURSOR for RT_GROUP_CURSOR 105, the plain arrow pointer. Cursor_Set's kind 0 and its default.

globals.name: g_frameRateSeconds
globals.comment: How many whole seconds Frame_Tick has measured. Forced to 1 by App_LogExit before the division, so a run shorter than a second does not divide by zero.

globals.name: g_cursorQuestion
globals.comment: HCURSOR for RT_GROUP_CURSOR 110, an arrow corner with a QUESTION MARK beside it, hotspot (0, 0). Cursor_Set's kind 2, and g_cursorByScreen gives it to screen 0x02 - the village, idle - and to the unreachable 0x0E. This is the pointer a player reported seeing in the town square. Its 304-byte payload is byte-identical to the shipped Cursor9.cur. It has nothing to do with the help screen 0x31 or the tip screens: those are separate mechanisms and the help screen's own row in g_cursorByScreen is 0.

globals.name: g_mouseLeftDoubleClick
globals.comment: A left DOUBLE click arrived this frame: (DAT_004EADA1 & 1), set by the window procedure on WM_LBUTTONDBLCLK (0x203). Windows counts the clicks, not the game. Read in exactly one place - Village_DoubleClick - and setting it also clears g_mouseClickPending, so the deferred single click never fires behind it.

globals.name: g_ddPrimary
globals.comment: The PRIMARY DirectDraw SURFACE - the front buffer, what the desktop shows. Renamed from g_ddrawInterface, which read as the IDirectDraw object; that is g_ddraw at 0x004E6974, and the two are used through different vtables. Every offset taken off this pointer is a documented IDirectDrawSurface slot: +0x14 Blt, +0x1C BltFast, +0x60 IsLost, +0x64 Lock, +0x6C Restore, +0x70 SetClipper, +0x7C SetPalette, +0x80 Unlock. It was NULL at the crash at 0x004522B5, which happened when the window was deactivated during startup under DxWnd - and the arm that would have re-acquired it is dead, see g_displayLost.

globals.name: g_mouseRightPressed
globals.comment: The right button went down this frame. Read five times in the binary and never to dismiss anything.

globals.name: g_cursorScythe
globals.comment: HCURSOR for RT_GROUP_CURSOR 113, an arrow corner with a SCYTHE beside it, hotspot (0, 0). Cursor_Set's kind 14, which g_cursorByScreen gives to screen 0x10 - the campaign map in army-movement mode, the screen Map_BeginMoveSelection opens.

globals.name: g_presentBudgetMs
globals.comment: Milliseconds accumulated since the last present, fed by Frame_Tick. Gfx_Present presents once it passes 0x31 and resets it to 0, which is a hard cap of one present per fifty milliseconds - twenty frames a second.

globals.name: g_mouseClickSettled
globals.comment: The pending left click stood for more than 300 ms without a second one, so it really was a single click. Village_ClickJob - the job popup - is gated on this and on nothing else, which is why that popup opens a fraction after the button comes up.

globals.name: g_mouseClickX
globals.comment: Where the pending click was released. Village_ClickJob reads this rather than the live pointer, so the popup opens on the cluster the button came up over.

globals.name: g_mouseClickY
globals.comment: The y of the same.

globals.name: g_screenHeight
globals.comment: 480. The vertical companion to g_screenStride, used as the bottom clip by every general blit.

globals.name: g_screenId
globals.comment: Which screen the interface is on. Screen_Draw, Screen_DrawWidgets and Screen_HandleInput all switch on it and nothing else does. The ids are listed in docs/screens-county.md section 1.

globals.name: g_cursorPeasant
globals.comment: HCURSOR for RT_GROUP_CURSOR 111, an arrow corner with a filled human figure - a head over a body - beside it, hotspot (0, 0). Cursor_Set's kind 12, which g_cursorByScreen gives to screen 0x06, the village while a selection of peasants is being carried.

globals.name: g_logBuffer
globals.comment: The line Log_Write assembles before Log_Append writes it. Each of its four contributors is capped at 100 bytes and there is no total bound, so a caller passing two long strings and a number overruns it; every shipped call site is well inside.

globals.name: g_ddBackBuffer
globals.comment: The back-buffer surface everything draws into, created by Display_CreateSurface(g_screenStride, g_screenHeight, 1) - system memory, because the game writes pixels with the CPU. Gfx_Present blits it to g_ddPrimary.

globals.name: g_mouseLeftPressed
globals.comment: The left button went DOWN this frame - the down edge of g_mouseLeftDown.

globals.name: g_cursorArrowAlt
globals.comment: A second HCURSOR loaded from the SAME resource as g_cursorArrow, RT_GROUP_CURSOR 105. Cursor_Set's kind 13, which g_cursorByScreen uses only for screen 0x07 - a screen no immediate store to g_screenId ever selects. An unfinished slot: a distinct kind that draws the default picture.

globals.name: g_screenStride
globals.comment: Screen stride, 640.

globals.name: g_logTimestamp
globals.comment: asctime's output, refreshed by Log_Timestamp before every line. Log_Write copies the first ten bytes of it - the weekday and the date, not the time.

globals.name: g_battleBothHuman
globals.comment: Set by Battle_ChooseSettlement when both armies' ownerIsHuman are set, and read at all three battle entries as the second half of (g_optFightHumansOnly == 0 && !bothHuman): the 'fight humans only' option never auto-resolves a battle between two people.

globals.name: g_formationClaimedCells
globals.comment: A 100-entry list of cell byte offsets already claimed during one Formation_AssignSearchedSlots pass, so two figures of a unit are never sent to the same cell.

globals.name: g_aiStrengthAdvantage
globals.comment: The AI's view of the battle, recomputed every 101 frames by Battle_UpdateStrengthAdvantage: weighted AI men as a percentage of weighted human men, minus 100, plus a -10..+21 jitter outside deterministic play. Every field and siege handler branches on it. It is one global for the whole battle, not per side and not per unit.

globals.name: g_menPerFigure
globals.comment: How many real soldiers one drawn figure stands for: 4, 8, 16, 32, 64, 128, 256, 512 or 1024 by size class. Reduced for a small army so that a side always gets at least 9 figures.

globals.name: g_tipShown
globals.comment: One 'already shown this game' byte per L2.eng group, set by Tip_Show and tested by Tip_Update. [V] FUN_00476A5D clears exactly 20 bytes from g_tipShown + 200, which fixes the tip-screen range at groups 200..219.

globals.name: g_pathSearchCount
globals.comment: Zeroed by Battle_Start, incremented once per flood fill actually run - that is, excluding the adjacent and clear-line early outs.

globals.name: g_moveDistOther
globals.comment: The same 64x64 i16 distance field, used for every realm that is not the local player.

globals.name: g_pathStepCost
globals.comment: Per-cell step cost the flood fill charges: a cell is only expanded once it has been reached this many times.

globals.name: g_moveCost
globals.comment: 64x64 i16 campaign movement cost map rebuilt each season by Move_BuildCostMap: 1 road, 3 open ground, 6 a standing field, 100 castle/settlement/plot, 0 impassable.

globals.name: g_pathVisitCount
globals.comment: How many times the flood fill has reached each cell, compared against g_pathStepCost.

globals.name: g_pathElevation
globals.comment: Per-cell elevation the flood fill and Path_Extract read; a step is only allowed between cells differing by at most 1.

globals.name: g_pathWaypoints
globals.comment: Scratch route built by Path_Extract: (x, y) byte pairs, at most 150, ordered destination-first. BattleMan_SetPath copies it into the figure.

globals.name: g_pathQueueTail
globals.comment: Write cursor of g_pathQueue; wraps at 0x1900.

globals.name: g_pathQueue
globals.comment: Pathfinder frontier, a circular queue of 0x1900 cell indices with head g_pathQueueHead and tail g_pathQueueTail.

globals.name: g_moveDistLocal
globals.comment: 64x64 i16 distance field for the local player, filled by Move_FloodFill and descended by Path_Extract. Map_DrawPathMarker uses its values as the path-ball sprite index.

globals.name: g_pathQueueHead
globals.comment: Read cursor of g_pathQueue.

globals.name: g_pathCost
globals.comment: Pathfinder cost field, u16 per battlefield cell, index y*80 + x. 0 means unvisited, 1 the start cell, 998 (0x3E6) blocked.

globals.name: g_pathFailCount
globals.comment: Zeroed by Battle_Start, incremented once per Path_Extract that returns no path. A ready-made diagnostic for how often the pathfinder is failing in a live battle.

globals.name: g_pathBlockedTemplate
globals.comment: The 80x80 u16 template Path_Search copies over g_pathCost before every search: 999 blocked, 0 free. Rebuilt by Path_BuildTerrainTemplate whenever the battlefield changes.

globals.name: g_battleStartedLatch
globals.comment: Set by Unit_EnterOccupiedTile when Battle_BeginFromCampaign opens an interactive battle. Units_Tick returns as soon as it is set, so units in higher slots do not move on that tick at all, and Unit_StepOnce returns 10 so no tile is entered and no movement is charged.

globals.name: g_dirtyTop
globals.comment: Top edge of the accumulated dirty box. WRITE-ONLY in the shipped binary: see Gfx_MarkDirty.

globals.name: g_dirtyBottom
globals.comment: Bottom edge of the accumulated dirty box, and the one the clamp gets wrong - Gfx_MarkDirty tests it against 0x27F and assigns 0x1DF. Write-only, so it never showed.

globals.name: g_dirtyLeft
globals.comment: Left edge of the accumulated dirty box. Write-only; see Gfx_MarkDirty.

globals.name: g_dirtyRight
globals.comment: Right edge of the accumulated dirty box. Write-only; see Gfx_MarkDirty.

globals.name: g_dirtyCount
globals.comment: How many more presents owe this change. Gfx_MarkDirty raises it to at least 1 and the sprite and map-view wrappers raise it to 2; Gfx_Present decrements it and presents only while it is positive. The ONLY part of the dirty-rectangle machinery that has an effect - the four edges are dead.

globals.name: g_netSendSlot
globals.comment: The g_netSendRing slot the next packet goes in, and the sequence number stamped into its +3. Net_SendCommand increments it after each command and resets it to 1 when it passes 0x27, so it cycles 1..39 and slot 0 of the forty-slot ring is never used. FUN_0043F01D, the session reset, writes it twice while opening a game. This wrap test is what fixes the ring's slot count.

globals.name: g_netSendCursor
globals.comment: Where the next byte of the packet payload goes. Net_SendCommand points it at g_netSendRing slot + 4 before calling the opcode's writer, and Net_WriteField appends through it and advances it - two sites, a writer and its reader, and nothing else touches it. The +4 is the same four header bytes the checksum at 0x00440038 skips.

globals.name: g_netSendRing
globals.comment: The outgoing packet ring Net_SendCommand builds into: FORTY slots of 0x104 bytes, 0x00512FB0..0x0051584F, of which the sequence counter g_netSendSlot uses only 1..39 - slot 0 is allocated and never written. The extent is arithmetic that closes exactly: 0x00512FB0 + 40 * 0x104 = 0x00515850, and 0x00515850 is the next address anything in the binary references - nothing at all is referenced between +0x104 and there. Slot layout: +0 opcode, +1 the declared payload length from g_netCmdLength, +2 a checksum, +3 the sequence number, which the triple-send path ORs with 0x40 and then 0x80 to mark the two duplicates; +4.. the payload, written through the cursor g_netSendCursor. The checksum at 0x00440038 sums length bytes starting at slot+4, and the sender is handed length+4 bytes from the slot base, so the four header bytes and the payload account for the whole packet. Settles a name recorded twice: the battle pass called this g_netSendRing and the campaign-map pass g_netPacketBuf, and they disagreed 39 against 40 because those are two different true counts - forty slots exist, thirty-nine are in rotation.

globals.name: g_netReadCursor
globals.comment: Where Net_ReadField takes the next bytes from. Net_ApplyPacket sets it to g_netRecvPacket + 4 before dispatching, mirroring g_netSendCursor on the writing side.

globals.name: g_netRecvPacket
globals.comment: The 0x104-byte receive buffer, the same size as one g_netSendRing slot. Byte 0 opcode, 1 length, 2 checksum, 3 sequence in the low six bits and a resend flag in the top two; the payload starts at +4, which is where Net_ApplyPacket points g_netReadCursor and exactly where Net_SendCommand starts writing.

globals.name: g_paletteWindowed
globals.comment: 256 PALETTEENTRYs for windowed mode. Indices 0..9 and 0xF6..0xFF are Windows' static system colours and are read back OUT of here into g_paletteRgb rather than written; only 10..0xF5 carry PC_RESERVED.

globals.name: g_paletteFullScreen
globals.comment: 256 PALETTEENTRYs for full-screen mode, where only index 0 and index 255 are reserved to the system and the other 254 are ours.

globals.name: g_smkPath
globals.comment: The 16-byte filename of the movie currently open. Smk_OnFinished strcmps against it to decide what to play next, which is how intro.smk chains to imptitle.smk and imptitle.smk to credits.smk.

globals.name: g_smkPlaying
globals.comment: A Smacker movie is on screen. Read through Smk_IsPlaying by Gfx_Present, which skips the present entirely while it is set, and by App_WndProc's WM_PAINT.

globals.name: g_troopsTable
globals.comment: The parsed TROOPS*.ENG table: short[35][2][5][11], row stride 0xDC, side stride 0x6E, difficulty stride 0x16. See docs/formats/eng.md and the correction in docs/battle.md.

globals.name: g_troopsAdvantage
globals.comment: The per-battle defensive advantage 0..10, one per TROOPS*.ENG row.

globals.name: g_musicChannelActive
globals.comment: i32 per streaming channel: whether it holds an open stream. Channel 0 is music, channel 1 a looping effect.

globals.name: g_musicChannelName
globals.comment: char[16] per streaming channel - the file name Music_Play copied in.

globals.name: g_rallyWaypoints
globals.comment: The field-battle rally waypoints Order_ToRallyWaypoint reads: two sides x two groups x three (x,y) int pairs, side 0 at 0x00522D30 and side 4 at 0x00522D60, group stride 0x18. Filled by Battlefield_BuildFromSkr and Battlefield_BuildRandom; on a .skr map all three of a group hold the same deployment marker cell.

globals.name: g_rankTrailer
globals.comment: The bottom-ranked realm: the last entry of g_rankTable that Score_RankRealms did not zero out. [V] See g_rankLeader - the two being equal is the game's victory condition, and it compares realm indices, not scores.

globals.name: g_strengthBand2
globals.comment: Band 2 threshold - 50% of a full figure.

globals.name: g_strengthBand3
globals.comment: Band 3 threshold - about 19-25% of a full figure.

globals.name: g_battleSizeClass
globals.comment: Battlefield size class 0..8, from the combined army size. It selects g_menPerFigure, the strength-band thresholds, and the burning-damage rate.

globals.name: g_aiRallyX
globals.comment: X of the enemy unit that attacked the melee unit which raised g_aiRallyRequest.

globals.name: g_aiRallyY
globals.comment: Y of the enemy unit that attacked the melee unit which raised g_aiRallyRequest.

globals.name: g_mapRotation
globals.comment: Map orientation, 0/2/4/6. Selects which of four projections Map_BuildLattice writes into g_screenLattice, and is subtracted from a unit facing to pick its sprite.

globals.name: g_tiles
globals.comment: Runtime tile array, 4096 records x 8 bytes in a 64x64 grid. Typed as struct Tile in docs/records.json - all eight bytes named, and every one of the 441 accesses in the binary is one byte wide (RecordProbe). The code indexes it by BYTE OFFSET, (y*64 + x)*8, so a step east is +8 and a step south is +0x200; Ghidra renders the two idioms as g_tiles[y*0x40 + x].county and (&g_tiles[0].county)[tileOffset]. See docs/formats/maps-layers.md 5.3.

globals.name: g_confirmX
globals.comment: Confirmation box origin x; the box itself is drawn 16 pixels up and left of it.

globals.name: g_confirmY
globals.comment: Confirmation box origin y.

globals.name: g_siegeCount
globals.comment: How many sieges survived Siege_StartPhase's link validation this turn. Zeroed there and incremented once per surviving besieger by Siege_ValidateLink.

globals.name: g_pickedTileUnit
globals.comment: The unit index on the tile Map_ResolvePick just resolved, out of the occupancy plane at g_tiles+5. Map_Click branches on its kind (1 army, 3 merchant) before it looks at the tile flags at all, and Panel_MoveButton and Panel_DisbandButton act on it.

globals.name: g_helpOptWidgetCount
globals.comment: Screen 0x31's widget count, written as 3 by the painter.

globals.name: g_mapViewX
globals.comment: Left edge of the map viewport in screen pixels: 0 at both live zooms (4 at the dead middle one).

globals.name: g_lastUnitIndex
globals.comment: Index of the unit Unit_Spawn just allocated. Callers read it straight after the call to fill in the rest of the record.

globals.name: g_minimapCounty
globals.comment: The 128x128 county id per minimap pixel, the companion raster in MAPnn.PL8. Minimap_Click indexes it as g_minimapCounty[(x-480) + (y-25)*128].

globals.name: g_otherBattleMan
globals.comment: Index of the other figure in the current interaction: the melee opponent, the missile target, or the figure being swapped with.

globals.name: g_countyTileTally
globals.comment: 32 dwords, one per county: how much of the viewport that county filled this frame. Map_DrawFrame seeds the current selection with 30 and then takes the maximum.

globals.name: g_units
globals.comment: Unit array, 151 records x 0x1A4 bytes, index 1..150 (0 unused); save block 5 is 63,420 bytes. Type at +0x08: 1 army, 2 revolting peasants, 3 merchant, 4 transport. Common: +0x00 owner, +0x07 sprite frame, +0x09 facing, +0x0A/+0x0B tile x/y, +0x0C tile offset, +0x10 county, +0x1C path length, +0x1D..+0x148 a 150-step (x,y) path, +0x14C move state, +0x14D on a road, +0x150 needs a destination, +0x151 destination county, +0x153 moves used, +0x154 move allowance (15 for an army, 10 otherwise). Army only: +0x11 home county, +0x14F army-name index into L2.eng group 93+owner, +0x155 starvation 0..5, +0x15C wages, +0x164 year formed, +0x166 morale, +0x168 total men, +0x16C+t*2 eleven i16 troop counts (0..6 campaign, 7..10 filled just before a battle), +0x182 three 6-byte siege-engine build records, +0x195/+0x196/+0x197 mercenary type/men/band, +0x198 garrison county, +0x199 besieged county, +0x19C siege seasons left. See docs/armies.md.

globals.name: g_strengthBand1
globals.comment: Men in a figure below which it drops to strength band 1 - 75% of a full figure.

globals.name: g_playerStartCount
globals.comment: Number of non-zero player start slots on the loaded map: 5, 4 or 2 across the shipped maps.

globals.name: g_mapViewCols
globals.comment: Lattice columns visible: 8 near, 40 far. The lattice is 65 wide, so neither zoom shows the whole map.

globals.name: g_alePreviewHappiness
globals.comment: The happiness Ale_PreviewGain says the pending ale purchase would give the selected county, already clamped by 5 minus county +0x219.

globals.name: g_curBattleMan
globals.comment: Index of the figure currently being updated. The whole figure state machine reads its subject from this global rather than from a parameter.

globals.name: g_battleIsSiege
globals.comment: Non-zero for a siege: selects the castle battlefield builder, the siege unit-order tables and Battle_RaiseSideSiege.

globals.name: g_messageGroup
globals.comment: The L2.eng group of the message currently on screen; 0 means none.

globals.name: g_bankMtns
globals.comment: Tile bank 0x04: Mtns1?.pl8 / Mtns2?.pl8.

globals.name: g_villani1Sheet
globals.comment: villani1.pl8, loaded by Village_Draw. Read by ONE blit in the whole executable - Village_Animate's iron-mine overlay, Pl8_DrawFrame(this, DAT_004D2938, 0xA4, top + 0xC). The file holds 21 frames of 40x62 and the counter wraps at 0x11, so three of them are never drawn.

globals.name: g_siegeBreachScore
globals.comment: Raised by the routine Missile_Step calls when a shot destroys a cell - once per orthogonal neighbour still of surface 5 - and by 4 when the drawbridge patch is laid. The siege-attacker handlers read non-zero as "there is a way in".

globals.name: g_villageDragCluster
globals.comment: The peasant cluster the rubber-band selection came from, 1-based; 0 for none.

globals.name: g_mapRedraw
globals.comment: Set alongside the map viewport's dirty rectangle by Gfx_MarkMapViewDirty and read in 55 places across the campaign, county and battle code. INFERRED as 'the map view needs repainting' from where it is set; its readers were not enumerated here.

globals.name: g_villageDropCluster
globals.comment: The cluster the drag was dropped on, 1-based.

globals.name: g_countyFieldTiles
globals.comment: 17 x 20 u32 tile indices - the map tiles that are this county's farm fields. Save block 12 is exactly 1360 bytes = 17 * 80.

globals.name: g_merchantHoverDamper
globals.comment: The merchant stall's hover throttle, and THIS is the damper a tooltip needs. Screen_Merchant sets it to 500 on entry; Merchant_HoverPlaque decrements it once per widget pass and swaps the price plaque only at zero, then sets it back to 500. So the plaque does not chase a moving pointer. It is screen 0x08's alone - there is no generic tooltip mechanism in this engine, and the merchant's mouseover is one function with one counter.

globals.name: g_troopCryCounter
globals.comment: i32 per (unit, event class) - the 0..3 round-robin Sound_PlayTroopCry steps before choosing a take.

globals.name: g_lastBattleMan
globals.comment: Index of the figure BattleMan_Create just allocated.

globals.name: g_battleMenA
globals.comment: Army A's living men, recomputed every frame by the figure census over troop types 0..6 only - so siege engines are worth no men and a side reduced to them has already lost. Battle_CheckOutcome ends the battle when it falls below 1, and the battle HUD draws it and g_battleMenB side by side, so the two numbers that decide a battle are the two numbers on the screen.

globals.name: g_scenarioIndex
globals.comment: The map slot, 0..59, used unshifted. Map_LoadLattice seeks slot * 0x80C1 (the whole slot stride), Eng_DrawString(101, g_scenarioIndex) indexes the 60 slot names in L2.eng group 101, and Minimap_Load takes the MAPnn.PL8 file from slot >> 2 and one of its four slots from slot & 3. An earlier note here said the low 2 bits select the season variant of the tile set: they do not - Gfx_LoadCountyMode takes the season from g_season.

globals.name: g_pathLen
globals.comment: Length in steps of each g_pathBuf entry, one byte per realm slot.

globals.name: g_gameOutcome
globals.comment: How the current game ended: 0 still in play, 10 won, 11 lost. [V] Cleared by Game_NewGame and by the static-resource loader; written in exactly one place during play, the category-0x0E arm of Msg_DrawWindow, which sets 10 for L2.eng group 225 and 11 for any other ending message whose subject realm is the local player. Every reader tests it against those two numbers.

globals.name: g_diploInbox
globals.comment: Six realms x five message slots x 8 bytes. Slot: +0x00 sender realm (0 terminates), +0x01 kind 0..6, +0x02 a county id for kinds 5 and 6, +0x04 gold for kind 0. Written only by Diplo_Post and drained by Diplo_AnswerInbox at AI step 1, so a message takes one turn to be answered.

globals.name: g_options
globals.comment: The persisted settings block: 0x468 bytes, fread/fwritten whole. Byte 0 begins a 31-byte player name defaulting to 'Player1'; +0x24 is a magic/version word (0x7EC = 2028) that Options_SetDefaults' second caller checks before trusting the file; +0x50 is g_optGameSpeed and +0x54 g_optScrollSpeed.

globals.name: g_optionsMagic
globals.comment: 0x7EC (2028), the settings-block version. 0x004AE2C3 compares against it and re-runs Options_SetDefaults when it does not match, which is how a settings file from another build is discarded.

globals.name: g_optSpeech
globals.comment: Sound options: speech on. Group 51 index 3, drawn as group 19 On/Off.

globals.name: g_optSoundEffects
globals.comment: Sound options: sound effects on. Group 51 index 2.

globals.name: g_optMusic
globals.comment: Sound options: music on. Group 51 index 1; turning it off stops the current track.

globals.name: g_optFullScreen
globals.comment: Display options: full screen. Group 52 index 2, Yes/No. The "(F5 key re-sizes window...)" line is drawn only while this is 0.

globals.name: g_desktopColours
globals.comment: Colours the desktop can show, computed in Display_Init as GetDeviceCaps(NUMCOLORS) x GetDeviceCaps(PLANES) and forced to 16 when NUMCOLORS returns -1. If it is not 8 the game switches itself to full-screen, because the windowed path needs a palettised desktop.

globals.name: g_optGameSpeed
globals.comment: Options > Game Speed. The slider dialog edits it with step 10 over 0..100 and displays it divided by ten. [V] It lives at +0x50 of the persisted settings block g_options, and its default is 90, written by Options_SetDefaults. A throttle at 0x004BBAC3 reads it with arithmetic exactly parallel to Map_ScrollThrottle's; [I] that this is what produces the main loop's ticksDue - the bytes were decoded, the link to the loop was not traced.

globals.name: g_optScrollSpeed
globals.comment: The Scroll Speed option, 0..100 in steps of ten, shown on the slider as 0..10. Map_ScrollThrottle turns it into a minimum interval of ((100-speed)/10)*12+2 ms; 0 disables scrolling. [V] The shipped default is 60 - 50 ms, 20 tiles a second - written by Options_SetDefaults. It sits at +0x54 of the persisted settings block g_options, and Menu_ScrollSpeed forms the pointer as g_options+0x54 rather than pushing the address, so a byte scan for readers misses the menu. Exactly two other references in .text: the default, and the sub inside the throttle. docs/decisions.md C59.

globals.name: g_optDifficulty
globals.comment: New-game difficulty 0..3 (easy/normal/hard/impossible, L2.eng group 103 indices 11..14). Scales AI gold, AI free resources and AI army wages.

globals.name: g_optAnimations
globals.comment: Display options: animations. Group 52 index 1, On/Off; Screen_BattleOutcome also branches on it for its animated variant.

globals.name: g_optTipScreens
globals.comment: Help options: tip screens. Group 45 index 1, Yes/No.

globals.name: g_optToolTips
globals.comment: Help options: tool tips. Group 45 index 2, Yes/No.

globals.name: g_campaignMap
globals.comment: How many maps of the current campaign have been won, and the row index into the campaign table. [V] Starts at 0 or 2 depending on which campaign was chosen, is incremented by Campaign_EnterConquest only on a win, and is compared against 8 in three places to decide whether the campaign is over.

globals.name: g_optAdvancedFarming
globals.comment: Advanced Farming (L2.eng group 102 index 0). When 0, weather is forced to Cloudy in every county and fertility is forced to 0.

globals.name: g_optArmiesEat
globals.comment: Armies Eat (L2.eng group 102 index 3). When 1, garrison and enemy troop counts are added to the county's food requirement.

globals.name: g_optExploration
globals.comment: Advanced options: exploration. Group 50 index 3, Yes/No.

globals.name: g_aiLordCount
globals.comment: How many AI lords are in the game: (Nobles + 2) - humanPlayers, from Setup_RecountAiLords, or the campaign table's +0x1C column. Realms_AssignLords hands out at most this many lords and writes strength = 0 into every realm past it, so it is what decides how many realms exist. One of only seven globals in the 0x0053F2xx block that Save_Write stores.

globals.name: g_optTimeLimit
globals.comment: Turn time limit in seconds, 0 for none.

globals.name: g_startWeapons
globals.comment: Row of g_startArmoury the game starts on, 0..3 - the committed Weapons option. Campaign maps take it from the table's +0x14 column, which is 1 on every row of both tracks. Not saved.

globals.name: g_startArmySize
globals.comment: Row of g_startTroops the starting garrison is raised from, 0..3 - the committed Army Size option; 0 raises no army at all, which is the test Game_SetupRealmsAndCounties makes. Campaign maps take it from +0x18, which is 0 on every row of both tracks, so a campaign never starts you with an army. Not saved.

globals.name: g_startingGoldChosen
globals.comment: The starting treasury in crowns - g_startingGold[Crowns] from Setup_CommitOptions, or the campaign table's +0x08 column, which is where docs/kingdom.md 8.5's 5000 / 2500 / 1000 comes from. Written into every realm's gold. Not saved.

globals.name: g_startCountyStatus
globals.comment: Row of g_countyStatus every county starts on, 0..2 - the committed County Status option, weak / medium / strong. Campaign maps take it from +0x10. Not saved.

globals.name: g_startCastle
globals.comment: The castle type every start county is given, 0..5 - none, wooden, bailey, keep, stone, royal - the committed Starting Castle option, or the campaign table's +0x0C column, which runs 1, 1, 2, 3, 4, 4, 5, 5 up track A. An earlier reading of that column as the opponent count was wrong: the opponent count is +0x1C. Not saved.

globals.name: g_optFightHumansOnly
globals.comment: Advanced options: "Fight humans only?", group 50 index 4 - stored inverted, so 0 displays Yes. When it is 0 and the local player is not a participant the battle is auto-resolved to screen 0x13 instead of prompting on 0x12.

globals.name: g_setupOptNobles
globals.comment: Custom game drop-down 2, Nobles: 0..3 for two, three, four and five lords. Written by Setup_SetOption and by Setup_NoblesFromMap; read by Setup_RecountAiLords. Not saved.

globals.name: g_setupOptTimeLimit
globals.comment: Custom game drop-down 10, Time limit: an index 0..6 into g_timeLimitSeconds, not a duration. Default 6 (no limit) single-player, 3 (4 mins) networked. Not saved.

globals.name: g_setupOptDifficulty
globals.comment: Custom game drop-down 4, Difficulty: 0..3, easy to impossible. Copied straight into g_optDifficulty by Setup_CommitOptions. Not saved - g_optDifficulty is.

globals.name: g_setupOptWeapons
globals.comment: Custom game drop-down 7, Weapons: 0..3, none / few / some / many. Becomes g_startWeapons. Not saved.

globals.name: g_setupOptArmySize
globals.comment: Custom game drop-down 5, Army Size: 0..3, no army / small / medium / large. Becomes g_startArmySize. Not saved.

globals.name: g_setupOptAdvancedFarming
globals.comment: Custom game drop-down 0, Advanced Farming: 0 off, 1 on. Copied into g_optAdvancedFarming. Not saved.

globals.name: g_setupOptArmiesEat
globals.comment: Custom game drop-down 3, Armies Eat: 0 no, 1 yes. Copied into g_optArmiesEat. Not saved.

globals.name: g_setupOptExploration
globals.comment: Custom game drop-down 1, Exploration: 0 off, 1 on. Copied into g_optExploration. Not saved.

globals.name: g_setupOptCrowns
globals.comment: Custom game drop-down 8, Crowns: an index 0..4 into g_startingGold, whose five values 100 / 500 / 1000 / 2500 / 5000 are the five strings themselves. Not saved.

globals.name: g_setupOptCountyStatus
globals.comment: Custom game drop-down 9, County Status: 0..2, weak / medium / strong. Becomes g_startCountyStatus. Not saved.

globals.name: g_setupOptCastle
globals.comment: Custom game drop-down 6, Starting Castle: 0..5, none / wooden / bailey / keep / stone / royal. Becomes g_startCastle. Not saved.

globals.name: g_setupOptFight
globals.comment: Custom game drop-down 11, Fight?: 0 humans, 1 all. Copied into g_optFightHumansOnly, which is why that flag displays inverted. Default is 1 in a single-player game and 0 in a network game. Not saved - and neither is g_optFightHumansOnly.

globals.name: g_diploLetterDraft
globals.comment: Four 200-byte free-text letter buffers, one per message kind 1..4, typed by the player on screen 0x1A.

globals.name: g_campaignTrack
globals.comment: Which of the two campaigns is being played, from the hotspot Setup_ChooseCampaign saw. 1 selects the table at 0x004D8F58 and anything else the one at 0x004D8E18. [V]

globals.name: g_battleRallyGroup
globals.comment: 0 or 1, chosen the same way as g_battleApproachLane. Selects which group of three rally waypoints the field handlers use.

globals.name: g_turnPhaseStep
globals.comment: Step counter within the current turn phase; incremented on every FUN_0049a010 call.

globals.name: g_mapRowStep
globals.comment: Screen pixels between lattice rows: 15 near, 3 far - half the tile frame height.

globals.name: g_levyBasket
globals.comment: Per-realm army composition scratch, stride 0x80, eight slots of 0x10 bytes. While raising: slot 0 unequipped peasants, 1..6 the six weapon types in g_weaponCost order, 7 the total, with +0x00 chosen, +0x04 available and +0x08 remaining. The army-split screen reuses the same buffer with +0x00 and +0x04 as the two halves and slot 7 as the mercenary band.

globals.name: g_counties
globals.comment: The county array: 17 records of 0x300 bytes, index 1..16 (0 unused). Base, count and stride all appear together in the multiplayer sync descriptor at 0x004D5B10 and in the save-block table at 0x004DE960.

globals.name: g_county0_anchorX
globals.comment: X of county 0's anchor tile in the county record array (stride 0x300); County_FindFreeRoadTile searches around county*0x300 + this.

globals.name: g_county0_anchorY
globals.comment: Y of county 0's anchor tile, as above.

globals.name: g_county0_castleRuined
globals.comment: County +0x1C2. Non-zero blocks both garrisoning and besieging: Army_BeginSiege refuses silently, and MoveOrder_ConfirmGarrison refuses with message 0xA5 = L2.eng 165, 'You cannot station men in a ruined castle.' The string is what names the field.

globals.name: g_villageGrid
globals.comment: vill_gd8.pl8, preload entry 12: a 45 x 40 grid of 8-pixel cells naming which peasant cluster each part of the village picture belongs to. The pixels start at +0x18 and Village_GridAt indexes them there.

globals.name: g_messageQueueHead
globals.comment: Write index into g_messageQueue, wrapping at 50.

globals.name: g_levyMen
globals.comment: Pct(county population, g_levyPercent): the headcount the slider currently proposes.

globals.name: g_hoverFieldCounty
globals.comment: Move-order target: the foreign county whose sown field the cursor is over - bit 0x20 AND County_TileIsField, so a fallow strip does not count. Raises L2.eng 10/10, 'Destroy field?'. Confirms from the UI side that Unit_CrossField's damage is gated on the county's owner differing.

globals.name: g_battleStrengthA
globals.comment: Autocalc strength of army A: sum of count[t] * g_troopStrengthWeight[t] over troop types 0..6.

globals.name: g_messageCategory
globals.comment: The category byte of the message on screen; selects the window layout in Msg_DrawWindow and the timing rules in Msg_Pump.

globals.name: g_messageVariant
globals.comment: The variant index of the message on screen. Drawn as string variant + 1 and passed straight to Msg_PlayVoice.

globals.name: g_pickedTileFlags
globals.comment: The clicked tile's attribute byte, out of the plane at 0x00522F91. Map_Click reads bit 0x80 as an industry building, bit 0x40 as the town square - the village - and bit 0x20 as screen 0x04; FUN_0041BEFE reads 0x20, 0x10, 0x08, 0x04, 0x40 and 0x80 for the map info panel.

globals.name: g_battleWinnerOwner
globals.comment: The owner byte of the winning army - always assigned as g_units[g_battleLoser].owner, at every one of the eight sites that write it. Battle_SelectOutcomeBanner compares it with g_localPlayer to pick the 'won' or 'lost' pair, which is the fourth independent confirmation that g_battleLoser names the winner.

globals.name: g_battlefield
globals.comment: Battlefield cell array, 6400 records of 8 bytes in an 80x80 grid. Typed as struct BattleCell in docs/records.json - all eight bytes named, and every dereference in the binary is one byte wide (RecordProbe; the only two wider hits are PUSH 0x5440e0, the array's address). Indexed by BYTE OFFSET, (y*80 + x)*8: a step east is +8 and a step south is +0x280. The 80x80x8 shape is confirmed from the game's own side - both callers of the isometric grid renderer pass FUN_004bc020(bank, bank2, g_battlefield, 0x50, 0x50, 8, 0, ...). See docs/battle.md 3.

globals.name: g_aiSortieThreshold
globals.comment: Set to 260 by Rules_InitConstants and read only by the four siege-defender handlers: above this advantage the garrison lays the drawbridge patch and charges out.

globals.name: g_confirmCallback
globals.comment: The function Ui_ConfirmClicked calls once either button is pressed.

globals.name: g_grainMaxSacksPerField
globals.comment: 10. The top of Grain_Sow's descending search; the manual's "up to 5 sacks" is wrong.

globals.name: g_historyWrite
globals.comment: The write cursor into g_countyHistory, wrapping at 400 - distinct from g_historyHead, which is the oldest turn and only starts moving once the ring is full, ending one ahead of this. [V] The England turn-one fixture has g_historyLength 1, g_historyHead 0 and this at 1, with entry 0 holding that turn's numbers and entry 1 empty.

globals.name: g_multiplayer
globals.comment: A network game is in progress. Read by 155 sites across the county, setup, battle and diplomacy screens. Written to 1 in exactly ONE place - FUN_004B7250, immediately after FUN_004B7585 succeeds - and to 0 on every failure and teardown path there and in FUN_004B743B, both of which then call vtable+0x24 on the DirectPlay interface at 0x004E2A2C; FUN_004B8243 fills that pointer from DirectPlayCreate and Lords2.exe imports DPLAYX.dll. Net_SendCommand returns immediately unless it is set, so all 112 network opcodes are dead in single player, and FUN_0043B593 branches on it to choose between calling Battle_Start locally and sending message 0x3C. RENAMED from g_deterministicBattle, which asserted the wrong thing: the flag is about the wire, not about determinism. Its determinism-shaped effects are consequences - when it is set Battle_Start advances g_battleApproachLane and g_battleRallyGroup cyclically instead of at random, Battle_UpdateStrengthAdvantage drops its jitter, and Troops_Load reads the side-neutral TROOPS.ENG - because a networked game may not diverge. Sync_Checksum and Turn_AllRealmsDone read it too.

globals.name: g_peasantIconSelected
globals.comment: 25 bytes, one per icon slot of the dragged cluster: 0 unselected, 1 or 2 for the two selected states.

globals.name: g_aiCommitCounter
globals.comment: Zeroed by Battle_Start. A field melee handler adds 3 when the side's engagement count passes its budget byte and 20 when the AI's missile troops fall below an eighth of its army; every unengaged melee unit counts it down by 1 per think. While it is non-zero every AI melee unit goes into free pursuit and every missile unit closes half the distance, so it is a commitment counter rather than a hold.

globals.name: g_pickedCounty
globals.comment: The county last picked on the minimap; the diplomacy screen reads it for message kinds 5 and 6.

globals.name: g_merchantCount
globals.comment: Number of merchants Merchant_SpawnAll actually placed, 1..6.

globals.name: g_miscCtySheet
globals.comment: Misc_cty.pl8, loaded by Gfx_LoadCountyMode. Frames 54/55/56/57/58/59/66 are the 162-pixel-wide campaign right panel, 86..90 the realm banners, 91..95 the minimap furniture.

globals.name: g_lastBattleUnit
globals.comment: Index of the unit BattleUnit_Alloc just allocated.

globals.name: g_setupPage
globals.comment: Sub-page within the game-setup screen (g_screenId 0x1F), 1..13.

globals.name: g_spriteSheetA
globals.comment: Sprite1a.pl8 / Sprite2a.pl8 - armies on the campaign map.

globals.name: g_turnCount
globals.comment: Turns elapsed; divides the happiness accumulator to give the running average.

globals.name: g_mapViewY
globals.comment: Y of the first drawn lattice row: 9 near, 21 far. That row is top-clipped, so the visible band starts at viewY + rowStep = 24 at both zooms.

globals.name: g_mapViewBottom
globals.comment: (g_mapViewRows + 1) * g_mapRowStep + g_mapViewY: 474 near, 408 far. Agrees with Map_PickTile s own bound and with Clip_Vertical(0x18, 0x1DA) in Map_DrawPathMarker.

globals.name: g_merchantStall
globals.comment: The merchant currently being traded with: 16 goods of 0x10 bytes, +0x00 the price and +0x04 a per-good counter, reloaded from g_goodsPrice by Merchant_ResetStall. The trade panel indexes it by the selected good id at 0x0056D8AC.

globals.name: g_mapScrollDir
globals.comment: Scroll direction 0..7 clockwise from north, 8 for none.

globals.name: g_displayOptWidgetCount
globals.comment: Screen 0x43's widget count, written as 2 by the painter.

globals.name: g_battleHoverEnemy
globals.comment: The battle figure under the pointer when it belongs to someone else AND you hold a selection, 0 otherwise. Battle_UpdateHover writes it; it is the FIRST thing Battle_Frame's battle cursor ladder tests, and a non-zero value draws g_cursorCrossTarget. That is the state L2.eng's battle help calls the cursor turning red over an enemy unit.

globals.name: g_grainLabourDivisorAdv
globals.comment: 5. Labour divisor used when Advanced Farming is on.

globals.name: g_villani2Sheet
globals.comment: villani2.pl8, loaded by Village_Draw. 44 frames: five equal-sized animation blocks (0-6 at 26x29, 7-14 at 39x40, 15-24 at 15x12, 25-32 at 32x42, 33-39 at 19x18) that are exactly the five overlays Village_Animate draws from it, then the three static buildings Village_Draw blits - 0x28 stone, 0x29 wood, 0x2B iron - and a 2x2 stub at 42.

globals.name: g_battleChoiceOwner
globals.comment: Who owns the take-the-field choice on the prompt screen: 0 when the local player is in neither army, 1 when the local player is a participant and decides, 2 when the local player is army B in a human-versus-human battle and the other person decides. Battle_ChooseSettlement sets it; the prompt screen, the outcome screen, the answer timeout and Battle_CheckOutcome all gate on it.

globals.name: g_movingUnit
globals.comment: The unit slot Units_Tick is currently driving; the whole campaign mover reads it rather than taking a parameter.

globals.name: g_messageCompose
globals.comment: The 0x18-byte staging record Msg_Enqueue fills before copying it into g_messageQueue.

globals.name: g_battleTrackSiege
globals.comment: The 0/1 toggle picking battle3 or battle4 for a siege. Stepped before use, so the first siege of a session gets battle4.

globals.name: g_pathBuf
globals.comment: Campaign path buffers, stride 300 = 150 (x, y) byte pairs, one per realm slot. Path_CopyToUnit copies one into a unit record.

globals.name: g_battleMenB
globals.comment: Army B's living men - the twin of g_battleMenA, counted the same way, drawn beside it, and the other of Battle_CheckOutcome's two field-battle end conditions.

globals.name: g_rankLeader
globals.comment: The top-ranked realm: the first entry of g_rankTable that Score_RankRealms did not zero out. [V] With g_rankTrailer, the last such entry, it is the victory condition - leader == trailer means one realm is left standing, since both are realm indices rather than scores. An AI also envies an ally that holds this slot. Both are 0 when nobody is in play, which passes the same test and makes the original crown g_realms[0].

globals.name: g_battleTrackField
globals.comment: The 0/1 toggle picking battle1 or battle2 for a field battle. Stepped before use, so the first battle of a session gets battle2.

globals.name: g_playerNames
globals.comment: Six 0x2C-byte player names. g_saveBlocks entry 2 is {0x00553D50, 264}, which is 6 x 0x2C.

globals.name: g_attackersOnWall
globals.comment: Recounted every frame by Battle_UpdateAllMen: live figures of side 4 standing on a cell of surface 5. Every siege-defender handler branches on it, and at 1, 2, 3, 4 and 6 attackers the defenders progressively abandon the wall for the keep.

globals.name: g_debugSelectedMan
globals.comment: The figure index BattleDebug_Panel prints.

globals.name: g_yearNext
globals.comment: g_year + 1, staged for the next roll.

globals.name: g_campaignLastMap
globals.comment: The scenario the conquest screen names as the country just fought over. [V] Campaign_EnterConquest copies g_scenarioIndex here before Campaign_LoadEntry overwrites it with the next map, so the interstitial can print both.

globals.name: g_messageQueueTail
globals.comment: Read index into g_messageQueue, wrapping at 50. Msg_Pump advances it.

globals.name: g_moveOrderClickGuard
globals.comment: How long a just-opened move order ignores the mouse button. Map_BeginMoveSelection sets it to 40 and Map_HoverUnitTarget decrements it once a frame while positive; the READER is Screen_FrameInput's screen-0x10 arm, 'if (g_mouseLeftPressed && this < 1) { g_screenId = 0; Map_ConfirmMoveOrder(); }'. So it exists to stop the same press that opened move-order mode being taken as the press that confirms the destination - 40 frames of deadness after the mode begins. [V] docs/hypotheses.json called it g_hoverDamper, said it was written twice and read never, and asked for the name to be DROPPED if no reader turned up. The reader turned up and it is not about hover at all: the entry is deleted and this is the promotion. Looked for while chasing a merchant tooltip, which it has nothing to do with.

globals.name: g_year
globals.comment: Displayed year. 1268 on turn 1.

globals.name: g_messageFrom
globals.comment: The `from` field of the message being displayed, taken out of the queue record by Msg_Pump. [V] The ending logic compares it against g_localPlayer: an elimination notice whose sender is me is a loss, and one about somebody else is not. It is also the realm whose player name the message window draws, except for group 225, which draws the local player's.

globals.name: g_diploWidgetCount
globals.comment: How many of g_diploWidgets the current group 72 menu layout uses.

globals.name: g_battleHoverSurface
globals.comment: The surface byte of the battlefield cell under the pointer, copied by Battle_UpdateHover out of g_battlefield[cell].surface. Value 0x0F raises DAT_0053E874. Battle_Frame's cursor ladder compares it against the order kind DAT_00568968 (< 6 for kind 6, < 4 for kind 4) to decide whether the destination under the pointer is legal.

globals.name: g_territoryBlockCount
globals.comment: How many blocks Territory_BuildBlocks ended up with. Written there and, as far as the corpus shows, read nowhere - the secession pass ranks blocks by scanning for a matching owner rather than by this count.

globals.name: g_soundOptWidgetCount
globals.comment: Screen 0x42's widget count, written as 3 by the painter.

globals.name: g_armourySelectedType
globals.comment: 1..6, the rack the player last opened, or 0 for none. Written by Armoury_ClickRack and cleared by Levy_Seed. It picks the levy-basket slot the four screen-0x0D buttons move men in and out of, the arm_cros/mace/swor/pike/bow/mail.pl8 sheet Armoury_LoadScreen reads, and the L2.eng group 8 noun at 0x34 + t*2. [V] Armoury_LoadScreen's fall-through for an unrecognised value is arm_cros.pl8, not nothing.

globals.name: g_aiEngagementCount
globals.comment: Counts, since Battle_Start, how many times a field melee handler has thought while its unit had a live attacker. Compared against the per-battlefield budget byte at 0x00553080 to decide whether the side should commit.

globals.name: g_historyLength
globals.comment: How many turns of g_countyHistory are filled, and how many bars Ui_HistoryGraph draws.

globals.name: g_diploMenuState
globals.comment: Which of the four group 72 menu layouts the diplomacy screen draws: 0 no ally, 1 allied to this realm, 2 allied to another, 3 a message from this realm is already waiting.

globals.name: g_castleEntered
globals.comment: Raised by Cell_TryEnter when a SIDE-4 figure steps onto a cell carrying flag 0x08, a step it refuses for both sides. Battle_CheckOutcome tests it inside the siege arm and ends the battle with army A - the besieger - as the winner, so getting one man to that cell wins a siege outright with the garrison still standing. One writer, one reader. docs/armies.md section 7.3 called it 'the escape-tile flag'; it is neither an escape nor the defender's. See docs/battle.md 14.3a.

globals.name: g_hoverMergeUnit
globals.comment: Move-order target: another unit of the local player standing on the hovered tile - not the mover itself and not a transport (kind 4). Raises L2.eng 10/5, 'Combine armies?', and is the value MoveOrder_ConfirmCombine passes as Unit_OrderMove's fifth argument, landing in unit +0x152.

globals.name: g_jobPanelJob
globals.comment: Which job the job popup is showing, 1..9 - the same index as L2.eng group 74, and one more than the labour slot.

globals.name: g_dairyPerHead
globals.comment: 5. People fed per head of the standing herd, without slaughter.

globals.name: g_tradeCrowns
globals.comment: The crown total of the trade line being composed on the merchant screen - negative when selling. Ale_PreviewGain runs the ale ladder on it, which is how the panel can show the happiness a purchase would buy before it is made.

globals.name: g_aiMenTotal
globals.comment: Surviving men over all figures whose owner is not human, from Battle_CountMenByType.

globals.name: g_battleHoverFriendly
globals.comment: The battle figure under the pointer when it is yours and no selection is being placed. Battle_UpdateHover writes it; a non-zero value draws g_cursorRing.

globals.name: g_siegeApproachScore
globals.comment: Siege progress as the AI measures it, and the most-read global in the siege handlers. Raised by the routine that turns a filled-in moat cell into open ground - once per adjacent cell of surface 3, 4 or 5 - and by 4 when the drawbridge patch is laid. Thresholds used against it are 3, 4, 8, 10, 16 and 400. The name is a reading of what raises it, not a label from the binary.

globals.name: g_battleOutcome
globals.comment: Which of the seven L2.eng group 82 heading/body pairs Screen_BattleOutcome shows.

globals.name: g_diploTarget
globals.comment: The rival realm selected on the diplomacy screen.

globals.name: g_battleStrengthB
globals.comment: Autocalc strength of army B.

globals.name: g_siegeEngineCount
globals.comment: Recounted every frame by Battle_UpdateAllMen: live figures of troop type 7, 8 or 9 - catapult, siege tower, battering ram - on either side. Three siege-attacker handlers refuse to move onto the castle objective while it is zero.

globals.name: g_siegeScreenCounty
globals.comment: The county Army_BeginSiege stashed for its confirmation callback, which passes it back to Siege_Link.

globals.name: g_realmsActive
globals.comment: A realm counter with TWO writers and two meanings: FUN_0049B6D3 sets it to the number of in-play realms and Turn_AllRealmsDone to the number that have not yet finished their turn. The diplomacy code tests it against 3 and reads whichever wrote last. Both readings mean 'the game is nearly over' and the branch refuses either way, but which was intended is not established.

globals.name: g_castleLevel
globals.comment: The castle level 0..4 being fought, written by Siege_LaunchAssault: castleDegraded 1 with a build in progress gives castleBuilding-1, castleDegraded 2 gives county +0x1F9, otherwise castleType-1. Army_PrepareForBattle switches on it for the defender's oil count (1, 2, 3, 4, 6) and Battle_CheckOutcome compares it against 3 to decide whether a failed assault repeats or ends the battle.

globals.name: g_weatherCounty
globals.comment: The county picked this season for the doubled local weather swing.

globals.name: g_mercBandsInPlay
globals.comment: How many of the twelve mercenary bands this map uses, from g_mercBandCountByCounties, clamped to 1..12. England has 14 counties and gets all twelve.

globals.name: g_wallHitsRampart
globals.comment: Damage accumulated against the rampart a figure is standing on (surface 5): +1 per frame per man in BattleMan_StateAttackWall, +20 in BattleMan_StateRamGate. At 5000 the cell becomes surface 4, the counter resets and 0x0055307C is bumped.

globals.name: g_moatFillSteps
globals.comment: Set to 15 by Rules_InitConstants. A figure filling in the moat (state 9) raises the target cell terrain byte by 1 every 81 frames - 101 if its owner is human - and the cell becomes open ground when the byte reaches this value.

globals.name: g_bankTown
globals.comment: Tile bank 0x0C: Town1?.pl8 / Town2?.pl8.

globals.name: g_peasantIcons
globals.comment: Eight clusters of 25 bytes: the sprite frame plus one for each peasant icon on the village screen, or 0 for an empty slot. Rebuilt by Village_RebuildIcons.

globals.name: g_industryRecordFromTile
globals.comment: The industry record index Map_Click derives from a clicked building's graphic before calling Industry_ToggleFromMap: graphic below 4 -> record 1, below 7 -> 3, below 10 -> 2, below 0x0D -> 0, and 0x15 or above -> 4. The first four rungs are the same terrain groups Unit_TrampleTile ruins and County_PlaceResourceSites places, agreeing a third time; the fifth rung, record 4 for the castle graphics, has no counterpart in either and is not explained.

globals.name: g_seasonPrev
globals.comment: The previous value of g_season.

globals.name: g_battleMen
globals.comment: Battle figure array, 81 records of 0x1B0 bytes, index 1..80 (0 unused). A figure is one drawn man representing g_menPerFigure real soldiers. +0x09 selected, +0x12 troop type, +0x13 owner is human, +0x18 facing 0..7, +0x1C cell byte offset, +0x20/+0x22 x,y, +0x24/+0x26 target x,y, +0x2C owner (0 = free slot), +0x31 state, +0x172 armour, +0x174 target figure, +0x178 owning unit, +0x17A side, +0x17E melee opponent, +0x189 move delay, +0x18B melee recovery interval, +0x197 strength band, +0x198 heavy-blow bonus, +0x19A hits, +0x19C melee attack, +0x1A0 men left. Full map in docs/battle.md. Eighty usable slots but eighty-one records of storage: every sweep is for (i = 1; i < 0x51; i++), so index 80 is live, and nothing else in the binary claims the space behind it.

globals.name: g_mapScrollStep
globals.comment: Lattice columns per scroll step: 1 near, 4 far. Rows move by twice this, which keeps the origins parity.

globals.name: g_mapViewRight
globals.comment: g_mapTilePitch * g_mapViewCols + g_mapViewX. 480 at all three zooms, which is what leaves 160 pixels for the right column.

globals.name: g_diploHelpCounty
globals.comment: The county the pay-for-help prompt refers to.

globals.name: g_flagsSheet
globals.comment: Flags1a.pl8 / Flags2a.pl8 - the county flags drawn over castle tiles.

globals.name: g_screenLattice
globals.comment: Runtime 129x65 dword screen lattice, row stride 0x104. Covered cells hold tileIndex*8; uncovered cells keep 0x0FFF0000 + backgroundFrame.

globals.name: g_hoverCountyTownCounty
globals.comment: One of the six move-order targets Map_HoverUnitTarget collects: the county whose county TOWN (plane-0 bit 0x40) the cursor is over, when that county is not the moving unit's. It raises no dialog; MoveOrder_Confirm reads it and refuses with L2.eng 286 when that county's castle holds a garrison. That is the user-facing half of Army_AttackCounty's siege gate.

globals.name: g_presentNow
globals.comment: Set by Gfx_MarkWidgetUrgent and cleared by Gfx_Present, and while set it forces the frame budget full so the next present happens immediately. Widget_Draw is what sets it, so a button that lights up under the cursor does not wait for the 20 Hz tick.

globals.name: g_mapStartCol
globals.comment: First visible lattice column, 0..64. Clamped by Map_ClampScroll.

globals.name: g_mapStartRow
globals.comment: First visible lattice row, 0..128, and always even - every setter uses an even literal, row & ~1, or steps of two.

globals.name: g_diploKind
globals.comment: The message kind picked on the diplomacy screen, 0..6. It is the L2.eng group 72 menu index minus 2: 0 gift, 1 compliment, 2 insult, 3 offer alliance, 4 terminate alliance, 5 ask for help, 6 ask for an attack.

globals.name: g_battleHoverOnField
globals.comment: 1 while the pointer is inside the battlefield viewport, 0 otherwise. Battle_UpdateHover sets it from FUN_004BC222(g_mouseX, g_mouseY) and clears it at the top of every frame; Battle_Frame's cursor ladder and Screen_FrameInput read it.

globals.name: g_levyHappinessCost
globals.comment: g_armyHappinessCost[g_levyPercent] plus county +0x2F4, clamped to 0..100. Subtracted from county happiness and from county +0x15 (shownArmy) when the army is created.

globals.name: g_rankTable
globals.comment: Five {realm, score} pairs, bubble-sorted into descending score order by Score_RankRealms, which then writes each realm its 1..5 rank at +0x2B and zeroes the entry of any realm at zero strength. [V] The sort reads one pair past the end; the two dwords at 0x00565438 are the sentinel it needs and are explicitly zeroed just before the loop.

globals.name: g_messagePending
globals.comment: Set by Msg_Enqueue when something has been queued, cleared by Msg_Reset.

globals.name: g_battleUnits
globals.comment: Battle unit array, 81 records of 0x34 bytes, index 1..80 (0 unused). A unit is what the player selects and orders. +0x00 owner (0 = free slot), +0x01 human controlled, +0x02 figure count, +0x03 side (0 or 4), +0x04/+0x06 first and last figure index, +0x08 category, +0x0F firing timer, +0x14 re-target countdown, +0x1A orders, +0x1E/+0x20 position, +0x22/+0x24 target, +0x2C ordered target figure, +0x30 target cell offset. Eighty usable slots but eighty-one records of storage: every sweep is for (i = 1; i < 0x51; i++), so index 80 is live, and nothing else in the binary claims the space behind it.

globals.name: g_foodPerHead
globals.comment: 10. People fed by one slaughtered animal.

globals.name: g_mapTileHalfStep
globals.comment: The same half pitch again, used as the x step for the half-offset lattice rows and as the divisor in Map_PickTile.

globals.name: g_tileCursor
globals.comment: Byte offset into g_tiles of the tile the render walk is on, i.e. the lattice cell value. Values below 0x0FFF0000 are on-map.

globals.name: g_diploHelpPrice
globals.comment: The gold an ally is demanding for help or an attack: personality +0x0C times the pair record's helpPriceMultiple, so it rises with every purchase.

globals.name: g_formationOriginY
globals.comment: Y of the top-left corner of the formation rectangle, and the output of Formation_FindNearbySlot.

globals.name: g_merchantRoutes
globals.comment: The six merchant trade routes: 6 rows x 16 county ids, built from plane 4 on castle tiles. Row n is the itinerary of the merchant named by L2.eng group 5 string n. See docs/formats/plane4.md.

globals.name: g_diploLetter
globals.comment: One 0xCA-byte outgoing letter per realm. Diplo_SendClicked copies the draft here and Msg_DrawWindow draws it for the recipient; it is saved and loaded with the game.

globals.name: g_pickedCountyOwner
globals.comment: That county's owner (+0x05), compared against g_localPlayer by every branch of Map_Click.

globals.name: g_pickedTileCounty
globals.comment: The county the clicked tile belongs to, from the county plane at 0x00522F97. 0x20 is read back as 0, so a tile in no county picks nothing.

globals.name: g_bankBase
globals.comment: Tile bank 0x00: Base1?.pl8 near, Base2?.pl8 far. Also the sheet the off-map surround is drawn from.

globals.name: g_battleArmyA
globals.comment: Index into g_units of the first army in the current battle. It is raised on side 4.

globals.name: g_battleArmyB
globals.comment: Index into g_units of the second army. It is raised on side 0, and is the side the castle-defender path is applied to in a siege.

globals.name: g_mapTilePitch
globals.comment: Screen pixels between lattice columns: 60 near, 12 far - the tile frame width plus two.

globals.name: g_formationFootprint
globals.comment: Cell footprint of the troop type Formation_PickGeometry chose for the current unit.

globals.name: g_battleCounty
globals.comment: The county a battle is being fought over. Written by Army_AttackCounty (the county attacked), by the army-versus-army path (the defender's county byte) and by Siege_LaunchAssault (the besieged county); read by Battle_ReturnToCampaign to decide which county changes hands, and by both battle screens for its name.

globals.name: g_territoryBlocks
globals.comment: The contiguity scratch table Territory_BuildBlocks fills every season: 17 records of 0x1C, +0x00 the block's total population, +0x04 its owning realm (0 marks the end of the list), +0x05 up to 20 member county ids. Not saved - it is rebuilt from scratch each turn.

globals.name: g_curBattleUnit
globals.comment: Index of the unit currently being updated by Battle_UpdateAllUnits.

globals.name: g_messageQueue
globals.comment: The message ring: 50 records of 0x18 bytes. +0x00 to, +0x04 from, +0x08 L2.eng group, +0x0C variant, +0x11 category (window layout), +0x12 county, +0x14 payload. Head g_messageQueueHead, tail g_messageQueueTail, both wrapping at 50.

globals.name: g_hoverTileOffset
globals.comment: Byte offset into g_tiles of the tile under the cursor - (y*64 + x) * 8. Map_HoverUnitTarget short-circuits when it is 0x0FFF0000 or more (no tile) and recomputes only when it changed since the last frame.

globals.name: g_bankCastle
globals.comment: Tile bank 0x10: Castle1?.pl8 / Castle2?.pl8. Never referenced by the stored map data, only by tiles the loader rewrites.

globals.name: g_lastMissile
globals.comment: Index of the missile Missile_Spawn just allocated.

globals.name: g_hoverGarrisonCounty
globals.comment: Move-order target: the county whose castle (bit 0x80, terrain above 0x14) the cursor is over when that county IS the moving unit's. Raises L2.eng 10/7, 'Garrison castle?'.

globals.name: g_wallHitsGate
globals.comment: The same accumulator for a figure attacking a cell that is not a rampart. At 20000 it breaches once and for all, raising g_siegeApproachScore and g_siegeBreachScore by 4 each. It is never reset, so a siege has exactly one of these breaches.

globals.name: g_historyHead
globals.comment: Write cursor into g_countyHistory, wrapping at 400.

globals.name: g_playerStartTable
globals.comment: Player start table, {county, slot} byte pairs indexed by the plane-4 value on a settlement tile. See docs/formats/maps-layers.md 5.1.

globals.name: g_mercBands
globals.comment: Twelve mercenary bands, stride 0x14, index 1..12 = the L2.eng group 16 nationality. +0x00 hiring unit (0 = free), +0x02 start county, +0x03 the county it is currently offered in, +0x04 the next county in its walk, +0x05 troop type, +0x06 countdown, +0x07 reload, +0x08 men, +0x0C price, +0x10 an unread wage figure.

globals.name: g_siegeScreenUnit
globals.comment: The besieging army the siege-preparation screen (0x1D) is showing. Written by Siege_Link for a human owner and by Map_Click when clicking an army that is already besieging; the screen's 'Lift siege' button passes it to Siege_Break.

globals.name: g_paletteBase01
globals.comment: Base01.256, preload entry 0. Screen_DrawCampaign installs it, so this is the campaign screens palette.

globals.name: g_merchantStartCounty
globals.comment: Six bytes: the county each merchant starts in, chosen by Merchant_PickStartCounties. A zero entry stops Merchant_SpawnAll.

globals.name: g_syncDigest
globals.comment: Six 10-byte multiplayer state digests, one per realm, stride 10. Byte 0 total, 1 counties, 2 realms, 3 units, 4 unused, 5 battle men, 6 missiles, 7 battle units (forced to 1), 8 unused, 9 frame tag. [V] Written by Sync_BuildDigest, exchanged whole by Net_WriteField/Net_ReadField, compared by Sync_BlockAgrees; L2.eng group 14 indices 2..9 name bytes 1..8.

globals.name: g_foundTileX
globals.comment: X of the tile the last Map_FindFree*TileNear search settled on.

globals.name: g_foundTileY
globals.comment: Y of the tile the last Map_FindFree*TileNear search settled on.

globals.name: g_turnPhase
globals.comment: Turn state machine phase, switched on by FUN_0049a010. Phase 6 step 1 is Merchant_AdvanceAll.

globals.name: g_minimapPixels
globals.comment: The 128x128 minimap picture for the loaded slot, read straight out of MAPnn.PL8 by Minimap_Load. 0x4000 bytes, and 0x569590 + 0x4000 = 0x56D590, just below the render walks cursors.

globals.name: g_latticeRow
globals.comment: Lattice row cursor inside the render walk.

globals.name: g_latticeCol
globals.comment: Lattice column cursor inside the render walk.

globals.name: g_moveTargetY
globals.comment: Y of the tile a move order is aimed at. See g_moveTargetX.

globals.name: g_moveTargetX
globals.comment: X of the tile a move order is aimed at. Written by Map_HoverUnitTarget from the hovered tile and by Map_SelectUnitForMove from the unit's own tile; read as Unit_OrderMove's third argument and serialised into network command 0x29.

globals.name: g_curMissile
globals.comment: Index of the missile Missile_Step is advancing.

globals.name: g_battleWithdrawal
globals.comment: Set to 1 in exactly one place, UnitOrder_SiegeAttKnight, when an all-knight AI besieger faces an unbreached wall and gives up; DAT_005656F8 records whose army withdrew. Battle_CheckOutcome tests it BEFORE either men counter, so a withdrawal outranks annihilation, and Battle_ReturnToCampaign reads it for the 'a loser with 50 or more men only has its siege lifted' branch. Cleared by Battle_InitArmies, by FUN_00477C89 and - decisively - by Battle_AutoResolve's first statement, which is why that branch is a SIEGE-WITHDRAWAL rule and not an autocalc one, correcting docs/armies.md section 7.

globals.name: g_scanBattleMan
globals.comment: Loop cursor of the figure-scanning target selectors - Missile_FindTarget and its two weighted variants, and Melee_ChooseChaseTarget - left holding the chosen figure on success.

globals.name: g_opponentsRemaining
globals.comment: How many realms are in play that are not the local player, recounted at the top of Score_RankRealms. [V] Msg_DrawWindow reads it to decide the ordinary human victory: when an ending message is displayed and this is zero, it enqueues L2.eng group 225 "Victory!" at the local player. That, and not the leader/trailer test in Score_RankRealms, is how killing the last AI wins a game.

globals.name: g_countyCount
globals.comment: Highest county id on the loaded map, i.e. the county count. Set by Map_LoadPlanes as max(plane5) over ids below 0x11.

globals.name: g_levyPercent
globals.comment: The raise-army slider, 0..100 - the percentage of the county population being levied, and what indexes g_armyHappinessCost.

globals.name: g_overviewH
globals.comment: Height of the overview panel: 160.

globals.name: g_mapViewRows
globals.comment: Lattice rows visible: 30 near, 128 far. Map_RenderIso draws this many plus one, the first and last half-height.

globals.name: g_overviewW
globals.comment: Width of the overview panel: 160.

globals.name: g_overviewX
globals.comment: Left edge of the right-hand overview panel: 480.

globals.name: g_overviewY
globals.comment: Top of the overview panel: 48. Screen_HitRegion raises it to 24 in campaign mode.

globals.name: g_aiMenMissile
globals.comment: Surviving crossbowmen plus archers on the non-human side. When this falls below an eighth of g_aiMenTotal the field melee handlers add 20 to g_aiCommitCounter.

globals.name: g_battleApproachLane
globals.comment: 0..3, chosen at random by Battle_Start in normal play and advanced cyclically in deterministic play. Selects which of four columns of the castle approach tables the siege attackers use, and which end-of-field slot the field handlers march to.

globals.name: g_menuPrevScreen
globals.comment: The screen an open menu-bar drop-down will return to. Menu_OpenDropdown saves g_screenId here before switching to 0x32, and the help topics and the refused option toggles restore it.

globals.name: g_castleSelection
globals.comment: The castle chooser's selected level, 0..4. Seeded from castleType - 1 by Castle_OpenScreen, written by CastleBuild_Select, read by Screen_CastleBuild (the picture), Screen_CastleBuildPanel (every number on the panel) and CastleBuild_Confirm (the two guards and the argument to Castle_Order).

globals.name: g_aiRallyRequest
globals.comment: Raised by a field melee handler that is under attack, together with g_aiRallyX / g_aiRallyY; the field missile handler consumes it and shifts two cells toward that point. The only unit-to-unit signal in the battle AI.

globals.name: g_advancedOptWidgetCount
globals.comment: Screen 0x39's widget count: written as 4 by the painter, read by the widget pass.

globals.name: g_formationCols
globals.comment: Figures per row of the current unit's formation rectangle, capped at the figure count and forced to 2 for units whose byte +0x09 is 1.

globals.name: g_spriteSheetB
globals.comment: Sprite1b.pl8 / Sprite2b.pl8 - the second army sheet, selected by a unit type byte of 4.

globals.name: g_countyHistory
globals.comment: 400 turns x 16 counties x 8 bytes: population as u32 at +0x00 and happiness as u8 at +0x04, indexed by county - 1. What both graph panels draw. g_saveBlocks block 10 is exactly {0x0056D8C0, 51200}, and the shipped lastturn.sav reads back all fourteen counties' stored population and happiness at turn 0.

globals.name: g_minimapMode
globals.comment: Minimap overlay: 0 owner colours, 1..3 three per-county ratings of the local players own counties.

globals.name: g_diploGold
globals.comment: The gold amount typed on the gift page; forced to 0 for every kind other than 0.

globals.name: g_missiles
globals.comment: Missile / effect array, 100 records of 0x4C bytes, index 1..100. +0x06 firing figure, +0x08 owner, +0x09 class (1 bow, 2 crossbow, 3 catapult, 5 fire, 7 falling figure), +0x0A/+0x0C position in 1/32 cell, +0x14/+0x16 cell x,y, +0x1C cell byte offset, +0x2F launch elevation, +0x36 distance flown, +0x38 range, +0x40 power.

globals.name: g_realms
globals.comment: Realm/player array: 6 records of 0x160 bytes, index 1..5. +0x00 AI step, +0x04 in play, +0x05 human, +0x07 lord, +0x28 empire tax happiness, +0x2B rank, +0x50 score, +0xFC army wages, +0x118 gold.

globals.name: g_aiAggressionThreshold
globals.comment: Set to 5 by Rules_InitConstants and read only by the three field order handlers: above this advantage they attack, at or below it they hold and skirmish.

globals.name: g_selectedUnit
globals.comment: The unit a move order is being given to. Map_SelectUnitForMove reads g_units[this].x/.y; Map_HoverUnitTarget tests this unit's moveAllowance minus movesUsed against the path cost; every MoveOrder_Confirm* passes it to Unit_OrderMove. Distinct from g_pickedTileUnit, which is what the click landed on.

globals.name: g_hoverSiegeCounty
globals.comment: Move-order target: the same castle tile as g_hoverGarrisonCounty but when the county is NOT the moving unit's. Raises L2.eng 10/8, 'Besiege castle?'. The two are the arms of one owner test, which is the same split Unit_ReachCastleBuilding makes when an army actually arrives - one function for the intention, one for the act.

globals.name: g_localPlayer
globals.comment: The player index this machine controls. Compared against a unit owner to decide whose units are on the player side.

globals.name: g_battleUnitCount
globals.comment: Number of occupied unit slots, recounted at the end of every BattleUnits_RebuildFromFigures pass.

globals.name: g_grainYieldPerSack
globals.comment: 12. "Each sack planted will grow into 12 sacks" - the game's own FAQ text, L2.eng group 292 index 4.

globals.name: g_battlePhase
globals.comment: Set to 2 by Battle_Start. BattleUnits_RebuildFromFigures does nothing unless it holds 2.

globals.name: g_villageTopY
globals.comment: Where the village scene starts: 64 normally, 132 with Advanced Farming, which is the strip the fertility and weather lines occupy.

globals.name: g_screenIdSaved
globals.comment: g_screenId stashed while a Ui_OpenConfirm box is up. Every yes-callback restores it as its first statement, which is the shape that identifies a callback in the corpus - that is how the campaign map's six move-order callbacks were found.

globals.name: g_battleLoser
globals.comment: CORRECTED - despite the name this holds the index of the WINNING army, and the name is kept only because it is the one the project has used everywhere. Four independent sites agree against it: Battle_AutoResolve assigns it the side whose troop counts it then keeps, zeroing the other's; Battle_ReturnToCampaign's g_battleLoser == g_battleArmyA branch hands the county to A and destroys B; Battle_CheckOutcome sets it to the side whose men are still above zero; and Battle_SelectOutcomeBanner maps g_localPlayer == g_units[g_battleLoser].owner onto L2.eng group 82's 'won' pair. Implemented on the name you destroy the winner and hand the county to the corpse.

globals.name: g_seasonNext
globals.comment: The season after g_season; the year rolls when the season that just ended was 4.

globals.name: g_season
globals.comment: Current season 1..4, used directly as the index into L2.eng group 29 (Spring, Summer, Autumn, Winter). Season_Advance sets it before running the economy, so the economy sees the season being entered.

globals.name: g_selectedCounty
globals.comment: The county the county panels display.

globals.name: g_messageTimer
globals.comment: Countdown while a message window is up; Msg_Pump sets it to 2000.

globals.name: g_formationOriginX
globals.comment: X of the top-left corner of the formation rectangle, and the output of Formation_FindNearbySlot.

globals.name: g_mapHalfPitch
globals.comment: Half the tile pitch: 30 near, 6 far.

globals.name: g_aiMenKnight
globals.comment: Surviving knights on the non-human side. Two siege-attacker handlers compare it against g_aiMenTotal.

globals.name: g_villageDragCount
globals.comment: How many peasant icons the rubber-band box selected. Multiplied by county +0xB8 to get workers.

globals.name: g_battleHoverFriendlyPicked
globals.comment: The same as g_battleHoverFriendly but for the case where DAT_00553078 says a selection already exists: Battle_UpdateHover routes one of your own figures here instead. Also draws g_cursorRing.

globals.name: g_siegeCursor
globals.comment: Turn phase 2's resumable position in the unit array. Siege_StartPhase seeds it with 1; Siege_TickPhase advances it to 150 and stops on the first army whose engines are ready, so the phase can leave the turn machine to run the assault and come back where it left off.

globals.name: g_confirmPrompt
globals.comment: Which L2.eng group 10 string the confirmation box asks.

globals.name: g_mapZoom
globals.comment: Campaign map zoom: 0 near (58x30 tiles) or 2 far (10x6). Written only by Map_SetZoom and Map_InitMode, and no caller ever passes 1, so the middle zoom is unreachable.

globals.name: g_hoverVillageCounty
globals.comment: Move-order target: the foreign county whose dwelling plot (plane-0 bit 0x10) the cursor is over. Raises L2.eng 10/4, 'Slaughter villagers?', which is the game naming Unit_BurnDwelling's effect for us.

globals.name: g_pickedTileGraphic
globals.comment: g_tiles[picked tile] - the clicked tile's graphic index, which is how Map_Click tells a mine from a quarry from a smithy from a forest from a castle without a second plane.

globals.name: g_foodPerSack
globals.comment: 6. People fed by one sack of grain.

globals.name: g_foundWallY
globals.comment: Y of the cell Siege_FindCellSurface4 last returned.

globals.name: g_foundWallX
globals.comment: X of the cell Siege_FindCellSurface4 last returned.

globals.name: g_redrawRequest
globals.comment: The interface's only redraw request. Every handler writes 2; the main loop is "if (g_redrawRequest != 0) { Screen_Draw(g_redrawRequest); g_redrawRequest = 0; }", so the value becomes Screen_Draw's firstFrame argument and 1 means a full repaint.

globals.name: g_bankRoads
globals.comment: Tile bank 0x08: Roads1?.pl8 / Roads2?.pl8 - roads, woodland, fields and the county boundary frames.

globals.name: g_grainLabourDivisor
globals.comment: 2. Labour divisor used when Advanced Farming is off.

globals.name: g_moveOrderAvailable
globals.comment: Set by Map_HoverUnitTarget when the hovered tile yielded a path, cleared when the distance field says the tile is the unit's own or unreachable. Map_ConfirmMoveOrder does nothing at all unless this is 1, so it is the gate between hovering and ordering.

globals.name: g_pulse160
globals.comment: The 160 ms animation pulse - every second g_pulse80 - set by Tick_Pulses and true for one frame. Read by Village_Animate (six of its eight counters) and FUN_004071A0. The village's slow animations run at 6.25 Hz because of this.

globals.name: g_panelsSheet
globals.comment: Panels.pl8, entry 10 of the startup preload table. 262 frames: two 52-frame 16x16 border sets at 0 and 204, a 144-frame 12x12 interior texture at 52, and eight 24x24 strip frames at 196.

globals.name: g_rand7B
globals.comment: randStateB & 0x7F, so 0..127. The die the alliance and help/attack decisions roll.

globals.name: g_sliderStep
globals.comment: How much one arrow press moves g_sliderValue.

globals.name: g_rand7A
globals.comment: g_randStateA & 0x7F after Rand_Advance. Battle_UpdateStrengthAdvantage takes (value & 0x1F) - 10 from it, so the AI's read of its own strength wanders by -10..+21.

globals.name: g_numberBuffer
globals.comment: 100-byte scratch that Ui_NumberToBuffer formats into and Ui_DrawNumber draws from.

globals.name: g_spriteDataOffset
globals.comment: Current source data offset within the PL8 buffer.

globals.name: g_randStateB
globals.comment: Second 31-bit LFSR state of Rand_Advance.

globals.name: g_sliderPrompt
globals.comment: Which L2.eng group 12 string the slider dialog is adjusting.

globals.name: g_sliderX
globals.comment: Slider dialog origin x.

globals.name: g_sliderY
globals.comment: Slider dialog origin y.

globals.name: g_randStateA
globals.comment: First 31-bit LFSR state of Rand_Advance.

globals.name: g_embossGrey
globals.comment: When non-zero, Ui_DrawText embosses with 0x3F above and 0x26 below instead of the screen-id pair 0x10/0x1F - black over a light grey rather than a dark olive over parchment yellow. Set by exactly three functions and cleared immediately after each: CountyStrip_Draw around the three Sovereign land of ... lines, Screen_Armoury, and FUN_004180F6. It is the reason the county name and the banner beneath it are embossed differently on the same plate; docs/bugs.md B64.

globals.name: g_absDy
globals.comment: Absolute y distance left by Dist_Manhattan / Dist_Chebyshev.

globals.name: g_mouseSheet
globals.comment: mouse.pl8 - the pointer.

globals.name: g_clipSrcSkip
globals.comment: Source bytes skipped per row = width - visible width.

globals.name: g_pulse80
globals.comment: The 80 ms animation pulse, set by Tick_Pulses and true for one frame. Read by Village_Animate (two of its eight counters), FUN_004071A0, FUN_00413526, FUN_004190DB, FUN_00451F1A and FUN_004BD574.

globals.name: g_clipVisibleWidth
globals.comment: Visible (clipped) sprite width.

globals.name: g_confirmAnswer
globals.comment: 1 for yes (the thumb-up hand), 0 for no. Written before g_confirmCallback runs, and read by it.

globals.name: g_drawX
globals.comment: Destination x for the next blit. The map render walk advances it by g_mapTilePitch per tile.

globals.name: g_drawY
globals.comment: Destination y for the next blit. The map render walk advances it by g_mapRowStep per lattice row.

globals.name: g_uiHotspotId
globals.comment: Id of the widget the pointer last acted on. For the minimap buttons 1..3 pick an overlay mode and 4 toggles the map zoom.

globals.name: g_uiHotspotArg
globals.comment: Widget record +0x14, published for the callback alongside g_uiHotspotId.

globals.name: g_absDx
globals.comment: Absolute x distance left by Dist_Manhattan / Dist_Chebyshev.

globals.name: g_engText
globals.comment: l2.eng, whole. Eng_GroupBase indexes the group table from here.

globals.name: g_spriteHeight
globals.comment: Current sprite height.

globals.name: g_sliderFormat
globals.comment: How the value is printed: 1 divides by ten, 2 prints it plainly, anything else appends a per cent sign.

globals.name: g_dropShadow
globals.comment: When non-zero, Ui_DrawText draws a DROP SHADOW rather than an emboss: one pass at (x+1, y+1) in colour 0x3F, then the glyph at (x, y). Set by the county strip's seven produce-row painters and by CountyStrip_DrawCastleIcon. g_flatText (DAT_005AEA40) is tested first and wins.

globals.name: g_font10
globals.comment: Font_10.pl8.

globals.name: g_fontBody
globals.comment: Fntl2_14.pl8 - every panel body line.

globals.name: g_fontHeading
globals.comment: Fntl2_22.pl8 - every panel heading.

globals.name: g_blitRowCount
globals.comment: Blitter row counter. Not frame-record byte 0x0D - Clip_Vertical overwrites it before every blit, so the byte-0x0D load in Pl8_DrawFrame is dead.

globals.name: g_systemSheet
globals.comment: System2.pl8 or System.pl8, entry 9 of the preload table; swapped by name from the pair of strings at 0x004DBBD0.

globals.name: g_spriteWidth
globals.comment: Current sprite width.

globals.name: g_sliderMax
globals.comment: Upper bound; the up arrow does nothing at or above it.

globals.name: g_engCursor
globals.comment: Where Eng_Seek leaves its pointer; the caller reads or copies the string from here.

globals.name: g_sliderPrevScreen
globals.comment: The screen the slider dialog returns to.

globals.name: g_sliderMin
globals.comment: Lower bound; the down arrow does nothing at or below it.

globals.name: g_fontSmall
globals.comment: Fntl2_9.pl8 - the county strip, and nothing else.

globals.name: g_font8
globals.comment: Fnt_8.pl8 - the battle overlay.

globals.name: g_clipDstAdvance
globals.comment: Destination advance per row = screen stride - visible width.

globals.name: g_penAdvance
globals.comment: Width of the text drawn since the last reset, in pixels. Every panel zeroes it, draws a label, and adds it to the x of the value - which is how a label and its value are laid out without either knowing the other's width.

globals.name: g_sliderValue
globals.comment: Pointer to the int the slider dialog is editing.

globals.name: g_clipState
globals.comment: Clip state: 0 unclipped, 1 clipped left, 2 clipped right, 5 fully offscreen.
